review_title: I Can No Longer Trust Amazon After This…
review_text: I Can No Longer Trust Amazon After This Experience As part of an earlier issue, I had filed an A-to-Z claim regarding a problematic order experience. During the resolution process, an Amazon Customer Service representative offered what was described as a one-time reimbursement exception for a future shipped-by-Amazon order under a specified amount. I received this promise in writing and carefully followed every instruction provided: •   purchased only shipped-by-Amazon items •   kept the total within the required limit •   waited until the order was fully delivered •   contacted Amazon again exactly as instructed However, when I followed up after delivery, another supervisor informed me that the previous representative had provided “false information” and that Amazon would not honor the written promise made to me. For me, the issue is not simply financial. Trust is one of the most important values in any relationship between a company and its customers. When a company gives written assurances and later refuses to stand behind them, customer trust is broken. I remained calm and respectful throughout the entire process, but after this experience I personally no longer feel comfortable doing business with a company that does not honor its own written commitments. Because of this, I have decided to close my Amazon account and move my future purchases to businesses that value transparency, accountability, and fair treatment of their customers.

review_text: Steel Toe Cap Trainers Work Safety Trainers Brand :BAGHUY A soul once laboured beneath the weight of endless toil, the purse reduced to withered husk, graced only by meagre offerings drawn from the land. Sickness came as ravenous beast, consuming what little coin could be scraped together, leaving the spirit battered and the pockets bare. the lovely shades of periwinkle and rose whispered of expenses scarcely afforded, pressing down upon what little remained. In search of shoes, this soul wandered through the "Source Of Hope". The green boots came first, yet my boy stumbled and fell in them far too often. Then came the temptation of fashionable white ones, so stylish and so desired, but the very stones seemed to cling to them, a constant annoyance with every hurried stride. Now, these boots: steel-toed and broad, a promised sanctuary. Yet, even as held, a protest arose. His toes were cramped, confined, pinched. Hark, crimson doth approach! They vowed protection, a shield from harm. But could this pledged safety keep him whole? The makers spoke of guarding against the sharp teeth of hard labour, of warding off every painful prick. Their word was taken, trusting they would spare Nick this trial. Light as a whisper, they claimed, feather-light and weightless. In this, at least, a truth. He found them light, delightfully light. Their soles gripped treacherous paths, clinging to anything that might send him sprawling. Young Nick had held his footing thus far. Yet still, a bitter truth gnawed away: that choosing the cheaper path, driven by desperation, often leads to far greater ruin than a modest, initial investment. It was painfully clear, and in that clarity burned a fire within those who simply tried to survive, to make their way, one struggling page at a time.

review_title: ZXHQ 2026 Diary A5 Page a Day
review_text: ZXHQ 2026 Diary A5 Page a Day, Jan-Dec. Regrettably, I find myself with a life fuller than I'd ever imagined—though not in the way we dream about. My calendar tells a story I never wanted to write, filled with medical appointments and clinical trials for cancer treatments that consume my days. You see, a diary demands what I can no longer easily give. It requires two hands when one is often occupied by my phone, and even a simple spiral-bound book has become a challenge I'd rather avoid. Stomach cancer brings its own unwelcome schedule of frequent bathroom visits, and inevitably, someone will call right when I'm least prepared to answer. My germaphobic son certainly won't be offering assistance, in the bathroom! I crave whatever privacy remains as my health continues its unfortunate decline. As much as I love the idea of a proper diary—that nostalgic companion of generations past—the simple act of turning pages and writing has become surprisingly difficult with hands that no longer cooperate as they once did. What I actually need is modest: just the date, time, location, and a few brief notes. My medical team knows what they're doing; detailed records aren't necessary when professionals are guiding my care. A wall calendar serves my purpose far better than an elaborate diary with all those extras—day-per-page layouts, religious information, expense trackers, habit monitors, inspirational quotes, maps, and time zones. They're lovely touches, truly, but excessive for what I require. Yes, a portable diary would be wonderful in the hospital where medical staff could add their own notes, but the thought of losing it and needing a duplicate troubles me deeply. So I hope to gift this beautiful diary to someone who will treasure it as it deserves. Word travels quickly about such wonderful presents, especially when they arrive with a matching pen—sea green with sea green, purple with purple. A spiral-bound option would have been ideal, but what I really covet is a dictaphone. For now, I lumber back from my throne to the coffee table whenever the phone rings, the zimmer frame clanking loudly, hoping it's not another nuisance caller. Anyone who's survived this particular journey uses far different describing words for that awkward shuffle than I can print here.

review_text: MERACH Under Desk Elliptical Machine for Home, Electric Elliptical Machine for Seniors This body tells many a tale. One of my knees deserves retirement, some fingers already claimed theirs. The other knee works double time, but we manage. I was never one for the gym. Expense. Travelling. The thought of all those eyes watching, the pressure of it all—no, that wasn't for me. So I found my comfort at home, in slippers, with the telly on. Years later, I discovered this little elliptical machine—low-impact, gentle on weary joints. It's perfect for someone like me, someone in leg rehabilitation. I think our forefathers dreamed of something like this: a contraption that moves your body while you sit there with a smile, watching the world go by. The motor's quiet too, though the television certainly isn't. There are no excuses left, really. The pedals don't slip, the straps keep your feet secure, and those anti-slip pads mean safety's guaranteed. My son Nick—he's a carer, autistic himself, caring too much perhaps—he helps me move it about. My own movements are confined these days, I'm afraid. There are resistance bands for the upper body too, though I must confess to laziness there. It requires just a bit of effort, which is precisely why it gets neglected so quickly. I could write an entire album about my misfortunes. There's the cancer, the walking frame, the little energy left. The stories are all there, waiting to be mangled. Years of living, of being a test subject, of struggling with energy, of walking with assistance, taught me this: when you finally find something that brings genuine pleasure without damaging your body, you hold onto it. I wish this joy had found me sooner.

review_title: eBay is a deeply broken marketplace…
review_text: eBay is a deeply broken marketplace where scammers thrive and honest customers are basically the punchline. It feels like they’ve built a playground for fraudsters, then stepped back to watch the chaos and count the money while buyers and sellers are left sweeping up the glass. Scammers can spin up accounts, grab your cash, vanish, and the system barely shrugs. Instead of tightening security or stepping in quickly, eBay’s idea of “buyer protection” is to make you wait. As a buyer, you’re expected to sit quietly for about a month before you can even open a claim and maybe begin the long, painful process of trying to get your money back. It’s like being mugged and then told to come back in 30 days to see if anyone feels like reading your complaint. And customer service? That’s gone. Retired. Bots have completely taken over. Good luck “talking” to a computer chip that has no intention of helping you in the first place. You’re funneled through endless scripted responses, fake “help” articles, and dead-end loops designed to protect the wealthy executives who designed this broken system, not the customer. No live agents, no real accountability, just the illusion of support while every ounce of effort and burden is dumped squarely on you … meanwhile, these executives are busy running to the bank. Cha-Ching. But let’s admit it: their fraud has been pretty successful since the early 90s. Still, if this is how buyers are treated, I can only imagine what honest sellers are enduring. They’re likely stuck dealing with fraudulent claims, inconsistent decisions, and a platform that seems far more invested in preserving its own metrics than protecting the people who actually keep it afloat. It looks and feels like a for‑profit machine built to keep the top tier happy, while everyone else is disposable. Here’s the deal in plain English: eBay has severed the public trust. What used to be a reasonably reliable marketplace now feels like a “you’re on your own” adventure game where the final boss is the company itself. If you absolutely must deal with them, do so with extreme caution. Assume no one is coming to help you, keep receipts, screenshots, and messages like you’re building a legal file because you just might need it. At this point, the smartest move is to close your eBay account and move to a marketplace that hasn’t sold its soul to automation and quarterly earnings. Never forget that the scams are on you, and the house always wins.

After the item was received, the seller repeatedly delayed the refund by citing internal “inspection” timelines that extended beyond eBay’s stated refund deadline. This experience showed me how easily sellers can complicate returns, delay refunds, and shift stress onto buyers — particularly disabled buyers who rely on clear, standardized processes. I had made $343 from the sale, but eBay wanted me to pay back $409, which is $66 more? They didn't give me an itemized invoice or any say at all, they just said they would be taking that about amount from my bank account! I took down almost everything in my eBay account, they are more trouble then they are worth! I feel robbed, and wronged, I think they have become a monopoly, which makes them app profit, and the products come from all of us. I'm left in a deficit. **UPDATE** I was finally able to talk with a live agent from customer service, and I told them that although the customer didn't seem to like the phone after he got it, as far as I knew (and according to Amazon) it was a real phone, not counterfeit? The agent filed an appeal for me, and said they would contact me Monday or Tuesday. I'm a Graphic Designer, and I do a lot of web design, if you are setting up a website that will involve items for sale, an easy to access USER FRIENDLY customer service area is vital! review_title: Higher Fees, Dishonest Buyers!
review_text: At one time, eBay was the hot online marketplace. No longer. The stigma of buyers wanting something for nothing or next to nothing was always there and is still true. If you sell on eBay, fees have gone up over the last year, with the introduction of optional promotion fees. These fees vary, but are typically 5-15% (on top of the fact that eBay collects a per-category percentage on the total amount of the sale, including shipping). Not opting in may mean less sales, assuming enough people do opt in. Return policies now favor buyers, even when a listing does not allow returns (and is priced accordingly). It's up to the seller to disprove false claims. There are enough dishonest buyers that it is a real problem, especially for anyone just selling personal items. That said, customer service has improved in the same time frame, despite having to navigate the somewhat obtuse help pages. Once at that point, a return call usually comes in 2-3 minutes, with the question answered or problem solved during the call. 2 stars overall.

review_text: I purchased a RV cover from ENDFOXSTORE on Ebay. We have a 30' RV and the cover was 30-33'. There was too much slack so we returned it in 3 days well within the 30 day return policy. We returned EVERYTHING, but the seller claimed that I did not return the "installation kit", BUT I DID. The seller would not budge, so I complained to Ebay who ruled in my favor, so I was refunded my full amount. Thank you Ebay, but buyer beware with ENDFOXSTORE.  Now I will have to document how I receive my purchases and my returns with lots of pictures to prove what I returned and the condition! ENDFOXSTORE provided a picture of the return, which I did in the ORIGINAL box. The picture only showed a duffle bag in the box. I had placed the "installation kit" pieces on top of the RV cover then cinched the bag closed. Why didn't they open the duffle bag and take a picture of the inside of the contents???

In 2025, ebay remains a solid platform for buying and selling. It's well designed and attractive. Recently added features contribute nicely to the user experience. The two stars off are due to fees. Yes, your items receive very little exposure because of the popularity of the platform; the staggering amount of competing listings will bury you. That isn't really their fault though and the advertising tools they added offer a workaround that lets the market sort this out via competition. But surely the advertising income earns them sufficient profit that they don't need to charge small sellers an additional 14% sellers fee for handmade items. Add that to shipping, materials, labor, taxes, and now advertising for exposure and gone are the days of your average seller making a living on eBay. review_text: I am giving eBay an extra star—moving from 2 to 3 stars —purely to acknowledge their excellent new update allowing home sellers to list used products for free with no commission and rightly keeping the vendors to be charged selling fees. As a platform for clearing out your garage, it’s now unbeatable. However, as a marketplace for tech, it remains a minefield of scams galore ​The "International  Scams While selling is better than ever, buying tech is becoming a high-stakes gamble. Especially on eBay now As an IT engineer, I recently purchased and  audited a "brand new sealed in box " unfortunately for me it was a phone from a Chinese vendor that I purchased from because I used my mobile phone where it's not quite as apparent since I don't ever buy from China any product above £20 . (Normally I use a PC which gives clearer information about the vendor location country) . Problems with the phone that I bought. It arrived with a modified, "dodgy" version of the Play Store baked into the firmware. Deceptively labeled as an "International ROM," these are security nightmares that block banking apps and leave your data exposed. The fake Play Store icon even survives a factory reset—a massive red flag that eBay’s automated systems seem to miss. ​The Seller vs. Buyer Imbalance: Despite my 22-year history and 100% feedback, eBay recently sided with a vendor over a technical dispute. It appears the platform currently prioritizes high-volume sellers over the security of its most loyal buyers. This is a dangerous trajectory; some people will always try to save a few pounds, but they are often buying "1TB USB sticks" for £12 that are mathematically impossible and lead to instant data corruption. ​The Need for a "UK Only" Filter: The UK Consumer Rights Act provides excellent protection, but those rights often evaporate the moment you buy from overseas. Dealing with "UK-based" drop-shippers who are actually shipping from China leads to a cycle of frustration designed to make the buyer give up. ​eBay desperately needs a "Default to UK Only" search preference. Forcing users to manually filter every single search just to avoid being scammed is unacceptable in 2026. ​Verdict: Top marks for the new commission-free selling for home users—that is a fantastic move. But until eBay allows us to filter out high-risk regions by default and cracks down on modified firmware, the burden of security remains entirely on the buyer. ​I have used AI to spell check my reviews

review_title: I'm a seller on ebay~~I've been selling…
review_text: I'm a seller on ebay~~I've been selling for over 24 years.  Buyers here complain but from what I've seen here they don't know the proper procedures to navigate ebay to get refunds if things go bad.  You say tracking says it was delivered but you didn't get it?  That is not the fault of the seller or ebay~~either you have a thief in your neighborhood or it may have been delivered to the wrong address~~contact your post office or rent a P.O. Box so you can pick up your packages & mail directly at the post office.  If both buyers & sellers used the options available correctly they might find they have no problems.  As stated~~I've been selling (& buying) on ebay for over 24 years & hopefully will have many more years ahead of me here on ebay. I'd like to add that there are as many scammer buyers on ebay as there are sellers.  They try to get things free by filing false claims.  I used to just refund & let them keep the item but over the last few years I've issued return labels to the buyer to return the item they aren't happy with to get a refund.  9 times out of 10 they never return the item.  They were just trying to get a refund & keep the items.  A few months ago a buyer contacted me asking if there were scratches on the inside of a casserole dish~~I assured him it was in excellent condition.  Within an hour of receiving it he filed a claim saying it was full of scratches.  The dish has a coated interior for non stick making it dull & not shiny.  I issued the return label but still haven't received the item but am stuck with a "return request" on my record.  I've read many of the reviews here & a lot of them could have had a different outcome had the buyer or seller known the correct procedures to follow to solve their problems.  I recently had a item not received complaint where the buyer said they didn't receive the item but tracking showed it was delivered~~I wasn't required to refund the buyer but ebay issued the buyer a refund with their own funds.  Ebay wants happy buyers & usually favor the buyers over the sellers.  As a buyer or seller learn the correct procedures & you usually won't have any problems like the reviews here describe.  Send EVERYTHING with tracking even though you have to charge the buyer for ground instead of media mail.  Most buyers will pay extra to have tracking so they know the seller actually did send it & they can see when it will be delivered.  You have to learn to protect yourself~~ebay can't protect you when you fail to protect yourself.

review_title: eBay is a crap shoot at best
review_text: eBay is a crap shoot at best. I’ve been a member since 1999. In the beginning eBay was amazing but people were different as well. Internet crime wasn’t so rampant and you could find some great deals and make some serious money. I did for many years buying and selling vintage pro analog equipment. Can’t do that anymore. Nowadays everybody is hip and everybody is a criminal until they’re not. There’s more scam artists than decent honest people anymore. eBay’s policies reflect that so much and it’s very sad, because the costs involved are getting higher and higher to the point where I don’t think it’s worth selling on eBay. But on occasion, I take a chance and buy something. I just bought a MacBook Pro and it’s a fantastic computer! Then again, I recently sold a analog mixing console and the cost involved in selling on eBay were astronomical! I lost so much money and I don’t even want to tell you how much, but it was a lot and I will never do that again. That said, eBay is a sad place and it looks like a Third World country but there are still good people and good buys. You just have to be really careful.

review_title: Defrauding a disabled senior male is a criminal act
review_text: I placed an order for home delivery on 12/31/2025 to be delivered at 8:00-10:00 pm. However, I started receiving notices that the delivery would be delayed. I continued seeing these notices until around 11:15 pm. At that time, I was directed to reschedule my delivery. I rescheduled it for 1/1/2026 at 4:00-6:00 pm. However, long before that time, I began receiving text messages telling me that I would have to come to the store to pick up my order. I must point out that I am 73 years of age, do not drive, do not own a motor vehicle, and suffer from documented disabling spinal conditions. I tried to get Walmart to make good on my order for home delivery, but Walmart persisted in sending me notices to come pick up the order. Some of the items in that order are needed immediately, but Walmart showed no intention of making the delivery. I have prepared a six-page PDF document that tells the entire story and includes images and print-outs of the story. I included the confirmation of my order on 12/31/2025, the notice given after my rescheduling for 1/1/2026 at 4:00-6:00 pm, and also screenshots of the text messages about the need to come pick up my order and the notice from the Walmart website confirming that I must come to pick up the delivery. It was on 1/2/2026 that Walmart sent an email telling me that my Walmart account had been deactivated and that I would not be permitted to place orders for home delivery. The reason that was given for the deactivation gave no complete explanation as to why deactivation was justified. I was told that I could only come to the store to shop in person. I think that trying to reach an agreement with Walmart would be worth far less than throwing a penny in a wishing well. Let me state that during my 21 years of residence in Washington, DC that ended on 4/8/2024, I was a Walmart customer there and frequently placed orders for home delivery. However, situations such as the ones that I have endured since relocating to Charles County, Maryland have been major culture shock. Walmart seems to be pursuing an extremist version of the sort of thumbs down attitude that is pervasive in Charles County. I have composed a file that explains the failing that ended on New Year's Day and the notice of deactivation of my account. I must mention that many times since I relocated to my current area of residence, deliveries were made to unidentifiable locations. It has been rare that I have placed an order, received a delivery to my home that contained all the items that I ordered. I had already traveled to Walmart with my caregiver driving many times because it was the only sure way that I could choose the items that I ordered, but if an item that I wanted to order was not in stock, I could search for a substitute of my choice. If these tasks were left for Walmart to process, the service record is dismal at best. Maybe if I threw a penny into a wishing well, that might get far more reliable service. I'm just desperate to find help to command Walmart to make serious corrective efforts because I now remain in a situation that if I should need an item urgently and cannot not arrange transportation, I would end up the loser and would be left in a very major crisis. Because Walmart has already revealed to me the rather dishonest character of the institution, I feel that demanding reparations would definitely be appropriate. Victims have a right to reparation, meaning that adequate measures to redress violations of human rights by providing a range of material and symbolic benefits to victims or their families as well as affected communities. Reparation must be adequate, effective, prompt, and should be proportional to the gravity of the violations and the harm suffered. As the OHCHR Support for Transitional Justice stated on its website, catalytic power that genuine remedy and reparations can have on the daily life of victims, families, communities and entire societies. That is what I feel is a fair and just way of solving a problem that Walmart created for me and shows a very malicious intention toward a disabled senior male whose income is well below the federal poverty level. To be fair, during my 21 years of residence in Washington, DC, I was a Walmart customer there and problems of this level of severity did not happen there. Relocating to Charles County, MD was definitely the worst culture shock that I have ever encountered in my entire life. I must add that my life story contains similar experiences that I endured on the other side of the Atlantic. I tell truthfully that li people that living here feels as if I have accidentally wondered onto a site where an episode for a revival of The Twilight Zone is being filmed using me as a character in the episode. That is my request and hope to receive it all.

review_title: Walmart's Aggravating "Plus"
review_text: This isn't just once.  I started ordering groceries from Walmart after my surgery when I couldn't get out to the store.  Probably 70% of the time, everything goes as planned.  But that 30% is just aggravating.  2 weeks ago, I ordered $150 worth of groceries.  That actually went well. 3 days ago, I ordered some snacks.  I had just joined Walmart Plus, but they only waive the shipping fee, not the delivery fee, unless the order is over $35.  ("Shipping" is from another location, not the one local to you.)  So, to get "free" delivery from my local store, I had to order $35 worth of snacks, otherwise pay an additional $6.99 for delivery.  So I placed the order, padding it with household items I might need, just to make the $35 requirement.  They texted me minutes before the delivery was to be made, telling me 3 items were unavailable and that I had to make substitutions.  It took a few minutes to make the selections, and when I did, I was told it was too late since the delivery was already on the way.  When I called about this, I was told I had to start a new order, which means either another $35 spent or a delivery fee.  I got them to credit the delivery fee, but by then it was too late for same-day delivery, so I received my 3 items the next day.  BUT I had to wait until the 3rd day for the remainder of the order, 2 items, shipped from Whoknowswhere. This afternoon, I got a text announcing the delivery, with a photo of it at someone else's front door!  So now I'm told I have to start yet ANOTHER ORDER to get these 2 items redelivered, and again argue about the delivery fee.  Then they have the nerve to ask for a tip! I hate the way they segment orders, so you often have to wait days to receive the complete order.  It is very inconvenient and frustrating.  Because of the segmenting of orders, your payments are also segmented, so you never know how much you're paying until it finally clears your bank account.  Same thing with receiving a credit -- you never know when you'll actually get it.  You end up having to do a lot of extra bookkeeping to keep track of it all.  The only thing that makes it tolerable is the lower prices, but that is wearing very  thin.

review_title: Walmart Plus Is Failing Apartment Dwellers—Here’s How to Fix It
review_text: Walmart Plus promised convenience, affordability, and access. But for apartment dwellers living alone—especially those on tight budgets—it’s become a logistical letdown. I’ve watched my order volume drop by 75% since they imposed a $35 minimum or a $6.99 penalty fee for smaller deliveries. That’s not just inconvenient—it’s regressive. Compare this to Instacart, where members enjoy a $10 minimum. Walmart’s fee structure matches Instacart’s non-member threshold. So incredibly, Walmart forces its own paying members to meet the same minimum as Instacart’s free-tier users. That’s not just bad math—it’s bad design. Walmart does offer a discount for low-income users, and I applaud that. But the delivery model undermines it. For those of us in apartment complexes, it would be trivial for Walmart to copy Amazon’s grouped delivery system. Let users opt into shared delivery windows. Let us piggyback on a neighbor’s upcoming order. Let us skip the fee. I proposed this. No response. No implementation. Not even an email acknowledging the suggestion. That’s not just poor customer service—it’s a breakdown in civic trust. Amazon has been batching deliveries for years. It’s efficient, scalable, and respectful of user needs. Walmart’s refusal to adopt this model makes it feel old-fashioned, out of touch, and structurally blind to how modern urban logistics work. Walmart doesn’t need to reinvent the wheel. It needs to listen, adapt, and treat delivery as a networked service—not a one-size-fits-all transaction. Until then, apartment dwellers like me will keep turning elsewhere.

Walmart had to get an authorization from my insurer for one of the medications and made a request by fax. Also, another medication wasn't in-stock, apparently, because I had to go back the next day to get it. On July 8, 2025, I went to pickup the one medication and asked about the pending authorization. She said it takes between 3-7 business days to hear from my insurer and that if I called my insurer, it may speed it up. So, I called Louisiana Healthcare Connections, which as anyone knows, has their own issues. After several recordings and live agents, they said they had faxed Walmart back on the same day, July 7, 2025, with a list of acceptable medications that could be used to replace the pending medication. I then called Walmart Corporate to ask if it takes Walmart Pharmacy in Deridder, Louisiana 3-7 business days to receive a fax from my insurer. This associate also had to do some research, and to my surprise, it does take 3-7 business days to receive a fax from insurers. Now, I'm sure there's something behind this length of time that they're not telling us about but it needs to be fixed. Everyone knows how long it takes to send or receive a fax. If this is true, USPS would be faster. Anyway, the associate politely offered to escalate the issue. Just a note. When contacting all the above, it was very difficult to get to a live person. review_title: A year of disappointment.
review_text: A Year of Walmart+ Disappointment: Beyond Frustration I am writing this review as a deeply frustrated, former loyal member of Walmart+ for over a year. What was marketed as a convenient service has consistently proven to be anything but. I've tolerated a litany of issues, but the latest incident has pushed me past my breaking point and has completely eroded any trust or goodwill I once had for Walmart. For months, I've put up with excessively long shipping times that directly contradict the promise of "fast delivery." Even more galling, I've frequently been charged for shipping on items that should have qualified for free delivery under my membership. This alone is a direct breach of the service's core value proposition. Beyond the misleading shipping, the most insidious issue has been the lack of transparency regarding unfulfilled orders. Walmart does not notify you when items are missing from your delivery or when your order is incomplete. Instead, it falls entirely on the customer to meticulously review every online receipt to identify discrepancies and verify charges. This has cost me countless hours, forcing me to play detective just to ensure I'm not paying for items I never received. It's an unacceptable burden placed squarely on the customer. The final straw occurred just the other night. With out-of-town elderly guests arriving, I attempted to place a crucial grocery order of approximately $250. My payment information was current, and deliveries to my address are routine. Despite being a paying member and receiving daily marketing emails from Walmart, I was blocked from checking out due to a bizarre and impossible request to verify an "old email address from years ago." This completely inexplicable and ill-timed technical failure prevented me from completing my essential order. The result? I was forced to abandon my cart, rush to Publix to buy all my groceries, and then immediately head to the airport to pick up my guests. This was a massive inconvenience and completely ruined my evening plans, all thanks to Walmart's abysmal system. Walmart+, you have repeatedly failed to deliver on your promises. You've wasted my time, charged me for services I didn't receive, and most recently, you left me in an impossible bind during a critical moment. My loyalty has been met with nothing but frustration and incompetence. I strongly advise anyone considering a Walmart+ membership to think twice. The supposed convenience is overshadowed by persistent problems and a complete disregard for the customer experience. Thanks for the Paramount Plus.

review_title: I actually like Walmart
review_text: I actually like Walmart. Not going in, but ordering groceries online for curbside pickup. This is like the most convenient thing ever, and I love it. Simple and time saving convenience at no extra charge.  If something you asked for is on backorder, and it has no shipping charge in the original description, they ship it to you free. Now, don't get me wrong, this system comes with it's drawbacks, just like anything else.  But the benefits outweigh the occasional (semi frequent) snag. Even then, they really try to make your experience as easy as possible. Take, for example, this floor wax I ordered. They sent me floor shine on accident.  I caught the mistake & just hopped back on my Account page,  pressed the start a return button, & printed a free return shipping label.  The next day fed ex came to my house & retrieved it.  I had an option of a refund back to my card or store cred for online ordering. I immediately was able to use my cred as soon as they received the floor shine back.  Easy peasy. And once they gave me a salad that was 2 days expired.  Once they left a salad out altogether.  And the order packers do not find nice produce intentionally. If they do,  it's purely random. I've come to realize that they just grab whatever is on top, and sometimes it is not a good thing.  Oh and they have ignored my substitution request for some Popsicles and tried subbing them with some yucky ones I definitely didn't want so I didn't get any Popsicles. Even with all these mistakes, I still choose online over walking in. Great concept! No effort required. Arlington, Texas @ Randol Mill road is my store, across the street from ATT stadium.

I had developed entirely new original collections and was actively removing non-compliant listings when access was revoked. I am not writing this review out of anger. I am writing it because I am devastated to have lost something I worked so hard to build, and because there is simply no way to reach a human being at Etsy to have a genuine conversation about what happened. The appeals process is automated and the outcome felt instant. For a platform built on independent creators and small businesses, I would ask Etsy to consider a more compassionate and human approach to sellers who made mistakes but genuinely want to make things right. review_title: Avoid opening an Etsy store
review_text: TLDR: The platform is a financial and time drain where high fees for Google visibility, forced refunds without returns, and a lack of protection against false reviews create a rigged system for sellers. You are better off building your own website where you control your business and reputation. The most successful path is the one where you don't have to fight your OWN marketplace just to survive. If you are considering starting a business, the strongest advice for any prospective entrepreneur is simple: Do not open an Etsy store. Selling on Etsy has become a hostile experience where the platform prioritizes automated metrics over the actual protection of the people who make and sell the goods. You will likely spend thousands of hours building a brand on "rented land," only to find the system is working against you. The "Google Visibility" Trap The biggest attraction to Etsy is the promise of instant Google visibility and built-in traffic. However, this is a calculated financial drain: Offsite Ad Fees: Etsy forces many sellers into "Offsite Ads," where they pass the cost of every Google click right back to the seller. You can end up paying an additional 12% to 15% on top of their already massive transaction and payment fees. The Cost of Fraud: When you factor in these fees alongside how often Etsy allows buyers to defraud sellers, the math doesn't work. It is objectively cheaper to pay for your own Google advertising or use a platform with its own visibility than to let Etsy take a massive cut while offering zero protection. The Feedback Loop: A Shield of Immunity The "law" Etsy frequently cites to justify their refusal to remove false or defamatory reviews is Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act.  Under this federal law, online platforms are generally not held legally responsible for content posted by their users. Etsy utilizes this as a shield to remain "neutral," avoiding the labor-intensive task of mediating truth. Even when sellers provide definitive proof that a buyer is committing fraud, Etsy will almost never intervene. This allows false negative feedback to stand indefinitely, damaging your store's reputation without recourse. The "Purchase Protection" Pitfall & Forced Refunds Etsy’s automated systems allow buyers to defraud sellers through the Purchase Protection Program. Even when a seller is cooperative, offers a full refund, and provides a prepaid return label, the system is often weaponized: * Forced Refunds: Etsy frequently issues refunds from the seller’s account even if the item is NOT returned and the seller proves it was exactly as described. Essentially, Etsy allows buyers to keep both the money and the product, leaving the seller with a total loss on inventory, shipping, and fees. * Premature Cases: Buyers can bypass direct communication and escalate to a case as soon as 48 hours after a help request. These cases negatively impact a shop’s visibility and "Star Seller" status regardless of the resolution. * Lack of Oversight: Sellers are expected to absorb the cost of carrier delays and buyer errors. A Rigged System and the Time Trap For the average independent seller, it often feels like the success stories are outliers or the result of sellers being forced to refund every unsatisfied buyer just to stay alive. Buyers know this and frequently exploit Etsy's unwillingness to protect their sellers. The Algorithm Wall: The search algorithm is a "black box" that prioritizes shops spending heavily on internal advertising. There is a pervasive sentiment that the only shops seeing consistent growth are those with "insider" knowledge of platform loopholes—perhaps only those who work at Etsy or have in the past. The Sunk Cost: By the time many sellers realize the platform is hostile, they have already invested thousands of hours into SEO and branding. This makes it harder to leave, even as they become fed up with the lack of support and eroding profit margins. The Final Verdict: Save Your Sanity Etsy has become a marketplace that has turned its back on the creators who built its reputation. Instead of pouring your life’s work into a platform that allows repeated false claims to destroy your business, consider building your own website where you control the rules and own your customer list. Your time and talent are too valuable to be wasted on a site that does not value its sellers. The most successful path is the one where you don't have to fight your OWN marketplace just to survive.

review_title: If You Sell Rare Items, You Should Stand Behind Them
review_text: Etsy positions itself as a marketplace for unique and rare items, but my experience shows that the platform does not take responsibility once a problem arises. I purchased a one-of-a-kind, author-made ring. After wearing it only a few times, the stone fell out. The seller initially responded and sent a replacement stone, but it turned out to be the wrong size and could not be fitted. After that, the seller completely stopped responding. Because the item is unique, no local jeweler can repair it without the original maker. As a result, I am left with a broken, unusable item. Despite contacting Etsy Support many times, the platform refused to meaningfully assist, citing that too much time had passed since the purchase. In practice, this means that if a seller stops communicating, Etsy simply removes itself from responsibility, even when the item is defective and the buyer has no way to resolve the issue independently. If a platform chooses to sell rare, author-made items, it should also take responsibility for post-purchase support and buyer protection. Unfortunately, in my case, Etsy did not.

review_title: Incompetent customer service, faulty tracking system
review_text: Etsy used to be great. I could order from anywhere in the world and immediately knew how much the overall cost will be. Unlike some other customers, I actually only ordered from proven sellers, who were all lovely and helpful within their limits, therefore I had no scam problem. And unlike my compatriots (based in CZ), I was able to reach Etsy through customer service - which is where their doom starts. My previous order was in early autumn 2025, and I ordered from the US, once Etsy tracking started showing the package reached Czechia, I contacted CS to ask for the tracking number as I wasn't sure if the customs were properly processed. I was given the right answer - and was able to pick the package up at the local post when it was possible. I would have preferred transparency on the Etsy's side and having the tracking shown immediately, though. As a buyer, I should be able to have the tools needed to contact my post in case I'm not able to wait at home for the delivery. Since the CS was originally able to help me, though, I didn't think it was a big deal back then. My latest experience, however, was extremely stressful. I ordered once again from the US in December. It was a different seller, but I already ordered from her before and everything went smoothly. Until now. I saw the package reached my country, according to Etsy tracking. I wanted to have some control over when it gets delivered, and reached out to CS to ask for the number. They provided me the tracking number of USPS, then said they're going to forward this to the seller, who of course didn't know - Etsy was the one doing the tracking, the seller could only watch. I reached out to CS several times - repeating, explaining I need the tracking number of the Czech post - I even referred to the earlier chat from early autumn where the worker immediately understood what I needed. All of the people with whom I was connected with (all had Indian-sounding names - aka, is Etsy hiring people from third world countries to save expense?) claimed they only had two tracking numbers - USPS and Global post, both of which showed the package was DELIVERED TO AN AGENT (aka, obviously Czech Post). They annoyingly kept repeating phrases like "let me fix this for you" (aka probably following corporate rules but not actually solving anything) but couldn't look into it or contact the post for me. Instead, they kept suggesting I open a case - lazy solution. It was Christmas break, I was out of town with my family, and wanted to be able to contact my LOCAL post and ensure I receive it. One of them, Arbaz, only looked up the USPS number, saw "delivered to an agent" and told me it must have been delivered! Why are they letting people, who don't understand how international shipping works, work in customer service of an international shop company?! As already said, the tracking should be transparent and allow the customer to have control over their package. Etsy's build-in tracking may show where the package approximately is, but offers no way of CONTACTING THE CARRIER.  Moreover, my last order's delivery got updated LATE - on DECEMBER 29th, it claimed that there was a FAILED DELIVERY ATTEMPT ON DECEMBER 23RD! I was at home that day, and no delivery attempt was made. This is more onto CZ post than Etsy itself, however, if I knew it on that day, I could have tried retrieving the package the following day through my ID, as it contained a Christmas present for my mother. I eventually succeeded in getting my package via showing my ID at the post. Unfortunately, for both me and the kind seller, it wasn't the end of trouble. The seller probably got stressed out by CS (who kept suggesting to open a case) to refund my payment. The same day, I was finally able to pick the package up, but I found that out after getting home. We both proceeded to contact Etsy to return the refund back to the seller, and were told it's not possible. I don't understand why it should not be possible. Now, I'll have to wait once the refund processes and hopefully return it to the seller via PayPal. (that is, if I'll receive the refund at all...) Lastly, the CZ post tracking number I was trying to get out of Customer service, was WRITTEN ON THE PACKAGE. Considering Etsy kept tracking it, despite the number change, the package had to be scanned under the new number and Etsy had to have access to it. Once again, this problem would be solved if Etsy's tracking was transparent to the buyer. As someone who loves supporting small businesses, this was a huge disappointment. I hope Etsy will fix its reputation and all its quirks, but until then, I refrain from shopping there again. I doubt Etsy's team will read this, but TLDR - FIX THE TRACKING, MAKE IT TRANSPARENT TO THE BUYER, AND HIRE PPL WHO UNDERSTAND INTERNATIONAL SHIPPING!

review_title: Overall good but can improve
review_text: I made almost 20 purchases on Etsy between June 2024 and May 2025. I love the extreme selection of products available on the said platform. My overall experience is that sellers ship in time and ship what I order. In one case, the 300-euro product was a bit damaged and visibly different from what I ordered, and Etsy issued a refund immediately. (I don't know whether they'd do that the second or third time, too.) In a couple of other cases, the product quality was not as good as promised. Here, of course, I could have demanded a refund, too, but the thing is that when you order a tailor-made garment from someone in India for €65 and the received product has got some flaws, you just don't give him a one-star review or demand a full refund from Etsy and ruin a business that is crucial for his income, you just let it go... What I'm saying is that when you buy from developing countries, your will sometimes be deeply impressed, other times disappointed, and accept that as part of the privilege of us ordinary citizens having access to handmade crafts from all across the world. I've had problems with Etsy charging VAT on behalf of my national customs and myself being charged VAT by my national customs simultaneously because of sellers failing to provide compulsory VAT details in the electronic shipping system, with Etsy subsequently refusing to refund the VAT money when I've paid double, despite my providing required documents. Considering that my country has an import VAT of 25%, I've effectively been forced to pay 50% VAT on purchased goods, the reason for why I've been forced to reduce my purchases on Etsy significantly. Thus, I give Etsy 3 out of 5 stars.

review_title: Pros and Cons to Etsy from a Buyer’s Perspective…
review_text: As a consistent buyer on Etsy for 14 years, I can say thus far the overall experience has been mostly pleasant. Of course there are some bad apples but as a buyer, I kindly urge you to reach out to the sellers via messaging with any questions you may have prior to ordering - so you can get a feel of whom you are dealing with. In addition, reading a shop’s reviews is definitely a useful tool and if they have a habit of sending out orders late or not at all and/or lacking of customer service - then you know what to do. Just move on, they’re not worth your time. This has saved me from a lot of potential negative experiences and headaches. My time is precious and so is yours. Etsy can be a fun shopping experience if you know how to use it right and I have ordered one too many handmade items from decor, seasonal, crystals, apparel, furniture, etc etc etc. What I’m not keen on is Etsy’s customer service. Over the years they’ve lessened their support to the point where it’s nearly impossible to get a live person on the phone and their chat is completely useless. Apparently it’s not the case for just buyers but for sellers too, which is unfortunate because I have seen one too many of my beloved shops abandoning Etsy altogether due to their ever-increasing fees as well as lack of support and moving onwards to Instagram and/or opening up their own websites. Etsy has been giving the impression they do not care about buyers and sellers and just pocketing the money. Etsy, let’s not forget how your company came to be. Without buyers and sellers, you wouldn’t be around. With this said, I have been decreasing my purchases over the past months although I still pop in once in awhile to make purchases with the shops I wholeheartedly trust and love.

review_title: Gone downhill as a place to sell

At first, it was great - the fees were much cheaper than a certain well-known auction site (where I sold before), and I got enough sales to justify being there. But over the last year or two sales have plummeted and I'm thinking of shutting my shop. Etsy's main problem (IMO) is that it doesn't seem to know who it is. OTOH, it pitches itself as a place to buy hand-made, one-of-a-kind gifts - mainly homewares. But when you actually look on the site, there's an awful lot of mass-produced stuff. There are also categories like supplies and digital items, which simply don't feature in Etsy's expensive advertising campaigns and so must surely be missing out on new customers. The same applies to vintage - unless you already know that Etsy does vintage items, you certainly wouldn't find out from the TV advertising and it wouldn't be all that obvious from browsing the site either. Final word: I've read some of the other reviews and can I just say to Etsy that if Temu is getting a better rating than you, then you need to sort yourself out.

review_title: READ WHOLE REVIEW!!
review_text: Ok. Completely honest review here. Been using ETSY for about 6 or 7 years now and would like to bring up a couple things. I like ETSY because I like supporting small shops. And you can find some really awesome unique stuff. Some not so much. More on that in a few.  I’m giving ETSY 3 stars only because of the shops and sellers that I’ve ordered from. They’ve been great. I’ve had one issue with an item and the seller fixed it light speed. So no problems there. That’s the good. Here’s the bad. And a suggestion as well. Whatever you’re looking for on ETSY and I mean WHATEVER you are looking for or find on ETSY shop around first. What I’ve noticed is ALOT of jewelry labeled “handmade” can be found on Amazon way cheaper. If you check out TEMU (which I don’t suggest unless you want your identity stolen) it’s pennies on the dollar. And it doesn’t stop there. I would say about 60% of that sites items are bought in bulk and sold at a 50% markup. Sometimes more. Which is pretty sad. The site sells itself as a place to get handcrafted items. And there are some really talented shops in there. But they’re few and far between as the years have gone on. So do your research and check other websites to see if you can get it cheaper. And it’ll most likely arrive sooner as well. Another thing I would like to bring up is, reading other reviews and some of them mentioned packages being stolen and delivery services not leaving them indoors for the customer. One reviewer said only USPS leaves them inside. Well I appreciate that. As I’m a letter carrier. But. And I will say Fed Ex, UPS and DHL do tend to leave packages outside. Not all the time tho. Sometimes they have no choice. If you live in an apartment complex 99% of the time those 3 have no way of opening a locked main entrance door. Letter carriers have what USPS calls arrow keys which will open most of those doors. So another suggestion. If you have a package being delivered FedEx, UPS or DHL and are afraid that it’ll be stolen. Either pay the extra for signature tracking or have it delivered to a hub and pick it up. Delivery services are businesses. The drivers are told to come back with an empty truck. These guys are just doing there jobs. Some of them are really bad. But the majority are really good.

review_title: I love Etsy
review_text: I love Etsy. I’ll just say that upfront. For a million reasons. But my topic for today is a growing concern, and I can’t post this to the Etsy community board, because I’m a ‘read only’ consumer. The issue is lost packages. International shippers do not understand how prevalent porch piracy is, within the U.S. we have safe delivery addresses, IF the delivery drivers would walk an extra 3 feet and put packages inside the buildings. If they don’t, it’s likely the package itself that will walk. So all these lost packages are being stolen, because FEDEX, yes them, DHL, and UPS will not put the mail inside. I’ve contacted my shippers multiple times, especially FEDEX, but it has little effect.  USPS is the only outfit that puts packages inside. So if you want to get your mail, have it shipped through usps, when possible. Overseas shippers have the option of creating this requirement for their packages.  But they need to specifically ask for it. Shippers also often fail to provide tracking information, which would go a long way to helping the consumer eliminate theft on their end. So please ETSY businesses, rather than accusing your buyers of negligence, look at your own responsibility as a shipper. Consumers need tracking information, and the requirement that packages are put inside their buildings. Demand this. Theft is too rampant to do otherwise.

review_text: I have ordered several items on Etsy.  I was happy with most of the items I bought.  This is why I gave 3 stars.  The ones that did not work out for me, I kept because unlike Amazon, returns are not easy to do with Etsy.  You deal directly with the individual sellers who decide about your return.  You contact them directly.  Etsy does not guarantee them.  You may incur shipping cost to return back to the seller.  Also sellers charge shipping cost to send you what you bought.  A few sellers offer free shipping.  Most sellers are internationally based so your recourse, if things do not work out for you, is very very limited. What is nice about Etsy are the unique hand-made items created by individual sellers.  Ones that are hard to find elsewhere.  You have to weed through the hundreds of sellers and you just might find something nice & unique. I would buy on Etsy items that are not expensive and ones that I can afford to monetarily lose. review_title: Be careful...
review_text: First of all Etsy is not a seller. It's kind of like Ebay. Etsy handles the interface to the seller, but the seller is going to determine your experience. Etsy is supposed to handle the emails concerning the purchase though (receipt, etc.) My recommendation is to create an account before you purchase, as I had a bad experience using the guest account for purchase. If you are concerned about returns, Etsy doesn't handle them, the seller does, so you'll have to look for their policies. Support (Etsy) is mainly by chat, and finding the link is a little complicated. (Start with the Help link.) You'll need your email receipt. The seller I used was selling jewelry and IT WAS JUNK even though the pictures showed otherwise, so be careful. Don't expect to find a phone number. If you need to communicate with the seller, you'll need an Etsy account, logged in, and you purchase confirmation in front of you (on the web site.) You'll need to click on message and from there on it'll be like texting them directly. All this is on the Etsy web site. Good luck! For anything complicated DON'T USE THE APP, instead use your PC browser.

review_text: I have been a professional seller on etsy since 2017. Now, is it perfect? No. However, recently many sellers have become frustrated because of payment reserves. Shops have been shut down for breaking the rules they agreed to upon selling on etsy. Yes, there are mistakes in suspensions, but there are countless sellers like me who maintain the star seller rating, get daily sales and make their livelihood from etsy. Is it easy? No, you really have to approach it as a business and it takes time. Etsy is a marathon, not a sprint--not matter what "experts" claim. But with dedication you can make a success. If it were not for etsy giving me a platform to sell when I fled DV, I would not have been able to support myself or my family. Selling on etsy is my full time profession. The downside right now is the amount of resellers, infringement items and mass influx of AI art. But, if you are serious about turning a hobby or passion into a business, with hard work, it is still possible on etsy.

My advice is to always pay by PayPal. Make sure you ask questions in advance about the location of the seller. This is an international platform. Check yourself on import duties and fees so that you are not caught out. Also ask about guarantees and warranty details. When you make a purchase do so, armed with the information you need to make a confident purchase. I’ve bought some amazing items on this platform. Sellers and Artisans who put in an incredible amount of time and effort and show great pride in the items they make and sell. You cannot blame Etsy because you purchased from an international seller then were hit with import duties. The location of the sellers is clearly listed. Some sellers include import duties and taxes in the cost. Others do not so if it’s not in the item description then ask. You can also filter so that you only see sellers located in the U.K. on search.

I then spent 30 minutes looking through the many other custom-made monitor stands, ordered one, and in checkout, I applied the Etsy credit. It is now eight days since i made a payment, having called Paypal twice and was cut off twice, by them, i waited another day and tried again eventually getting through to an actual living breathing human being. They could not understand why, the payment was showing on my account but was still not showing on my credit ballance, so as usual, i was placed on hold whilst they put me through to another department. review_title: Decent Payment Processing with Room for Improvement
review_text: PayPal has established itself as a widely recognized and convenient payment solution, but it has its fair share of shortcomings. While it offers some benefits, there are aspects of PayPal that could be improved upon. One of the notable advantages of using PayPal is its widespread acceptance. Many online merchants and service providers support PayPal as a payment method, making it a convenient option for customers. The user interface is generally straightforward, making it easy to send and receive payments, and the ability to link bank accounts and credit cards provides flexibility in funding sources. However, PayPal's fees can be quite high, especially for certain types of transactions. The fee structure can be complex to understand, and it's important for users to carefully review the associated costs. Additionally, when it comes to currency conversion, PayPal's exchange rates are often less favorable compared to other alternatives, leading to potential financial losses for international transactions. Another drawback is PayPal's customer support, which is known for being inconsistent. While some users have reported positive experiences, others have faced challenges when trying to resolve issues. The response times can vary, and the overall support experience may not always meet expectations. PayPal's dispute resolution process can also be frustrating for users. While it offers protection against unauthorized transactions and buyer/seller disputes, the resolution process can be lengthy and complex. This can result in delays and potential frustrations for those seeking resolution for payment-related problems. Furthermore, PayPal's account limitations and occasional freezes are known to cause inconvenience for users. These restrictions can be imposed with little to no explanation, leaving users without access to their funds and requiring additional steps to resolve the issue. In conclusion, PayPal is a widely accepted and convenient payment solution, but it falls short in several areas. The high fees, unfavorable currency conversion rates, inconsistent customer support, and occasional account limitations detract from the overall user experience. While it remains a popular choice for many, PayPal could benefit from addressing these concerns to provide a more reliable and user-friendly payment service.

review_title: Review for the Paypal application.
review_text: PayPal is unrivaled when it comes to the ease of making payments online. Users can safely send and receive money with just an email address and an authorized password, eliminating the need to share sensitive financial information with various merchants. Wide Acceptance: Due to its widespread acceptance by online stores and businesses around the world, PayPal is a flexible payment mechanism for a variety of transactions, from purchases to bill payments. Security: PayPal uses robust security measures, including fraud detection systems, encryption technology, and buyer protection programs, to protect users' financial information from unauthorized access. Customer Protection: The PayPal Buyer Protection policy shields customers from potential scams and disputes with merchants. If an approved item doesn't exist or match the description, PayPal could issue a refund. Cellular Payments: The useful on-the-go payment and money transfer features of the mobile app expand PayPal's reach. International Business: Because the software handles the operation automatically, PayPal users may send and receive money internationally without worrying about currency adjustments. Connecting Various Payment Methods: Users who use PayPal can connect their accounts to a variety of financing options, such as credit cards and bank accounts, increasing their financial freedom. At the end i would say online purchases have undoubtedly altered as a result of PayPal, which provides users with unmatched convenience, security, and variety. Due to its wide acceptance and buyer protection strategy, many clients and corporations favor it. Users need to be on the lookout for potential account limits, platform fees, and customer service issues.

Instead, the disputes team completely messed up and closed the case the first time around. When I called them up, I told them it was imperative that they spoke to me in person and didn't just accept GOAT's version of events, because GOAT gave a totally wrong narrative and I have a very long email trail to prove it. Crucially, I highlighted to both GOAT and Klarna right at the start in February that I was recovering from major surgery and needed this sorted quickly because of the stress and worry it was causing. I also explicitly told Klarna they needed to speak to me over the phone because of my ADHD and dyslexia, as trying to navigate the broken written systems of both GOAT and Klarna was causing so much frustration. I have always been a very good customer of Klarna, which they can clearly see from my exemplary record, and I am so deeply disappointed in the service I've received this time. It has completely taken away my confidence in using them. When the second dispute was opened, I stated clearly in a thorough email that I needed a phone call and not another generic response because of how incompetent they were the first time. Instead of calling me, Klarna ignored my email and all my evidence for weeks. It was only when I chased them by phone two days ago that they suddenly closed the case and claimed it’s now "out of time"—a deadline issue that is entirely down to Klarna's own three-month delay. We are now in May and this is still dragging on. When I demanded to speak to a higher manager on the phone to get this resolved, I was refused. When I explained on the phone that I was deeply upset by this and that they needed to put another stop on future payments until this is fully resolved, they refused that too. I was just told it had been referred to the complaints team and to watch out for an email. That is no way to treat a valued customer. This is highly upsetting because at every single point I have cooperated and just wanted it resolved as quickly as possible. My involvement with Klarna has actually caused more problems than it’s solved, and the extraordinary amount of personal work I’ve put into trying to resolve this just to get this outcome is ridiculous. I thought the whole point of using a company like Klarna was to get protection against things like this. Now they've reinstated the payment plan, forcing me to pay £64.35 for faulty shoes, and are trying to get the remaining £42.90 for a product I can't even use. I am more than happy to return the goods because I have no use for faulty trainers that are not as described under British law; they are literally still sitting in the box taking up room in my house. My view was I needed to speak to a senior manager as soon as possible to discuss this entire process and work to a resolution. review_title: Moldy, unsafe, fraudulent property - Booking.com ignored us for 16+ hours
review_text: I booked Casa Colorista En El Casco Antiguo in Alicante as an anniversary surprise for my sister and her husband. What they walked into was a health hazard and a complete fraud. The apartment had visible mold covering walls and ceiling, a structurally collapsing ceiling with open holes, filth and dust everywhere, and a wardrobe full of the owner’s personal belongings. The Booking.com listing photos show none of this. When confronted, the owner Eduardo told us the mold is “authenticity.” I have the full WhatsApp conversation to prove it. We called Booking.com support — they hung up. The chat took 16+ hours to respond, only to say they would “check with the owner.” We were forced to find and pay for alternative accommodation ourselves for an anniversary trip. Booking.com endorses fraudulent listings, ignores guests in crisis, and protects dishonest hosts. I am now pursuing a full refund, filing complaints with consumer protection authorities, and disputing the charge with my bank. Do not trust this platform with important trips. They will leave you stranded.

review_title: Fake reviews of properties, utterly unhelpful customer service
review_text: I have been a long term user of booking.com I recently stayed at a property via booking.com in wadi rum Jordan. Property was called "Nadine Luxury camp and Bubbles" where the property owner fraudulently gave himself a 10/10 rating when my phone was in his hands for taking some pictures of me ostensibly. I think this dilutes the very essence of ratings and reviews on booking.com's platform. I have tried for nearly a week to get this sorted via their customer service but they come back with the same stock answer - click this and that and post your review. But the post review button is not visible strangely. This is my actual review that booking.com cs is not able to let me post. Why? : 1 star “Booked this property for a night and was poor experiences from word go. They have 5 bubbles on site and a very basic dining hall. The bubble number 2 that I was had an AC that was completely ineffective - the owner Ahmed said the AC does not cool because the bubbles are plastic!! Then say that on your property description. Second, the bathroom had only cold water and this matters as nights in the wadi rum are cold, the toilet douche did not work. The bed and duvet sheets were synthetic and not cotton which felt not very nice. When asked for drinking water Ahmed said ‘take it from the fridge’, not bothered to even send water upto the room. I specified that I am vegetarian YET the breakfast box in the morning had cold tinned meat pieces on it along with dry bread and butter and cheese cubes - that’s it, I gave it back - as this was not breakfast it was a poor joke. I was charged £40 each (£80) for a 2 hour sunset and a 1.5 hour sunrise dune tour. The pick up truck was ancient, the windows did not work, the pain work was rusted, the windscreen was covered in sand and the wipers did not work and the seating at the back was benches covered in dirty rugs. What was most shocking though was that they used my phone to take my photos and posted themselves a 10/10 review on booking cm which I have now complained to them to remove and rectify. All around awful experience- I think most of their high reviews are faked like mine was above! “ I emailed two senior booking.com executives on linked in to seek their help after failing with CS. One was Chief Business Officer at Booking.com and the other Global Talent Acquisition Leader @ Booking.com. Neither has bothered to look at the message. Will avoid this platform from now onwards.

review_title: Poor service quality, incompetent company
review_text: Poor service quality, incompetent platform! I booked a flight from Nantes to Palma de Mallorca specifically because it was advertised as a DIRECT flight via Booking.com. That was the entire reason I chose and paid for this ticket. After everything was booked and paid, they suddenly sent an email saying the flight had been changed. The original journey was around 1 hour 45 minutes. After their “change,” it became a 5-hour trip with connections. That is NOT a minor modification — it is a completely different journey. Then I contacted the customerservice-very tough journey: you have to wait on line over 30 -50 mins to get the phone call through and they promised to come back with solution but they never did. They just refer the client to the airline directly. The airline is even a big jok: you can never get a living person to talk to, unless you tell the bot that you need a new booking!!! Naturally, I requested a cancellation and refund because I do not accept such a significant change. Their response was basically: “Since we informed you more than 15 days before departure, you are not entitled to a refund. You may only rebook another flight with us.” In other words: they just work with the airlines and take your money first, then change the product entirely, and finally trap you into their loop. This company treats customers like cattle to be milked for money — first extracting every cent possible, then showing absolutely no respect or responsibility afterward. Absolutely unacceptable business practices. Avoid this company if possible.

review_title: I am extremely disappointed with…
review_text: I am extremely disappointed with Booking’s service. We had a serious issue with a car rental reservation due to an error on their platform. We correctly filled in all the details and selected my partner as the main driver, as I do not have a driving licence. However, the system automatically assigned my name as the main driver because it is my account. When we reviewed the booking, my partner’s name was correctly entered as the main driver, and we also completed both the driver and billing details using his information. Despite this, at the rental desk my name appeared as the main driver, making it impossible for us to pick up the vehicle. We contacted customer service and spoke with several agents, but none of them provided a real solution. Although they partially acknowledged the issue, they refused to give us a full refund. The response to our complaint was clearly an automated, generic email that did not address our case at all. After researching online, we found many similar complaints on Google and Trustpilot, so this is clearly not an isolated issue. I would not recommend using Booking for car rentals.

review_title: Systemic platform failures left my family stranded at a foreign transit hub
review_text: Booking.com is a liability for families. They cancelled our confirmed accommodation, leaving me stranded at a foreign transit hub with my family. Their customer support was entirely non-existent when we needed urgent help. I was forced to scramble for hours to secure a replacement room via Agoda, costing me extra out-of-pocket expenses. Every single follow-up email I have sent since the trip has been completely ignored. Worse, as a former host on their platform, I experienced the exact same systemic failure last year when their system double-booked my property, forcing me to manage stranded, angry guests via WhatsApp while I was in a remote area with intermittent Wi-Fi and zero support from Booking.com. Whether you are booking a holiday or hosting one, this platform will abandon you the second their system fails. Use alternative platforms that actually understand customer care and basic duty of care.

review_text: Absolute nightmare. "PLACE OF SCAMERS" is booking.com Do not book in this website! Save your Money and time We booked a specific villa for a family getaway (8 adults, 3 kids, including an 8-month-old baby), but our experience was a complete disaster from start to finish. On May 1st, 2026, we arrived at 11:00 AM at the location shown on the app, only to be told our selected villa wasn't available. We were forced to travel another 6-7 km to a different property. When we arrived, there was no management—just a boy who refused to let us see the room. We were forced to wait until 1:00 PM for the management team to arrive. They aggressively demanded full payment and slapped us with mysterious "extra charges" before even letting us inspect the villa. Wanting to save our holiday, we paid and went inside. The 3-BHK villa was filthy. When we complained, we were met with empty promises. Ground floor bedroom: Infested with insects and ants. 1st-floor bedrooms: The ACs did not cool, and the ceiling fans were broken. Bathrooms: Not a single drop of running water. We complained continuously until 8:00 PM. After we finally lost our tempers, the staff pretended to fix the plumbing—and incredibly, they actually made us help them do the plumbing work! It felt like we paid them just to work as their maintenance crew. To top it off, the swimming pool was an toxic chemical hazard—it looked like chlorine with a little bit of water mixed in, completely unsafe for children. Exhausted and completely stressed, we packed up and fled the resort at 11:00 PM. A management representative named Joshua promised a 50% refund. Weeks later, he is still dodging us and pretending to be responsible while doing absolutely nothing. They ruined our family peace, wasted our time, and stole our money. Avoid this scam at all costs!

review_title: Refund acknowledged in writing on 5 March 2026 — still unpaid on 20 May 2026.
review_text: Refund acknowledged in writing on 5 March 2026 — still unpaid on 20 May 2026. Booked an airport taxi through Booking.com (Gdańsk → Sopot, 4 February 2026, arrival 00:25, flight W61792). The driver confirmed by SMS she would be waiting. She never showed up. We waited an hour at the airport at night in freezing temperatures, called and texted multiple times — no answer. Had to take Uber (166.93 PLN). Full evidence sent: booking with correct flight details, driver's SMS confirmation, call logs, Uber receipt. First agent (Maram, 25 Feb): refused, claimed flight details were missing. They weren't. Second agent (Alaa, 5 March): acknowledged the claim in writing — "I have uploaded the receipt to our relevant team to apply your refund... 7–10 working days to reach your Booking.com Wallet." Third agent (Zeyad, 2 April): copy-pasted Alaa's message word for word. Same "midnight confusion" line. Same 7–10 days promise. My escalation was clearly not read. Today: 2.5 months after Alaa confirmed the refund. Zero payment. Zero update. Zero accountability. This isn't a dispute about whether I'm owed money — Booking's own agent confirmed I am. It's a company stalling on a claim it has already accepted internally, hoping the customer gives up. Case IDs: 8224937, 8381806. Booking ref: 216218874.

review_title: Booking.com is colluding with rogue hosts to exploit customers! SECOND price error scam in one week!
review_text: I am absolutely appalled by Booking.com's complete disregard for consumer rights. This is the SECOND time in just one week that my confirmed and fully paid reservation has faced malicious price manipulation on this platform. I successfully booked a property, completed the payment, and received an official, legally binding confirmation from Booking.com. The reservation was entirely FIRM. However, the host later regretted listing the price too low and tried to force a cancellation, which I firmly refused because a confirmed booking constitutes a binding contract. Instead of standing up for the consumer and enforcing their own platform policies, Booking.com support agent Rob actively stepped in to act as an accomplice for this rogue property. Rob sent me an official email trying to pressure me into accepting a ridiculous "pricing adjustment," demanding my confirmation to pay an astronomical total of $1,200 CAD! Is this even legal?! This is a textbook "bait-and-switch" scam. Booking.com is blatantly violating consumer protection laws by allowing properties to lure travelers in with low rates, and then using their own customer service agents as leverage to squeeze more money out of customers once they are locked in! I demand a formal investigation into agent Rob’s handling of this case and immediate intervention from Booking.com's senior compliance team. I will NOT pay a single penny of this unauthorized price hike. If this is not resolved according to consumer laws, I will escalate this entire thread and evidence to international travel watchdogs and formal regulatory bodies.
