The complimentary taxi ride did not appear on the confirmation. After several attempts to contact the company - made very difficult through sloppy AI links and messaging - I was finally told the following: After carefully reviewing your reservation, we can confirm that a free taxi service was indeed offered. However, we regret to inform you that, as per the applicable terms and conditions, this benefit is currently not eligible to be availed. The amount or criteria required to qualify for this service does not meet the necessary threshold outlined in the policy. This was literally false advertising. I have used Booking.com many times over the years, but I will never use them again. Disgusting and dishonest service.

review_title: Last minute cancellation, broken promises, and zero accountability
review_text: I booked accommodation in Edinburgh over a month in advance through Booking.com. Throughout that entire month, the property never collected payment despite my repeated attempts to contact both the property and Booking.com to resolve this. I have full records of every contact attempt. Less than one week before my stay, the property cancelled my booking without warning. Two days prior to this, a Booking.com representative had explicitly assured me the booking would not be cancelled at this stage, and also committed to providing either compensation or alternative accommodation. Neither promise was kept. I was forced to find and book alternative accommodation at short notice at a significantly higher cost. My bank statements confirm no payment was ever attempted by the property. I also successfully booked the replacement accommodation using the exact same card immediately afterwards, proving there was never any issue on my end. Booking.com has repeatedly dismissed my compensation claim, blaming a "payment error" despite being unable to provide any evidence of an attempted transaction. They have ignored the broken promises made by their own staff, ignored the call recordings that would corroborate my account, and ignored the fact that even if a payment issue existed, the property had over a month to resolve it before resorting to a last-minute cancellation.

review_title: Sold Premium, delivered Standard - closed complaint without reviewing evidence
review_text: Booking.com sold me a Premium category car (Volvo S60 or similar, booking ref. 795242733) for a rental through Europcar at Tbilisi Airport. At pickup at 00:30 AM, Europcar gave me a Hyundai Sonata instead — a car that does not appear in Europcar's own Premium fleet list at any level — and refused to hand over the Volvo S90 that was physically present at the station, without additional payment. This was a forced upsell, not unavailability. The car delivered also had a yellow warning light on the dashboard immediately upon leaving the airport. I was about to drive high-altitude mountain roads in the Georgian Caucasus in snow conditions. I contacted Booking.com that same morning. One agent (Olethokuhle) acknowledged in writing that receiving a car outside the booked category is "unacceptable" and that the warning light raises "valid safety concerns" — and then told me to file a complaint after the rental ends. Five different agents gave me the same non-answer. The most telling detail: while Europcar told me on the phone they had "no Volvos available," I searched Booking.com's own platform at that exact moment and found Europcar Tbilisi actively advertising Volvo S90, XC60, XC90 at the airport and Volvo S60 at the downtown branch for that same week. The cars existed — they were just being withheld from me as an existing customer to sell to new bookings at full price. After I returned the car, I filed a formal case. Booking.com's Aftercare team closed it on 13 May 2026, accepting Europcar's claim that the Hyundai Sonata was "a complimentary upgrade." No reference to the evidence I provided. No acknowledgement of the warning light. Case closed. This is a clear pattern of supplier misconduct that Booking.com actively enabled by accepting the supplier's version without checking their own platform listings.

review_title: I rarely leave negative reviews
review_text: I rarely leave negative reviews, but my recent experience with Booking.com has honestly been one of the most frustrating customer service experiences I’ve had. My original accommodation booking was cancelled due to a disruption on Booking.com’s side, not mine. Because of this, I had to urgently arrange alternative accommodation and pay additional costs out of my own pocket. What followed was over a month of: * repeated follow-ups, * delayed responses, * agents confusing my case with unrelated matters, * requests to resubmit documents multiple times, * and inconsistent information from different customer service representatives. I was initially informed that the reimbursement for the price difference would be processed within 12–17 days after submission of my invoice. Instead, I spent weeks chasing updates and correcting misunderstandings regarding my case. Eventually, the reimbursement was issued — but not as an actual refund to my original payment method. Instead, Booking.com converted the amount into “Travel Credits” without asking for my consent or preference beforehand. This is where my biggest issue lies. The additional costs I incurred were paid using real money from my personal account due to a problem caused by Booking.com. I never agreed to receive the reimbursement in credits tied to future use of the platform. To make matters worse, these travel credits are barely usable for the kinds of bookings available to me in my country, and many listings do not even accept them. What disappointed me most was not just the inconvenience itself, but the lack of flexibility, the poor communication, and the feeling that customer concerns were secondary to internal policy. I remained respectful and cooperative throughout the process, but unfortunately the overall experience has left me with very little confidence in using Booking.com again.

It sends the message that even when a guest’s safety and comfort are compromised, Booking.com is willing to treat it as a minor inconvenience. A platform of this size should uphold higher standards, especially when the issues involve safety, hygiene, and professional misconduct. Instead, the response I received was dismissive and completely disproportionate to the situation. Booking.com needs to take these cases seriously. This level of support is far below what guests should expect.

When I finally reached the correct department, I was repeatedly told to call a hotline, despite explaining multiple times that I was unable to make international phone calls while travelling abroad. No meaningful written support was provided. The customer service experience was chaotic, uncoordinated, and highly frustrating. I spent a large amount of time trying to resolve a relatively straightforward issue, without any real help from Booking.com. In the end, I had to manage the situation myself directly with the airline. Very disappointing experience, especially for a company of this size.

review_title: Stuck not being able to access flights booked in January!
review_text: Booked Wizz Air flights through Booking.com and it has been an absolute nightmare trying to manage the booking. I’ve been incorrectly redirected to accommodation support, told about “unconfirmed bookings” despite the flights being confirmed for months, and advised to call international numbers at my own expense to resolve a problem caused by their booking system. It has been incredibly stressful and time-consuming trying to get a simple issue resolved, with no clear way to communicate directly with somebody from the Flights department who actually understands the problem. I will never book flights through Booking.com again. Completely unacceptable customer service and support.

review_text: I've booked rooms and flights on booking.com. There room bookings have been fairly smooth, and for that I would give 3 starts. But for the flights, this is a big warning. review_title: Booking.com Car Rental: Beware of the Real Cost at Pickup
review_text: In April 2026, I rented a car for three days through Booking.com. The advertised total price was $268.86 (approximately), including taxes, fees, and extra charges. However, upon arrival at the rental company’s desk, I was required to pay $490.11, which is $221.68 more than the advertised price. Bottom line: DΟ ΝΟΤ rely solely on the advertised prices for rental cars on Booking.com. In my experience, you may end up paying substantially more at the counter.

review_title: Lists untrustworthy properties
review_text: They list a lot of properties in London who you can’t trust. Three of them cancelled my reservation last minute. Two of them lied saying I was a no show and kept my money. I had to waste a lot of time phoning customer service to sort it all out

review_title: Booking.com supports substandard…
review_text: Booking.com supports substandard housing and fails its customers ​ ​I am extremely disappointed with the lack of support and accountability from Booking.com. I stayed 19 nights at The Manor Residence in Kuala Lumpur under unacceptable conditions. The apartment was filthy, I found cockroaches in the unit, and both the bed sheets and mattresses were heavily stained. ​The situation was made unbearable by constant construction noise starting as early as 7:00 AM. This was not just a minor annoyance; I work online and my two teenagers were attending online classes. The noise made it impossible for any of us to work or study properly. Furthermore, the swimming pool, which was a key reason for our booking, was closed for renovations during the entire stay without any prior notice. ​Despite reporting these issues with evidence from day one, Booking.com acted as an accomplice to the host. They refused any relocation or fair refund, offering only a derisory compensation of 280 MYR. This is insulting considering the total price paid and the severe impact on my family’s work and education. Booking.com clearly prioritizes its commissions over the safety and well-being of families. I strongly advise travelers to be cautious, as their customer service offers no real protection when things go wrong.

review_title: Unacceptable Limitation Resulting in Overcharged Taxes
review_text: I booked accommodation for myself and two guests through Booking.com. My guests stayed for 12 nights, while I stayed for 19 nights. In many countries this wouldn’t be an issue, but in Mauritius, taxes are charged per guest per night. As a result, I am now facing a tax bill that is higher than it should be. Unfortunately, Booking.com does not allow either the customer or the host to adjust this critical information once the booking is made. I contacted them multiple times before my stay ended and was assured they had reached out to the host to confirm the correct details. However, the host later confirmed that they had received no communication at all. When I called customer service, I was told there is nothing they can do within their system to reflect the different lengths of stay for each guest. This is extremely disappointing, especially for such a significant issue. I have been using Booking.com for nearly two years. While I would have rated them one star for this experience, I have received helpful support in other situations. The message I received — “Changing the dates of your stay isn’t possible” — is simply not good enough. It is unacceptable that they cannot even add a note to the booking to clarify the actual stay details. This would at least allow local authorities to correctly assess the number of nights for each guest. Overall, this reflects a serious limitation in their system that needs urgent attention.

review_title: Unclear handling of complaint and compensation
review_text: I rarely write reviews, but this experience with Booking.com requires attention. We booked a family holiday in Greece for 4 people, based on a listing that clearly indicated suitable accommodation for four guests. Upon arrival, we were immediately told that we would not fit, despite the fact that all family members and ages had been correctly declared during the booking process. The apartment was significantly smaller than described, and the sleeping arrangements were inadequate. We were asked to wait two days for an alternative, which turned out to be essentially the same. A folding bed was eventually provided, but it was unstable and not appropriate. As a result, one of my children had to leave on the third day, and the rest of the family left on the seventh day, although the booking was for ten days. The most concerning part, however, is how this was handled. Booking.com stated that 84 EUR was provided as compensation, yet this amount appears in my Wallet as “reward you earned from your stay,” which raises a serious question about whether any actual complaint-related compensation was issued at all. I have been trying to resolve this issue for approximately 9 months without receiving a clear and consistent answer. It is also concerning that the accommodation continues to be listed and operate on the platform without any visible consequences, despite the issues described. Beyond the financial aspect, this situation had a significant impact on our family holiday, which was particularly important to us. Experiences like this create uncertainty about how such cases are handled and whether customers can rely on the platform when issues arise.

review_title: Terrible and dishonest online service
review_text: Booked a flight to Japan with them last year for a holiday this year in April.  The airline (Air Asiana) cancelled one of our flights.  Booking.com via gotogate.com, sent an email saying that our flight was cancelled. After I got online and chatted with them online, they recommended getting a refund and rebooking.  But with everything happening right now, prices have skyrocketed.  I called Air Asiana and they said that there was no need to get a refund, just get our flight changed.  They even gave me the alternative flight.  When I got back online with booking.com, they said they couldnt see that flight.  One more call with air Asiana, they gave me the information, told me that because I booked with booking.com, it was booking.com who had the authority to change the flight and they gave me the flight details, and even their email to give to booking.com to call them so they can help them get it sorted.  I was told by booking.com, firstly, that they couldnt see the flight, and next, that the flight was all booked out, depite Air Asiana explicitly telling me that there were seats available!  They then kept telling me that only Air Asiana could change the flight, and outright refused to email them for help!  It only got sorted after we told them we would be taking this to fair trade.  We ended up just calling the booking.com help line, and finally got the flight changed.  I gave them 2 stars because they eventually changed it, but this was literally after hours of chatting online.  I definitely do not recommend using them,as it seemed like the online chat team (spoke to multiple agents too) couldn't be bothered to do what was necessary to change our flights, and it was a massive headache.  Do yourself a favour and just book via the airlines themselves

review_title: Hope nobody else needs to use Booking.com Customer's Service
review_text: Booked a hotel that included dinner, and once I got there, they told me it was not served on weekends, to contact Booking.com where I made the reservation to get the difference back. I contacted Booking.com the very same day, they said all was fine. It has been 3 weeks that I've been spending hours on the telephone to get the 27 euros back, and the only answer I get is that the hotel doesn't reply to their messages. Anyone who calls to the hotel gets the answer that no dinner is provided on weekends, it is really frustrating that just to get what you paid for and such a small refund, you have to go under so much stress.

review_title: No customer service
review_text: No customer service. Properties are misadvertised and there is no direct communication with Booking.com to resolve issue.

review_title: The site gives false info, and customer service is not helpful
review_text: The experience of making my booking was very easy, and there were a lot of options when it came to filtering the results to help me find flights and hotels. However, I had a lot of trouble when it came to making changes. I needed to change the return flight for a journey I'd booked, and the only way to change or cancel a lot of bookings on booking.com is to contact customer service. I don't mind doing that, but this was at the time when the situation in the Middle East was just starting, and customer service was made uncontactable during that time. I absolutely appreciate that they needed to put their resources towards short-notice changes and cancellations caused by that, and my flight was hardly the biggest issue caused by the war, but this effectively meant that booking.com had made changes and cancellations impossible for an undetermined period of time. My flight was about three weeks away at that point so I kept checking back to see if I could contact them, but in the end I went ahead and booked the new flight because the prices were going up each day. The information given for my initial flight booking was that it was refundable with a fee, so my plan was to cancel the first one as soon as I could get through to someone, as per the website's guidance. Finally I was able to speak with an agent a few days before my flight. I explained the situation and they told me that I could only cancel after the outbound flight had departed, as the one I wanted to cancel was the return. I then got in touch with them again after the outbound flight, and at this point was told that the booking was non-refundable. I submitted a complaint but the responses from customer service have been pretty unhelpful, as the impression they seem to be under is that I don't understand that they have to follow the policies of each airline. I absolutely understand that, and that was never in question: my complaint was about the fact that the information displayed on their website was false, and the only method of making changes to bookings, or even getting correct info, was blocked. I know the money I've lost on the flights is nothing to a company like them but it's a decent amount for me, and the response has been quite terrible. I've used this site in the past with no problems but I'll be avoiding it from now on, as I know that I cannot trust the information given.

review_title: Last 2 bookings were negative…
review_text: Last 2 bookings were negative experiences. 1st, was borderline lying in property description, Booking.com customer services not helpful with complaint. 2nd, a mistake was made during booking a night at a hotel in Skegness (lets just say its on this site with very poor reviews..) and had to request cancellation, booking was live for matter of minutes, hotel agrèed cancellation and kept all the money. review_title: Repeated extra check-in work defeats the purpose of using Booking
review_text: I have used Booking for years, but I am increasingly frustrated by the growing amount of extra work shifted onto guests. A major issue is that some properties now require extensive external check-in forms after booking, even though all guest data is already provided through Booking. In one case, I spent around 60 minutes completing a separate form, including PDF document uploads and additional calls to clarify unclear instructions. For a one-night stay for two people, this is disproportionate. What I find particularly problematic is that this is often only disclosed after payment, not transparently before booking. If I have to re-enter sensitive personal data with each property, complete extra check-in administration, and still Booking takes a commission, I seriously question the value of using the platform. Because of this, I am increasingly avoiding Booking and choosing to book directly with accommodations I find via Google Maps to avoid duplicate work. Booking should simplify travel, not create more administrative burden for guests.

review_title: Booking.com does not provide good customer support
review_text: I had to cancel my booking for this hotel (Art & Hotel Treviolo) because the situation was so ridiculous. The hotel was affordable, had breakfast and the rooms had good reviews. The issue was that on the hotel website and on Booking.com, it says they have a "shuttle bus" and I was expecting to pay no more than 30 euros total for the service (they are usually cheaper than that). Instead, this turned out to be a lie and there is no shuttle bus service. You book a taxi which is more expensive than the room itself. While there are technically other ways to get to the hotel, this was a major selling point for me and it just was just false advertising. I then sent an email and the hotel refused to acknowledge this mistake, and also refused to give a refund despite the false advertising. Booking.com has been very unhelpful in resolving this issue as as of yet they have not updated the advertising of the hotel on their own website, so others may fall for this trap. I don't recommend Booking.com and I am yet to receive a refund. I have got screenshots as proof.

review_title: Booking.com
review_text: Title: Booking cancelled after reassurance – left £600 out of pocket We had a very disappointing experience with Booking.com. We booked Hôtel du Square d’Anvers in Paris (booking 6137212901). Shortly after booking, we received suspicious messages requesting payment details via external links. We reported this to Booking.com on 26 March. Their customer service team reassured us that: - our booking was secure - no further action was required We relied on this reassurance in good faith and proceeded to book non-refundable flights. However, on 9 April, we were informed that the hotel would not honour the booking and it was cancelled. We are now facing around £600 in additional costs for equivalent accommodation. Despite clearly explaining that we relied on Booking.com’s advice, their response has simply been to say they cannot assist because the property is no longer working with them. This completely ignores the fact that we acted based on their reassurance. We understand that issues can arise with properties, but in this case we raised a security concern, followed guidance, and are now significantly out of pocket as a result. We would have expected Booking.com to take some responsibility and offer a goodwill contribution in these circumstances. Very disappointing handling of what should have been a straightforward case.

review_title: Automation gone mad
review_text: Automation gone mad. Never will I book via Booking.com with its constant demand for booking numbers, confirmation codes and ID etc. Next time I will book a hotel with real people who take a booking and talk to you.

review_text: Booked 3 nights stay at hotel in Liverpool the deal was pay in advance. That's fine.  A good rate. review_text: Most of my bookings have been OK, but the website is awful for such a big company and they simply don't do customer service (which should be illegal). It's a waste of time. If you absolutely don't want to contact their customer services, but want to waste an hour and take 5 years off your life, click their "Contact customer services" button.  It's a hateful way to treat paying customers.

review_title: Booking the hotel and transfer is all…
review_text: Booking the hotel and transfer is all quite easy - but if there are problems it’s not easy to sort out. review_title: Goodbye Booking.com
review_text: Booking.com is good for research, finding options and convenience of transactions. That said, the prices aren't any better than the hotel/rental company/attraction's own websites and using Booking prevents you from receiving any customer service from the services you're using. Booking.com's own customer service is a big ZERO, and even if you max out the rewards status, there is zero benefit. Prices, perks, and customer service is all the same as if you have no rewards status. I used them for international, and USA domestic hotels, vehicle rental and attractions. After several ridiculous experiences, I've found better service and pricing by going directly with the various service providers. Goodbye Booking.com. Neither of us will miss the other.

review_title: We stayed in an apartment in Beaune
review_text: We stayed in an apartment in Beaune, France this past month.  We had multiple issues, no working internet, hot water turned off so a very cool shower.  The worst was a gas leak which we reported to the owner-we did not hear back for several hours so we called Booking for help.  They said they would get back to us in 4 hours.  We received an email which said they had spoken to the owner of the apartment and the owner would fix the gas leak (which they did after 24 hours) but we never did have internet during our 4 night stay.  Booking said the apartment owner would not give any restitution or cancel the booking.  It seems that they stand up for the apartment owners and not the people who are paying for the apartment.  This will be the last apartment I rent from Booking. Air BNB service is far superior in customer care.

review_title: I am beyond disappointed with…booking.com and NU Car rentals
review_text: Had the worst experience with booking.com and NU Car rentals. THEY STOLE MY MONEY! After waiting for a shuttle for 30 minutes, we were dropped off 3 blocks away from the rental office. I am beyond disappointed with both NU Car rental and Booking.com!!

review_title: Booked a hotel through Booking.com
review_text: Booked a hotel through Booking.com — or should I say Booking.conartist. They’re more than happy to list questionable hotels, take your money, and then completely wash their hands of it when things go wrong. When I raised a complaint, the response was basically: “you should’ve read the reviews better.” So let me get this straight — they profit from listing poor-quality properties but take zero responsibility for what they promote? That’s not a platform you can trust, that’s just passing the buck. If you’re using them, be warned: once they’ve got your money, you’re on your own.

review_title: I had a very disappointing experience…
review_text: I had a very disappointing experience with Booking.com’s Price Match policy. I booked a hotel at a significantly higher price, only to later find the same room available for much less. I submitted a price match request while the lower rate was still available and provided all required evidence, including screenshots and links. What followed was a lengthy and frustrating process involving multiple emails and two phone calls, where I repeatedly had to explain the same situation. The request was initially declined based on a technicality regarding “room type,” despite my booking not specifying any view and the room I was ultimately given having no view at all. After considerable effort, the claim was eventually approved. However, despite clearly requesting a refund to my original payment method, the difference was issued only as travel credit, which is not practical for me to use. Overall, the process was unnecessarily complicated, time-consuming, and lacked transparency. While the claim was eventually acknowledged, the experience has significantly reduced my confidence in using Booking.com in the future. I would strongly advise others to carefully review the terms of the Price Match policy and consider booking directly with hotels where possible.

review_title: Qantas airlines and nonstop long haul.
review_text: Qantas airlines are making a big deal about being able to fly nonstop from Australia to/from Europe. I recently did one of these flights - Perth to Paris non stop in just on 18 hours. The seats were flexible economy and cost a great deal due to the conflict in the Middle East. About 200% on the same flights prior to Feb 28. The problem started when Qantas, for operational reasons, decided to not load around 30 passengers checked baggage. It stayed in Perth. So on arrival in Paris about a half dozen names were called but eventually all those with missing baggage had to queue and wait to fill in details with just one person to respond. It took while over 90 minutes. None of this was necessary as Qantas knew which bags were not loaded. No apology. No compensation for failing to bring all these bags - not because of human error, but because the plane couldn’t do the distance with that load. My bag turned 3 days later. I had to go to the airport from the city to get it. I had to buy clothing because the temperatures were 4-11c and carry on bags means not much comes with you. Five weeks later, I’m still waiting for Qantas to respond. Pathetic The long haul claim is nonsense - I’ve heard this is a common experience

review_title: Fake listings, false reassurances, and ZERO customer protection
review_text: I am writing this to warn others about the absolute lack of safety and customer protection on Booking.com. I booked an apartment in Rome (San Lorenzo Home) for my group of friends, and it turned out to be a complete scam. What makes this situation truly unacceptable is that I was suspicious of the payment method requested by the host (a direct bank transfer to their IBAN via a link). I explicitly contacted Booking.com customer service BEFORE making the payment to ask if it was safe. They reassured me in writing that it was a legitimate and safe procedure. Trusting their supposed authority, I paid. After 3 weeks, the "host" canceled the reservation and disappeared. It is utterly unacceptable that a massive, supposedly secure platform like Booking.com allows fake, fraudulent listings to be published and remain active. People use this website specifically to avoid being scammed, yet they clearly do not vet their hosts properly. But the worst part is how they handled the aftermath. While I eventually managed to force a refund for the original amount, finding a new accommodation so close to our travel dates was obviously much more expensive. Despite the fact that I was scammed on THEIR site, and only paid because THEIR customer service told me to, they blatantly refused to cover the €100 price difference for a relocation. They hid behind a ridiculous internal policy about check-in dates to wash their hands of the problem. They allowed a scammer on their site, gave me false reassurances, and when the worst happened, they left me and my friends stranded, forcing us to pay out of pocket for their mistake. I have completely lost trust in Booking.com. If you encounter a scam on their site, do not expect them to help you with the extra costs or take any real responsibility. Extremely unprofessional. Book elsewhere.

review_title: Unacceptable  customer service

Booking.com only offered a minimal compensation of 11.72 EUR in travel credits. This does not reflect the seriousness of the issue or the impact on my safety and overall travel experience. I expected Booking.com to properly support customers when accommodations are not as described, but in this case the response was inadequate and dismissive. Very disappointing experience.

review_title: Censorship of scam-related feedback and fundamentally broken customer support
review_text: I’ve used Booking.com for many years without issue and generally haven’t had a problem with the platform. However, this is the first time I’ve needed to engage with customer service or had a review blocked after raising a concern, and the experience has been concerning. I received multiple scam messages after making a booking through Booking.com, and when I included this in my review to inform other travelers, the review was ultimately rejected without explanation. This is particularly notable because an earlier version of my review — which did not mention the scam messages — was published almost immediately. The only substantive difference was the inclusion of this information, which suggests that content relating to potential fraud or scams may be selectively withheld. I followed up multiple times over several days with Booking.com customer service through their app, not simply to have the review published, but because I believed this was important information for both the platform and the property to be aware of and address. I had also raised this with the property directly on more than one occasion and received no meaningful response, which further reinforced my view that the issue was not being taken seriously. The support experience was fragmented, poorly handled, and showed no clear ownership of the case. I was given contradictory information at different points — that the review was under review, approved, rejected, and then again still under verification — with no coherent handling of the case. At no point was a specific reason provided for the rejection, despite repeated requests. Rather than addressing the reported issue or providing guidance on how such incidents should be handled, the focus appeared to be on preventing the content from being published. Based on broader customer feedback, this does not appear to be an isolated case, particularly in relation to inconsistent communication and lack of accountability in customer support. This raises broader questions about how Booking.com handles fraud and scam-related concerns on its platform, as well as the transparency and integrity of its review moderation process. All customers should expect clear communication and accountability in situations like this. The fact that this was my experience even as a Genius Level 3 customer is particularly telling.

review_title: Disappointing handling  of serious accommodation issue
review_text: I have generally had positive experiences with Booking.com in the past, which is why this situation has been particularly disappointing. I booked and paid £265 for a 5-night stay. From the first evening, I encountered cockroaches in the apartment, including multiple live insects and droppings in cupboards, which clearly indicated an infestation rather than an isolated issue. I reported this during my stay. The host acknowledged the issue and mentioned that bait had already been placed, suggesting prior awareness. However, no effective action was taken in a timely manner. I was even asked to use insecticide and place bait myself, which is not appropriate for a guest. A cleaner was said to attend, but there was no visible improvement. My request to be moved to another apartment was refused, and only on the final evening was a brief spray carried out, which did not resolve the issue. Despite providing evidence, Booking.com’s handling of the case was disappointing. The host denied responsibility and made inaccurate claims, yet was still allowed to offer only €50 compensation. Booking.com then offered a €25 credit, which does not reflect the severity of the issue or the amount paid. I remained in the property only due to lack of alternative accommodation, not because the conditions were acceptable. The situation also impacted my sleep and caused discomfort during the stay. I would have expected stronger support and accountability in a case like this. While I have had good experiences previously, this has reduced my confidence in how serious issues are handled.

review_title: I made a car rental reservation through…
review_text: I made a car rental reservation through Booking.com, relying on the information clearly presented on their website regarding included and excluded charges. At the rental desk (Avis Zagreb Airport), I was asked to sign a document on a tablet very quickly, without proper explanation and without being given sufficient time to review it. Due to my limited English proficiency, I reasonably believed this was a standard vehicle pick-up procedure, not the purchase of additional services. After the rental was completed, I discovered that approximately 544 USD had been charged to my card. What is particularly concerning is that this charge was processed on the day I returned the vehicle, which prevented me from questioning it at the counter. I contacted Avis, but their response was simply that the charges were valid because I signed the agreement. This does not reflect the reality of how that signature was obtained. I also contacted Booking.com, as the reservation was made through their platform. Customers trust the accuracy and transparency of the information provided there. However, I did not receive a satisfactory resolution. This experience raises serious concerns about transparency and sales practices, especially for international customers facing language barriers. I hope this issue will be reviewed and resolved fairly.

review_title: Mirante Porto Galinhas beira-mar on booking.com
review_text: We have used Booking.com for many years and usually had good experiences. However, our recent stay booked through the platform was very disappointing in terms of customer support. We stayed in an apartment in Porto de Galinhas (Brazil) from 17–23 December 2025. During the entire stay there were major construction works both inside the building and on the adjacent property, starting every day around 7:00 a.m.. The noise (hammering, drilling, machinery) made it impossible to rest properly. In addition, the private terrace and pool were not usable due to construction debris, dust and dirt. These issues were not communicated prior to booking or before arrival. We contacted both the host and Booking.com and provided documentation. Despite this, Booking.com stated that they are only an intermediary and offered only a very small goodwill amount (around 5% of the total price), which is not proportionate to the severity of the issues. We made several attempts to resolve the situation and even set a deadline, but no fair solution was offered. While we understand that Booking.com is a platform, we would expect stronger support in cases where the accommodation clearly does not match the description and significantly affects the stay. Overall, this experience has reduced our trust in the platform.

review_title: I’ve stayed at Marriott hotels several…
review_text: I’ve stayed at Marriott hotels several times before and have always had pleasant experiences, which makes this visit particularly disappointing. On this occasion, the cleanliness was completely unacceptable. I saw cockroaches in the food area and flies hovering around the food, which is shocking for a hotel that promotes high standards and charges premium prices. This is not a minor issue—it’s a serious hygiene concern that immediately put me off eating. What made matters worse was the response from staff. I raised the issue at the time, but it didn’t feel like it was taken seriously. There was no proper acknowledgment, no sincere apology, and no reassurance that anything would be done. There was also no mention of pest control or any immediate corrective action, which only added to my frustration. As a result, I completely lost my appetite and any confidence in the food hygiene standards. Cleanliness is something I always prioritise when choosing a hotel, especially one with such a strong reputation, and this experience fell far below expectations. Overall, I’m extremely disappointed and quite frankly appalled. This is not the level of service or hygiene I expect, and it has definitely made me reconsider staying here again.

review_title: Loyal Genius Level 3 Member Seeking Help, Flight Flexibility, During Family Travel Crisis
review_text: I am a Genius Level 3 Plus member and a long-time, loyal Booking.com customer. I truly value the platform and use it almost exclusively for hotel reservations worldwide, where my experiences have consistently been excellent. This was my first time booking flights through Booking.com, and unfortunately it has been extremely challenging and questions the value of our partnership. This booking involves five flights total, two of which were with British Airways (non-refundable economy). Shortly after booking and beginning travel, we encountered serious unforeseen family challenges while traveling with our two very young children — a 10-month-old and a 2-year-old. The reality of multi-leg travel with children this young quickly became overwhelming. Both children struggled significantly being away from home, out of routine, overtired, and unsettled. What was intended to be manageable family travel became physically and emotionally exhausting, and continuing the itinerary raised real concerns about their well-being. So i appreciate the flexibility with the hotels as Booking.com is accommodating/understanding. But the airline solutions are much more challenging. I want to be very clear: I understand airline fare rules and am not demanding full refunds w no recourse. What I am seeking is reasonable flexibility and advocacy — such as flight credits, a one-time compassionate or courtesy exception, or even a refund with the clear understanding that I would rebook more expensive, last-minute tickets through Booking.com at the same time (we still need to get home!). I am actively trying to continue booking and partnering with Booking.com and was simply hoping for support during a legitimate family hardship. Following Booking.com’s direction, I contacted the airlines directly. Each airline advised that because the tickets were issued for more than 24hrs through Booking.com, only Booking.com can submit changes or exception requests. A British Airways booking agent explicitly confirmed that notes were placed in both the airline reservation and the Booking.com reservation and advised that Booking.com should contact the British Airways trade line. The airline agent stated clearly that “Booking.com will understand what this means.” However, when I returned to Booking.com, I was told that they would not submit the request to their internal flights team and would not contact the airline trade line unless the airline contacted them directly — something British Airways confirmed they do not do for OTA-issued tickets. This leaves customers like myself in an impossible position with no clear path forward. The airlines are happy to accommodate but their hands are tied behind their backs. Compounding this, I spent over one hour attempting to work with a third Booking.com agent (3+ hrs total). During that call, the agent refused to contact the airline, refused to escalate the case to a supervisor, and repeatedly relied on scripted responses with no apparent willingness to help. The interaction felt robotic and stone-faced, with no human empathy shown despite the family circumstances. The only option mentioned was a possible refund of taxes, with no discussion of credits, rebooking options after, or escalation. As a top-tier customer, I expected clear ownership of my case, proper escalation with the airline, and transparent communication — to find a needed compromise like the airlines were willing to do if i booked directly with them. Instead, the experience has been fragmented, circular, and deeply discouraging, especially during an already difficult situation involving two very young children. I am sharing this publicly in hopes of connecting with a senior customer care or flights escalation team who can review this case properly. I genuinely want to continue using Booking.com — including for flights — but this experience has highlighted a serious gap compared to the otherwise excellent hotel service I’ve relied on for years. Multiple Booking reference available upon request and snapshots of the conversations with Booking Agent is possible.

review_title: Dishonest, Fine till you need customer service assistance
review_text: I’ve been a loyal Booking.com customer for years and have always used the platform to arrange both flights and hotels without any issues. Unfortunately, this recent experience has been incredibly frustrating and has led me to rethink using their services in the future. I booked flights to Morocco for September and had to cancel due to personal reasons. At the time of cancellation, the app clearly displayed a refund amount, which I was satisfied with, so I proceeded. A week later, I received significantly less than what was displayed. I immediately contacted customer service (GoToGate) through both chat and phone. I was assured that the remaining amount would be refunded within a few days. This turned into weeks of chasing, only to eventually be informed—six weeks later—that the initial (lower) refund was the correct amount due to “airline policy.” This contradicts both the refund amount shown in the app at the time of cancellation and messages from agents confirming I would receive the rest. Despite providing screenshots and repeatedly contacting customer service by phone and email—on a weekly basis—I keep receiving the same vague responses: “Just wait a few more days; the remaining amount will be paid.” It has now been repeatedly delayed, with no resolution. If Booking.com displays a refund amount upon cancellation, that amount should be honoured. It’s misleading and unacceptable to show one figure and then pay significantly less without explanation. The lack of transparency and accountability, along with the constant runaround from customer service, has been extremely disappointing. I hope this issue is finally resolved, but this experience has completely undermined my trust in Booking.com. EDIT April 2026 I emailed someone high up at the company, and they pushed my complaint through to their senior specialist from their customer service team and my issue has since then been RESOLVED. If only this was progressed in this manner earlier I would’ve saved a lot of time, but it’s done and that’s the main thing.

review_title: Opinion of an Agency Advertising Multiple Apartments and Villas on Booking.com
review_text: Advantages The Booking.com app and company policy are extremely user-friendly. It is a very powerful distribution channel, essential to filling the booking calendars of our properties. The app contains all the necessary information for communication with hosts and for check-in procedures. Disadvantages The Extranet for hosts is not very transparent and not user-friendly. When uploading a new property, the Extranet only guides the user partially through the process, then prompts premature publication. This often results in unwanted reservations, since only one reference price has been entered and restrictions or policies have not yet been properly set. There is a high risk of double bookings if Booking.com is not fully synchronized with a property’s PMS. The most serious issue, however, is that many Booking.com users reserve multiple properties for the same travel dates, and only decide the day before the free cancellation period ends which one to keep, cancelling the others. This practice creates uncovered gaps in calendars and results in financial losses for hosts. Advice for Booking.com Your platform is very clever and effective in many respects. However, we strongly recommend introducing a mechanism that makes it more difficult—or ideally impossible—for the same guest to reserve multiple properties for identical travel dates. Such a change would not only protect hosts and agencies from unnecessary risk but would also benefit Booking.com itself. As it stands, many hosts restrict their availability on your platform to last-minute bookings only, precisely because of this issue. Addressing it would encourage greater trust and broader availability from your partners.

review_title: I see little real benefit in using Booking.com. Prices are often higher than booking directly with the hotel, and my credit card information is unnecessarily shared with third parties
review_text: Booking a room via Booking.com is generally easy and straightforward. However, what I find absolutely unacceptable is that my credit card details are passed on directly to the hotels. In reality, the booking is handled by the hotel itself, which means I could just book directly without using Booking.com. On two occasions – in Thailand and in Corsica – I faced issues because the hotels were using outdated payment software without 3D Secure. As a result, I had to whitelist the hotels as “trusted merchants,” which is a serious security risk. The review system on Booking.com is also misleading. Compared to Google reviews, hotels receive much better ratings, since the score is largely based on factors such as location and staff friendliness. This means even if a hotel offered a mattress in a garage instead of a 5-star suite, the overall score could still look good. Another serious issue is the photo policy: hotels can upload pictures that are 5+ years old, showing freshly renovated rooms, while in reality the place might be in very poor condition today. Often, promotional pictures show suites, but the booked room has nothing to do with what is displayed. Booking.com should introduce strict checks to ensure photos are recent and accurately represent the room being booked. On the positive side, I once ended up in a tourist trap and Booking.com helped by canceling my reservation from the second day onwards, saving me from paying for 10 full days. Still, I see little real benefit in using Booking.com. Prices are often higher than booking directly with the hotel, and my credit card information is unnecessarily shared with third parties.

review_title: Booking .com Customer Service Experience
review_text: We booked well in advance several nights in different destinations around Scotland between August 5th and the 16th 2025 with Booking.com. On the 12th August we arrived in Nairn at the Clubhouse B&B to be told that we had no reservation. We showed our Booking.com confirmation of reservation and was told that the previous landlord had left several months earlier. The current landlord was very helpful and apologetic saying we were by no means the first guests to be in this situation. He gave us a Booking.com number to call and after some 25 minutes of listening to dreary music we spoke to a call handler. We attempted to listen to what he had to say but it sounded as if he was under water, couple this with a strong accent made understanding difficult. The jist of the conversation was that he would contact the landlord (in this case the previous landlord) and get back to us. It took a while but eventually he rang back suggesting we find another venue and offered a monatary gesture of good will (up to £40 approx) after we submitted an accommodation receipt. We looked for other B&B's in Nairn but as it was high season only a few very expensive places were available. By this time a couple of hours had passed...it was hot and we are in our seventies so we were pleased that the current landlord rallied to our cause and offered a room at  £233.88 for the night (cheaper than anything available on Booking.com) and we were able to stay in the property of our choice. We tried to email Booking.com but contact is strictly controlled. We finally worked out how to send off the invoice for our one nights stay in Nairn and received a refund of the original monies paid £133.88 with no accompanying email. However the difference was £100.00 No gesture of good will has been received. The failure of Booking.com to recognise the recurring issue with the previous landlord. The drawn out process of trying to contact Booking.com their incessant email requests for reviews, payments etc and their lack of communication on a customer service level has soured our experience. We are sure that for the most part the system works well but found that even with careful planning things can go wrong and this is where good customer service sets certain companies apart.

The room was next to the check‑in area, with very loud gates, and directly beside a main road. There were no proper curtains, allowing people outside to see inside. Your money is gone and nobody will help you. If you book here, purchase travel insurance and read every policy word by word. Because if anything goes wrong, you are completely on your own.

review_text: Very disappointing experience with this rental company. We booked our London accommodation from May 13th–18th back in February because we were travelling for work with a team of four people attending a coffee festival. We specifically chose a property close to the event venue with two bathrooms so the team could rest properly after long workdays. The day before our trip, after contacting them ourselves to confirm everything, we were suddenly informed that our reservation had been cancelled. We never received any proper notification beforehand. Even worse, weeks earlier we had received suspicious messages asking us to enter our card details through an external link or risk cancellation. After contacting Airbnb support, we were advised it looked like a scam attempt, so we froze our bank card for security. review_title: READ THIS BEFORE YOU USE AIRBNB
review_text: Booked 4 months ahead. Host canceled for more money. Airbnb's fix was a 50$ voucher. Reserved a property 3-4 months in advance for a holiday. The host canceled before the trip with a simple reason: they wanted to relist at a higher rate. Rebooking a similar place for the same dates now costs 1200$ more than what I had originally locked in. So the host canceled my booking, raised the price, and pocketed the spread. - He used the holiday as an opportunity. Airbnb's response to all of this was a 50$ gift voucher. That covers maybe 7 to 10 percent of the gap the host's behavior created. This is not a guest-protection policy. This is theater. If a host can cancel a confirmed reservation whenever the market shifts in their favor, and the platform's idea of accountability is a voucher worth a fraction of the damage, then 'confirmed booking' is just a placeholder the host can drop whenever it becomes profitable to drop it. Until Airbnb starts treating opportunistic host cancellations as a contract breach with real consequences, my advice to anyone planning a trip is simple: do not book anything you cannot afford to lose.

review_title: Airbnb protects hosts
review_text: Airbnb is there to protect hosts, not guests and their policies make that very clear. Hosts are given a 72-hour window to accept or decline refund or money requests, and in my experience the process gets dragged out long enough for guests to lose the right to even a partial refund. Listings also fail to disclose important details. In my case, the property was located in council housing/buildings, which would have been a complete deal breaker if it had been clearly stated beforehand. Once you discover something like that after arrival, you risk losing all of your money. Overall, this was an extremely bad experience. I would strongly advise people to avoid booking through Airbnb unless they are comfortable staying in a place that may not fully match the listing or the expectations created by it.

review_title: My booking was cancelled — but Airbnb made it right
review_text: My booking was cancelled due to a missed payment notification sent to an email I don't actively use, leaving me without accommodation in Nice just days before my trip. I had already paid €220 and was ready to pay the remaining €190 immediately. The host did not respond to Airbnb's attempts to contact him, and at first I was told no refund was possible. However, Airbnb's team came back to me, resolved the situation swiftly and made it right. That level of commitment is rare and genuinely impressive. I have since booked new accommodation through Airbnb and I am looking forward to my trip. This experience showed me that when things go wrong, Airbnb does stand behind its guests. A brand that truly cares. I will continue to recommend it. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

review_title: Genuinely one of the worst customer…
review_text: Genuinely one of the worst customer service and dispute resolution experiences I have dealt with from a major platform. After years of using Airbnb without issue, I was left dealing with a review implying dishonest conduct despite there being no evidence of theft, no missing property claim, no reimbursement request and no proof of any loss whatsoever. Property: Villa Lou Lia, Callian France The location of the items was provided immediately. After that, the host made no further allegation and pursued nothing further. Despite this, Airbnb still refused to remove or properly moderate the review and effectively confirmed they apply no meaningful evidential standard before allowing potentially defamatory implications to remain attached to a guest profile. That should concern every future guest using this platform. Airbnb appears entirely comfortable allowing unsupported allegations implying criminal or dishonest behaviour to remain publicly visible provided they are framed as part of a “host experience”. In practice, this means your reputation can be damaged permanently without evidence, without investigation and without accountability. The complaints process itself was equally poor: scripted responses, no transparency, no meaningful escalation and no indication that fairness or evidence played any real part in the decision-making process. For a company that markets itself around “trust”, the reality of how disputes are handled behind the scenes was extremely disappointing. I would strongly encourage future guests to consider whether they are comfortable using a platform where unsupported allegations can apparently be published and protected indefinitely regardless of the facts.

review_title: Airbnb Support Gave Conflicting Payment Information and Threatened Cancellation
review_text: I rented this place for 6 months and specifically clarified the payment schedule in advance. The rent is officially due on the 21st of each month, but Airbnb starts trying to charge you 10 DAYS earlier, which is already ridiculous for long-term rentals. Before booking, support clearly told me multiple times that I could safely pay between the 11th and 18th so the payment would arrive before the 21st. For two months everything worked exactly like that with no issues. Then suddenly on the 12th I received a threatening message saying I had to pay by TOMORROW or my reservation would be canceled. My pregnant wife saw this notification, panicked, and we literally had to go to the hospital because of the stress. Of course I paid immediately on the 12th, but what if I had no internet connection or simply didn’t see the message in time? Airbnb support responds like robots and completely ignores previous conversations. I even sent them screenshots where their own support agents confirmed the payment window until the 18th, but nobody cared. They just kept repeating that they “cannot change payment dates,” even though I never asked them to. Very stressful and extremely unprofessional experience for a long-term stay.

review_title: Seeking legal advice
review_text: I rarely leave negative reviews, but after almost a month of trying to resolve a disputed reimbursement charge with Airbnb, I feel I have little choice. The original stay itself was already deeply problematic long before the reimbursement dispute even began. From the outset, there were issues accessing the property properly, confusion around entry, and requests for additional payments outside the Airbnb platform in order to use parts of the house. During the stay, I repeatedly cut my foot on broken glass left embedded in a rug in the kitchen area — on multiple occasions. This alone was upsetting enough, but unfortunately it was only one of a long list of problems with the property and amenities. A number of features either did not function properly, were damaged, incomplete, or missing entirely. Examples included: - projectors displaying warning messages that their bulbs had exceeded their operational lifespan, - projector remotes missing entirely, making them extremely difficult to use, - promises that replacements would be sent which never materialised, - amenities advertised as luxury features but functioning poorly or not as expected, - and a general level of maintenance which did not reflect the premium nature of the listing price. Following the stay, I later discovered that if you search the property address independently online, there are also notably poor reviews associated with the address on other booking platforms,l, which suggests my experience may not have been isolated. Despite all of this, the situation later escalated into me being pursued for a reimbursement claim relating to a chair which: - I fundamentally dispute responsibility for, - do not believe justified the amount being demanded, - and which appears to have been valued at an amount wildly disproportionate to the actual item involved. What has shocked me most has been Airbnb’s handling of the dispute afterwards. For weeks, I have: - submitted information and appeals through the Resolution Centre, - requested meaningful escalation, - repeatedly asked to speak with somebody senior, - attempted to provide context and contradictory evidence, - and tried consistently to resolve matters calmly and cooperatively. Instead, I have found myself trapped in what feels like an endless administrative loop: - being redirected back into the same appeal process repeatedly, - receiving sympathetic but largely generic responses, - being offered calls that either never materialised or occurred at impractical hours for UK time, - and being told the matter was simultaneously “under review” while also effectively already decided. Most concerningly, I still have not been provided with: - a transparent explanation of how the reimbursement amount was calculated, - clear evidence supporting the valuation being claimed, - clarification as to why my evidence and wider context were disregarded, - or confirmation that the appeal process involved any genuinely independent review. I fully appreciate the importance of protecting hosts and processing legitimate claims fairly. However, fairness must also extend to guests — especially when serious concerns existed about the condition of the property itself. At present, the experience has left me feeling extremely disappointed, unsupported, and exhausted by what has felt far more like a procedural system than a genuinely transparent dispute resolution processes

When I challenged the listing, Vacasa defended it by saying the complex has beach access and that the balcony view was shown in the photos. That is a weak excuse. Had the listing been honest, I would have chosen a different condo in Myrtle Beach that was actually oceanfront. And Airbnb defended the listing telling me that it followed the Airbnb requirements.  Really, misleading listing follows Airbnb rules? review_title: “When Security Goes Too Far”
review_text: “When Security Goes Too Far” For several months, I have been trying to regain access to my Airbnb account after the option to log in via Facebook was removed. The problem is that the account was connected to a work email address and phone number that I no longer had access to after my employment ended abruptly. What frustrates me is that I have been able to prove that the account is mine through: government ID bank transfers and payouts previous bookings and trips official address registration documents rental contract connected to the property Despite this, I still have not regained access to my account. As a result, I am now losing more than 10 years of reviews and ratings, my entire history as a host/user, as well as professionally taken photos connected to my account. I have also tried, through a GDPR request, to at least retrieve my personal photos, but apparently Airbnb does not believe I even have the right to that. I understand the need for security and identity verification. However, when a company changes its login systems, there also needs to be a reasonable way for users to recover their accounts when their previous contact information is no longer available. In my case, the process has felt extremely rigid and practically impossible to resolve despite extensive documentation and proof of ownership. Surely it cannot be the intention that it should become practically impossible to regain access to your account when you are able to verify your identity and have legitimate reasons for losing access — including circumstances that were completely outside of your control, or? Would the situation really have been handled the same way if my account had been hacked?

review_title: Airbnb’s review system is broken
review_text: Due to hosts are getting better at earning honest 5-star reviews from guests, Airbnb began to find that hard to believe. I’m stuck with nonrefundable flights and tuition for school programs my daughters were set to attend in Mexico—this wasn’t even a World Cup trip for us, just essential family travel. Hosts and Airbnb: this kind of last-minute bait-and-switch is outright scummy. Travelers, beware and book at your own risk.

review_title: Shocking service

We stayed at a cottage where we had several issues which were investigated by  the host booking a plumber to investigate a horrible smell in the pantry which occured around breakfast time but the plumber wasn't there at the time so the host wouldn't believe us. We also had problems with the immersion and chimney. The property also had no smoke alarm which I didn't see before booking as we took it for granted every property had one. We are now in a situation where other hosts can read our previous hosts review it will prevent us from booking again through air BnB as the hosts will reject our accommodation. We did not leave an abusive review we just told the truth as we found it and wasn't helped by the host portraying us as making up fictitious complaints. Another thing I think is very wrong is when a host advertise their accommodation saying it has no smoke alarm that they allow the host to accept bookings when they know renting a property without one is a serious breach of the law. I would advise anyone to make sure the property they are booking has a smoke alarm and I am disgusted and dismayed with air BnB that accepts hosts accommodation who states their property having no smoke alarm which is a duty of care by the host not an option. We won't book through air BnB again  and do not recommend their service to anyone. D M Norfolk

review_title: Incompetent and Deceptive Customer Service
review_text: I am filing this complaint regarding Airbnb’s handling of a failed Airbnb Experience and the customer service process that followed. I physically attended the experience in Bangkok at the scheduled meeting point, but the host never showed up and did not respond to Airbnb messages while I was waiting. I eventually had to independently track down the host’s WhatsApp information outside the platform just to get a response. When I contacted Airbnb support, I requested a refund but specifically stated in writing that I wanted my ability to leave a review preserved because future guests should be warned about the host no-show. Airbnb support assured me that I would still be able to leave a review. Instead, Airbnb retroactively canceled the booking after the experience date had already passed in order to process the refund, which removed my review eligibility entirely. Afterward, multiple representatives avoided directly addressing why support handled the case in a way that contradicted what I had been told. In the end, I requested either that Airbnb restore my ability to leave a review or provide a travel credit/voucher due to the mishandling of the case and the false assurances I was given. Airbnb refused both requests and ultimately closed the case rather than continue addressing the issue. My complaint is not about receiving the refund. It is about Airbnb support giving misleading assurances, mishandling the case, and then removing my ability to publicly document a host no-show that I personally experienced firsthand.

review_title: Unacceptable customer service policies
review_text: I've been hosting on Airbnb for ten years, during which time their customer relations has steadily gone downhill. I recently had a terrible experience with a guest who was harrassing me and they've done nothing to help, even though I'm a Superhost with an excellent rating and hundreds of 5* reviews and happy guests. The guest booked for a month (I host long term stays, so my minimum is 28 days). Throughout her stay, she communicated in writing how much she loved me and the house. In fact, she wanted to book another stay, which I asked her to do via the platform. She then had a van load of stuff taken out of storage and delivered here without any warning. She wanted to book a shorter stay (not the one month she originally told me), do it off platform, plus leave piles of stuff here for two weeks for free. I politely declined but she wouldn't take no for an answer and became hostile, so I called Airbnb for help. They promised they would back me up. Instead, they restricted my listings, meaning I lost a long term booking. The guest then attempted to get a full refund for her stay. When I declined this, she left me a 1* review. I requested Airbnb remove this review as it was clearly retalitory and provided all the written evidence. However, it seems that now this is handled by AI rather than a person, and the BOT will automatically decline without looking at any evidence. CS say that, while they agree the review is retalitory and should be removed, there is nothing they can do about it. It's not just guests who get treated unfairly. They don't protect the hosts against scammers either. I have unlisted my rooms from Airbnb.

review_title: Very disappointing experience.
review_text: Very disappointing experience. Our family could not travel because airport operations were affected due to regional security tensions — a situation completely outside our control. Despite this, the host refused any flexibility or partial support and strictly hid behind the non-refundable policy. Policies are understandable, but genuine force majeure situations should be handled with fairness and empathy. Unfortunately, there was zero cooperation. Would not recommend for travellers expecting understanding during emergency situations.

review_title: Made a booking
review_text: Made a booking. The moment the booking was made, the host raised the cost. Said he priced wrong. But, took the £800 deposit. Not returned 2 weeks later. Airbnb refuse to help.

review_title: Home in Urb Puerto Rico
review_text: Home in Urb. Solimar, Puerto Rico Hosted by Maureen Co-host Monica Reservation details: Confirmation code HMN42T2AXM I had a highly disappointing experience regarding a recent accommodation booking handled through a platform-connected host. Due to an emergency situation involving my baby’s health, I needed to adjust our accommodation to reduce travel time and ensure a more comfortable stay. This was not a change in travel plans, but purely a health-related necessity. Despite clearly communicating the situation and requesting support, the host declined any flexibility. The resolution process felt rigid, with limited consideration given to the emergency circumstances. As a result, I was unable to receive meaningful assistance or a fair resolution. While I understand policies are in place, I believe there should be stronger emphasis on empathy and case-by-case review, especially when health-related concerns are involved. At this point, I have no choice but to prioritize my family and my baby first, even if that means cancelling the booking and facing the financial loss. I am sharing this feedback so that future guests are aware of how such situations may be handled and to encourage improved customer support standards in similar cases.

review_title: Do not trust Airbnb.
review_text: Do not trust Airbnb to protect you as a guest. I arrived to a unit that wasn't ready, had to scramble for last-minute accommodations at midnight after hours of travel, and paid out of pocket for a place to sleep. The host confirmed the cancellation and said a refund would be issued — so I moved on, reasonably assuming it was handled. It wasn't. $514 never came back to me. When I finally caught it reviewing my finances and contacted support, Airbnb hid behind a 72-hour policy window that was never communicated to me — not by the host, not by the platform, not once. They knew the unit wasn't ready. They had the photos. The host confirmed the refund. None of it mattered. Airbnb will take your money and leave you with nothing to show for it. Book direct. Book a hotel. Do anything but trust this platform to have your back when something goes wrong — because they won't.

review_title: Worst customer service I have ever experienced
review_text: I am currently in the middle of a dispute with Airbnb over a four thousand dollar stay that had a strong urine odor and more than 20 visible urine stains on the carpet, which I reported immediately upon arrival with video evidence. The host acknowledged the smell in writing, then when I pushed for a refund, they denied there was any odor at all. Airbnb told me the host said there was “no smell” and moved to close the case. Now I have to dispute the charge with my credit card. What made the experience worse was being passed between multiple support agents, receiving conflicting information, and repeatedly being promised updates that never came. I have spent thousands through Airbnb over the years, but after this experience and the complete lack of support despite clear evidence, I will never book through them again.

review_title: They blamed me for the problem after saying it happened to others/
review_text: I have used AirB&B in the past and I usually select to pay half now and half closer to the time of the trip. If I had, why would I be surprised to see the total amount on my credit card.  So I told him instead of blaming me, they should think about fixing their website because there are other options people can use for lodging and I will next time.  GRRRRR

review_title: Avoid Airbnb
review_text: Extremely disappointing experience both with the Airbnb stay itself and with Airbnb customer service afterward. The property had multiple issues: difficulty accessing the apartment late at night, an unsafe exterior door that would not close properly, almost no basic supplies provided, and a furnace failure overnight that left the unit at 16°C with no response from the host until morning. The listing was also misleadingly described as “waterfront” despite the area beside the water being littered with garbage. What made the experience worse was the handling afterward. The host initially thanked me publicly with a 5-star review, but after I posted an honest review of my experience, Airbnb removed my review citing “pressure and coercion” without explaining what policy was violated. Afterward, the host changed his positive review into a negative one containing inaccurate claims, which felt retaliatory. I spent hours trying to get clarification from customer service and received only vague, scripted responses with no transparency or meaningful explanation. Guests should be allowed to leave honest factual feedback about legitimate concerns without feeling silenced.

review_title: accused of damage
review_text: I was accused of cracking a bathtub during my stay at an AirBNB. I denied it and provided reasoning for how this damage could not have been caused by me, but AirBNB sided with the host. I was given a chance to appeal, during which I once again explained how I could not reasonably be responsible for this damage, I am below average weight, did not fall, did not drop anything, and only took showers standing at the opposite end of the tub from the claimed damage (a 3/4 inch crack) but it was once again denied. I was given no proof that the damage wasn’t there before my arrival, as well as no reasoning for why a crack wouldn’t be caused by improper installation (common cause of fibreglass tubs cracking). I was given no explanation for their reasoning despite my requests, and my card was charged automatically. I am appealing again today, but so far have gotten no further explanation to the concerns I have raised in previous appeals, I am extremely disappointed, not only of being accused and charged for this, but also in the customer service after having spent thousands through AirBNB.

review_title: ​I traveled to Florida under the worst…
review_text: ​I traveled to Florida under the worst possible circumstances: to say goodbye to my grandfather, who was passing from aggressive spine cancer. After driving 29 hours straight, I arrived at my Airbnb only to discover a bed bug infestation. When I contacted support, the nightmare truly began. ​Despite being physically and emotionally exhausted, Airbnb refused to help unless I went back into the infested room to take photos. I complied just to get my money back, but then spent the next 12 hours trapped in a loop of corporate incompetence. I called repeatedly, only to be hung up on, transferred to the wrong departments, or left on hold. They offered no relocation assistance and no emergency voucher, leaving me stranded and homeless for an entire day while I should have been with my family. ​Eventually, I gave up on their "help" and paid for a hotel out of my own pocket just to have a safe place to sleep. After all that, Airbnb offered a measly $20 compensation—a literal slap in the face. This company has zero empathy and no safety net for guests in crisis. They are an absolute disgrace.

review_title: Damage claim process ignores guest evidence, be warned. Safety team absent.
review_text: I stayed 2 months in a shared apartment in  Switzerland. The host smoked cigarettes in the shared kitchen and her son smoked cannabis in the room next to mine, causing me dizziness. This was not disclosed in the listing, and Airbnb safety team did nothing regarding the usage of cannabis. The bedroom had no lock, and the host entered my room without permission while I was out, confirmed this in her own review by describing details of my private space. After my stay, I left an honest review. Shortly after, the host filed a damage claim for   for minor cosmetic wear. Scratches only visible under extreme zoom. Chipping at the base of bed legs that doesn't affect functionality. I submitted a detailed appeal with photos of the room's poor condition at check-in. The host provided no before photos. None of my evidence was considered by Airbnb. Every response I received was generic and templated. Airbnb's damage claim process appears designed to side with hosts by default and exhaust guests into paying. If you dispute a claim with detailed evidence and it gets ignored, the process is not a mediation, it's a formality. My advice to future guests: photograph everything at check-in. You will need it, because the burden of proof falls entirely on you, even when the host provides none.
