review_title: Asked to pay nearly £520 for alleged damage without evidence (ongoing dispute)
review_text: I’ve been using Airbnb as a guest for around 10 years and have consistently received 5-star reviews, along with communications describing me as a valued member of the community. After my most recent stay, a host requested approximately £520 for scratches on the floor. I was surprised to see Airbnb support this claim and request payment, but no clear evidence has been provided to demonstrate that the damage occurred during my stay. I am currently disputing this and have formally requested the supporting documentation needed to assess the claim. At this stage, I have not been provided with sufficient evidence (such as pre-stay condition records or itemised repair documentation) to verify the request. I believe it is reasonable to expect transparent and complete documentation before being asked to cover such costs. This experience has significantly affected my confidence in the platform. As a result, I now feel the need to document the condition of properties upon arrival and departure to protect myself. However, it is not realistic to expect guests to comprehensively document every aspect of a property’s condition on arrival, particularly for issues that may not be immediately visible or apparent. I will update this review once the dispute is resolved. Update: 04/05/2026 Airbnb has informed me that they are closing their correspondence regarding the claim, stating that Host Damage Protection has been used to support the host. However, no evidence has been provided— No pre-stay photos, timestamps, or repair invoices. — Leaving the claim entirely unsubstantiated. The host’s messages in the platform were strongly accusatory, blaming my luggage for the alleged damage. Despite this “closure,” the Resolution Center in my Airbnb account still shows the case as “in dispute.” I cannot respond, upload evidence, or see any payment request, and Airbnb’s communications suggest that my account could potentially be charged in the future. I am also contacting Airbnb’s Support Team directly, as the Resolutions Team has not provided full transparency or engagement regarding this claim. I will update this review once Airbnb provides full transparency and clear confirmation of the claim’s status.

review_title: Airbnb refunded us, but offered no real help after a last-minute cancellation
review_text: We booked an Airbnb for our trip, and the host/co-host informed us that they could no longer accommodate us at the exact time of check-in. Instead of taking full responsibility and cancelling the reservation themselves, they asked us to cancel from our side to “speed up the process,” saying they would accept the cancellation without penalties. Airbnb did refund the full amount of the original reservation, but that did not solve the real problem. At that point, we were already supposed to check in and urgently needed a place to stay. When we asked Airbnb to help us find another accommodation or provide a discount/compensation for the price difference, we did not receive any useful support or clear response. In the end, we had to find another place by ourselves with similar characteristics and pay around 3,000 MXN more than the original booking. This caused unnecessary stress, disrupted our plans, and forced us to cover an extra cost that was not our responsibility. The most disappointing part is that Airbnb treated the refund as if it solved everything, but in a same-day check-in cancellation, a refund is not enough. Guests still need a place to stay immediately, and prices are usually much higher when booking at the last minute. Overall, this was a very frustrating experience. Airbnb should protect guests better in these situations by helping them rebook or offering fair compensation when a host cancels at the exact time of check-in.

review_title: I had a disappointing experience with…
review_text: I had a disappointing experience with Airbnb customer service. I contacted support immediately after booking to request a simple date change due to a change in my travel plans. The property was fully available, and the request was made within a reasonable time frame. Despite this, the host did not respond, and Airbnb failed to step in and assist. I spoke with a representative who assured me the case would be handled and reviewed. All calls are recorded, so this can be verified. After waiting, I was informed that nothing could be done because the host did not approve the change. This left me with no real support or solution. I was effectively forced to either proceed with dates that no longer worked or cancel and lose 50 percent of the booking. This is not acceptable. When plans change, especially within such a short time after booking, there should be a fair and reasonable process in place. Customer service should protect both sides, not leave the guest without options. In this case, Airbnb did not provide any meaningful assistance or resolution. I will think carefully before booking again.

review_title: Our experience with Airbnb regarding…
review_text: Our experience with Airbnb regarding this incident was highly disappointing. Although the platform promotes that it provides safety and support to its guests, in our case the opposite occurred. We encountered a serious issue with the accommodation, for which we bore no responsibility, and found ourselves in a very difficult situation. Despite contacting support promptly, the response was inadequate, and the handling of our case was both slow and emotionally draining. Instead of receiving meaningful assistance and an immediate resolution, we experienced delays, repeated inconvenience, and a lack of clear communication. To this day, no refund has been issued, even though the additional expenses arose from circumstances beyond our control. We believe that when a platform charges for and promotes protection and safety services, it should respond effectively in such situations. Unfortunately, our experience does not reflect that.

review_title: I recently had an issue with Airbnb
review_text: I recently had an issue with Airbnb. When I got to the rental, it was in an area that I didn’t wish to stay in due to safety concerns. Several houses on the block were boarded up, some were even collapsed and some sort of transaction was taking place in front of the driveway to the property. We left and canceled the reservation. When I contacted Airbnb to tell them about the situation, I was told I should have stayed at the property and called for a ‘safety team’. When I inquired as to what is a safety team I wasn’t given an explanation. Then I was told I didn’t provide evidence to my claims. I reiterated that they wanted me to remain at a place and take pictures when I didn’t feel safe?! That makes no sense. They told me the host didn’t agree with me and therefore there wouldn’t be a refund. I argued back and forth and eventually was give a partial credit for future use. My concern is that they don’t check properties that are advertised on their site. I googled maps the location and only saw rooftops, therefore I was relying on them to advertise safe locations or at least describe the location more accurately. I write this review to warn others to be more cautious when renting from this company. Do your own research because Airbnb does not check at all!

review_title: Disappointing experience, a clear gap from the Airbnb I once valued
review_text: I was a personal Airbnb host for several years and genuinely enjoyed working with the platform in the past. The experience was smooth, consistent, and aligned with the values Airbnb promoted at the time. My recent experience, however, through the new host onboarding/accompaniment program, has been deeply disappointing. Despite a significant and measurable investment of time, travel, and hands-on support to ensure proper and compliant onboarding, the compensation received did not cover the actual costs incurred. In one specific case, my expenses exceeded $200, making the engagement financially negative despite full compliance with all requirements. The bonus calculation relies on internal criteria, but these do not reflect the real workload involved when providing serious, quality support to new hosts. It is concerning that a program designed to encourage quality and engagement ultimately penalizes those who invest the most effort. This stands in stark contrast to the Airbnb experience I previously valued and supported. A meaningful review of the compensation model would be necessary to ensure fairness, sustainability, and alignment with the platform’s stated values.

review_title: AirBNB not doing enough to prevent false adds
review_text: It seems AirBNB do not have any responsibility for the accuracy of their adds. We booked one that had the wrong district and wrong location showing on the map. When we arrived , we were given the actual address as being 13km away from the location advertised. Airbnb were informed , however 4 weeks later the incorrect Add is there. Make sure you get the actual address from the host before you depart.

review_title: I've stayed in Airbnb's from California…
review_text: I've stayed in Airbnb's from California to Maine, some 40 states. I stay at Airbnb's to cook my own food. Invariably,  the kitchens are stocked with horrible cooking pans, often mottled and/or rusted. There is never a full oven, so one must use these awful frying pans. Generally,  there is a limited amount of silverware. There is almost never enough toilet tissue or soap-some ask us to buy our own. One host in West Palm Beach told us to wash our own towels. Reviews are not credible because if a guest gives a host a poor review, the host can retaliate & give the guest a poor review, thereby leading other hosts to be reluctant to rent to thia guest. Since hotel rates have skyrocketed out of control, we are left no choice but to use Airbnb type establishments.

review_title: Publicly Humiliated
review_text: We recently paid over £1,500 for a stay in Gibraltar and during our stay was publicly humiliated by a security guard at the property. He made us feel threatened and frighted and left us with a shaken experience. We were told we had access to the pool area but he threw us out whilst screaming and shouting. At 67 years of age it's the last thing we expected. We complained to Airbnb and was given a paltry £200 credit for our next booking.

review_title: Airbnb… we once loved each other.
review_text: Seven years as a spotless host, hundreds of guests, and complete trust in Airbnb — all wiped out by one absurd case handled with arrogance and bureaucracy instead of fairness. Yes: on Trustpilot, we describe companies according to the trust and fairness they show in real-life situations. And until now, I had enormous trust in Airbnb. I have been treated to a stubborn and senseless refusal of a damage claim, carved in stone like the Ten Commandments, despite the many photos, receipts, one invoice, and a video fully supporting my case. If Airbnb can take such a defiant and irrational attitude over a minor matter like this, I truly wonder what would happen in more serious circumstances. This is their Host Protection Program, supposedly designed to cover damage to hosts’ properties caused by Airbnb guests — but in reality, it has turned out to be an empty promise. And all this over about €515. Their “final” message came from someone named Natalia, a “Floor Manager” — whatever that means — who simply copied and pasted a pre-written response, ignoring 28 previous emails and all the evidence provided. That position was later confirmed by a chap called Marshall S., amid hypocritical expressions such as “sincere appreciation”, “feedback and interactions have been beyond helpful”, and “we truly value the partnership we have built with you”. Not a single word was spent explaining the “various factors” supposedly justifying the denial of a fair resolution. After seven years as an impeccable host, the last few as a Superhost, with hundreds of guests and a spotless record, I was treated as if I were trying to cheat the system. This attitude is not only unfair and arrogant; it is deeply offensive to the trust that thousands of hosts place in Airbnb every day. My experience shows that Airbnb’s so-called protection is illusory, and that when a host genuinely needs support, what they get instead is bureaucracy, empty formulas, and evasion of responsibility. Even if this ends up costing me money, I am going to take legal action for damages against this company, which has failed — without offering any explanation whatsoever — to meet its contractual obligations or to conduct itself in accordance with basic standards of respect and business ethics. After this experience, trust has been seriously damaged.

review_title: Bad customer service experience.
review_text: We had a booking for a week in Venice, Italy. Although the apartment was quoted as a 5 star the place was unfit to stay in. We reported the problem and got a total refund but got no help with finding another accommodation. We were given a vague explanation about AirBnB having a global issue and that they could not do anything for us. We were left on our own, late in the evening, walking around the city in the rain with our luggage to find an hotel that could take us in.

review_title: Whenever you been a nice visitor (host)…
review_text: Whenever you been a nice visitor (host) at an expensive stay because of airbnb stay and they gave you no review, Airbnb is not your friend in confrontating the bad room renting party with this. So airbnb is only getting the money and is not doing anything about it.

review_title: Subpar experience
review_text: Subpar experience.   My first reservation didn't work because host wanted 24 hours notice (for a same night stay)!   The app did not work on my phone (hasn't for a long time, despite repeated attempts to fix it).   I did get a reservation, but place does not have internet!

review_title: Slow customer service
review_text: I had a terrible experience with customer service, and with the guy who was renting his small apartment. I needed to go out of town to stay in an apartment for a week, and decided to go for one of the houses. The process was like always, but the guy who was renting started to back up, and disappear. He didn’t respond to phone calls and messages. I tried to contact the customer service to understand what I have to do, but the answer took so long. Please, take more people into your support stuff or do something with the speed, because the situation was bad, and I was sitting there for hours not knowing which step to take next…

review_title: Disappointed
review_text: On arrival it seemed pleasant, however on closer inspection found a number of issues. All the beds 1 x double & 2 x singles mattresses were very uncomfortable, with the springs and lumps giving discomfort, even one of the  single  beds had missing slats under the mattress so was unusable, when we went to use the sofa beds there was a dirty sheet, and mess /crumbs in the base, so my grand daughter placed the sofa cushions on the floor for her bed. The D/bed headboard was covered in dust, all the table lamps & cooker hood had not been cleaned and were dusty. One of the kitchen unit doors next to the oven was delaminated with very sharp edges. My wife went to use the  hairdryer and it went off and smelt of burning we also noted that the portable appliance testing of electrical appliance (although not a legal requirement but deemed a 'best practise') many were tested in 2021 and some like the hairdryer was not tested, the tenant was notified and responded by stating it was due in Oct. The white mugs were badly scored inside and out, the dining table chairs seats of which two were cracked/split and only three! Overall not impressed with the experience

review_title: Unsafe water and no good follow up
review_text: We've had some good stays, but when it's bad it's bad. We stayed at a place with mouse poop on a bed, unsafe brown drinking water that was not disclosed to us prior to the stay, and broken items. When we asked for a small refund, the host ghosted us and wrote a review that we left the place "messy and in need of a deep clean" when it was already not cleaned well to begin with. And our review was taken down, with no indication that Air BnB will follow up with the hosts to require they can't rent it with unsafe water or at least need to disclose. The experience of trying to follow up on the issues was worse than the stay, and not worth it for the good stays.

review_title: Unable to deal with issues fairly due to subservience to their 'processes'.
review_text: Writing as a host I have concerns re Air BnB's ability to deal with issues fairly. A guest left me a glowing review, a message saying they had a great time and wanted to return, but only a 3 star overall rating.  I haven't been open long, so one 3 star review in amongst the other 5 star reviews has made a dent in my overall rating, and that matters when you are a small BnB at the very bottom end of the BnB price range. The guest promised to change or delete it, but they didn't. I contacted Air BnB and they sent me a link that they told me the guest could use to delete the review. I sent it to the guest. The guest said that they would do it but a week later nothing had happened. I used Air BnB's review appeal process twice to try and get the rating removed but they refused both times, and then said that as I had used up my permitted two attempts they couldn't do anything further. In between these attempts I telephone them and the person I spoke to assured me that if I requested it deleted again it would be done, but it wasn't. Mean time the guest got back to me saying that the followed the link I sent them and they have looked and looked but couldn't see any way to delete the review. I called Air BnB again, and this time they said that the guest needed to sent them a message asking/authorising them to delete the review - which they could, and should, have told me the first time I contacted them (i'm not sure what the link that they sent me was for). But my issue with them is this... Air BnB's policies and blurb goes on endlessly about the importance of accurate and fair reviews and how the whole system works on the trust of these reviews. In this case no one was claiming that the 3 stars were fair. Air BnB could see my conversation with the guest, they could see that the guest was saying it was a mistake, but they still refused to delete it... so fair reviews are apparently not that important to them after all. I have ME and I have recently reopened, having had to give up my paid job through illness. So the BnB income, although small, is everything to me. This makes me feel lousy every day, but stress, emotional and mental etc, cause me to crash and get much sicker. Each time I have to spend an hour on the phone to Air BnB it causes a crash. So this stuff matters. It's disappointing as previously I have found their customer support people quite helpful, but this time they seem to be at the mercy of their 'processes' and there are no ways to correct mistakes.

review_title: I am completely blocked from using…
review_text: I am completely blocked from using Airbnb and the support has been no help at all. My account was banned some time ago because I was underage. Now that I am 18, I submitted an appeal and got an email confirming that I had been unbanned. However, nothing changed—I am still stuck on the ban screen. review_title: Not the best experience
review_text: The apartment looked much better in the photos than in reality. It wasn’t very clean, and the check-in process was confusing. The location was fine, but overall the stay didn’t meet expectations. I expected more professionalism from an Airbnb host.

review_title: Gift Card debacle
review_text: I have been a faithful AirBnb user for a few years with great reviews as a renter. This last booking just put me out on AirBnb. I booked a unit for 6 nights at $1200. Great price. Then, the fees added on an extra $700. So, after the initial down payment, I had finally built up enough rewards to purchase 2 AirBnb gift cards. I read all of the dos and don'ts about gift cards. I thought I had a handle on it, but it seems not. I added the first gift card under the PAY NOW, which is the only way it would take the credit. That worked but when I tried to add the second, it showed the whole remaining balance was paid. I never got to add the second gift card. I called support and nothing they could do. There has to be a way to add multiple gift cards after you have made a payment. What a waste.

review_title: The idea of Airbnb is nice
review_text: The idea of Airbnb is nice, but in reality it can be frustarting. Extra fees make listings much more expensive than advertised, and customer support is slow when problems come up. Feels unreliable compared to hotels.

review_title: Good location, poor service
review_text: Airbnb has many nice listings, but the customer service is disappointing. My booking had issues, and support replies were slow and unhelpful.

review_title: Air B N B Services Is Very Difficult To Work With
review_text: As a new host for Air B N B services, the process to get approved has been excruciatingly frustrating.  I own a brick and mortar spa that is rated 5 stars on Google and has been open 5 years.  In May 2025, I submitted my business to Airbnb services. Since then I have received first AI generated information saying that I had to change the listing. They gave me very little information about what needed to be changed. After making the edits and submitting them it took nearly 2 months to get the edits approved. In fact, I am still waiting for the approval process. I’ve had to have meetings with their associates, and even after that meeting and asking for them to not include my personal name in the listing they still provided me back copy 10 days later of my personal name included in the listing. I’ve explained to them several times that it should not take three months to get a listing approved. it is ironic that it is so easy for a host to put up a property and they barely verify it, yet you have to go through scrutinizing approval to get an Airbnb services listing. At this time, I would not recommend other businesses to work with Airbnb services because it will take so much of your time and resources, and they will continue to leave you in the dark about what is happening. If you’re listing finally gets approved, it could take over 90 days to do so. And then, of course I don’t even know what to expect once the listing is approved. I have been asking if there is a Supervisor for me to provide feedback with and there is no supervisor available. So far it looks like Airbnb services is a great idea, but they are too disorganized and overloaded to be able to actually make it work out.

review_title: Charge back claim after positive review
review_text: We rented an apartment with airbnb in France. We paid 4000 eur for just over a week stay. The apartment had a lovely view and was large but it wasnt properly clean when we arrived- dust/spider webs in the corners/under furniture, dirty cups/dishes with previous users stains on them, kitchen filter covered in grease... We also experienced a broken boiler and shutter during our stay- both of which we facilitated repair people for and made no issue of. The owner gave us positive feedback on leaving and we did the same for him- for peace sake, however 2 weeks after doing so we got a text from the owner asking us to contribute to the broken shutter either directly to him or he would claim it back via airbnb. We couldn't believe it. We said no obviously- as the issue was clearly electrical as it wouldn't open. I've had good experiences with Airbnb before but this incident left such a sour taste in our mouth I'm not sure we'd ever use them again.

review_title: Generally I find the AirBnb system…
review_text: Generally I find the AirBnb system rather bad. With the hotels and other big renters it works ok, but with the private hosts (which, avowedly, are what makes the app stand out), it differs from case to case. Some hosts seem to forget that they run a business, and don't offer informal couch-surfing opportunities, and might behave impolitely or unprofessionally; and if you stumble upon such an unfortunate person - you get very little protection, as the company wants to protect its image first. Plus, the ability of hosts to write the reviews of their guests, while seemingly fair, opens the way to defamatory claims in revenge. All in all it's not a good dynamics and if you want to use it, especially renting from private persons, know it is a risk.

Airbnb’s only response has been to tell us to WAIT, which is incredibly frustrating.

review_title: I've used Airbnb several times over the…
review_text: I've used Airbnb several times over the past few years, but lately, I've become increasingly frustrated with their service fees. The total cost of my bookings often ends up being much higher than the initial nightly rate due to the added Airbnb service fees. Sometimes, the service fee alone can be a significant percentage of the total price, making the platform less affordable than it appears at first glance. What's more disappointing is that these fees aren't always transparent until the final stages of booking. It feels misleading, and I wish Airbnb would be more upfront about the total cost from the beginning. While I appreciate the convenience and variety of listings, the high and sometimes unclear service fees make me reconsider using Airbnb for future trips.

review_title: Policy and Hosting

The drain was clogged and standing water was 6" deep with soap scum. I had to ask for someone to come and clean it. When I booked, I was charged 30.00 cleaning service.

review_title: French bookings are a nightmare
review_text: I am normally very happy to book with Airbnb, but booking French properties is an absolute nighmare. You need to wait for confirmation of the booking, and in my experience 80 per cent of the properties are not available for booking, yet they are listed for the dates you look for. They take payment and then you have to wait around a week for the refund. I am currently looking for a property in the Alps, and 5 properties have rejected my request for different reasons, mostly because they have not updated their prices for the next ski season, but they haven't bothered to remove the listings. What a waste of time. Airbnb should not allow this, it makes it very frustrating and time consuming to look for accommodation, in fact I given up, I will look elswhere,

review_title: Airbnb’s Review System Encourages Pressure, Not Honesty
review_text: As a frequent Airbnb user, I’ve noticed a troubling trend: many hosts now push hard for 5-star reviews - sometimes through messages, signs in the home, or follow-up pressure after your stay. It’s clear this is driven by Airbnb’s algorithm, which seems to only value perfect ratings. This creates a fake sense of quality. Some listings are overrated because guests feel uncomfortable giving anything less than 5 stars, even when the stay was average. I’ve even experienced hosts offering small gifts or guilt-tripping messages to “earn” that perfect score. Airbnb should consider a fairer system, like a Net Promoter Score (NPS), where guests anonymously share whether they’d recommend a place. This would promote real feedback and better experiences for everyone. Until then, take glowing reviews with a grain of salt, many are more about keeping the peace than telling the truth.

review_title: Airbnbs business model favors dishonest hosts.
review_text: Airbnb favors hosts who try to maximize their profit by scamming the system  they claim false damage charges,charging extra to have cleaning that’s supposed to be a part of the contract, or they provide some cleaning supplies for you to clean it yourThe hosts want to communicate with you off of the platform so they can sell you anything from their rental without the platform fees, to products they or their family sellsIf you complain you probably will get blocked from using the platform being labeled high riskThey need hosts and they favor them over paying guestsThey do not even favor guests who have used their platform repeatedly .

review_text: The booking and holiday went well but there was a dispute about some damage at the end of our stay. I contacted Airbnb Résolution and described the issue to them. They never responded. 24 hrs later they closed the issue. I have asked them what they did about it several times; - - nothing it seems.

review_title: Airbnb Ignored Clear Policy Violations – Harmful Review Left Up
review_text: I’ve been a loyal Airbnb host and have always tried to maintain a high standard for my guests. But I recently faced a deeply frustrating experience that I believe every host should be aware of. A guest left a review that included false and damaging claims, including: •	Speculation about hidden surveillance devices (with no evidence) •	A false statement that my listing was an “entire home” when it’s clearly listed as a guesthouse •	No issues raised during the stay — only false allegations made after checkout I submitted two formal requests for removal, clearly referencing Airbnb’s own Review and Content Policies (which prohibit false or misleading content and unsubstantiated accusations). Both times, I received what felt like automated responses with no real explanation. Eventually, I was told the case was closed and the decision couldn’t be overturned — despite the review clearly violating the rules. This has had a real impact on my family’s small business, and I no longer feel protected as a host. Airbnb encourages hosts to be transparent and professional — but when the system fails to enforce its own policies, that trust breaks down. I hope Airbnb re-evaluates how it supports its host community in situations like this.

review_title: Hosts Beware
review_text: Hosts, take note: Airbnb primarily views guests as their customers, not hosts. In many disputes, they tend to favor the traveler’s side—even when it comes to property damage or violations of house rules. Getting reimbursed for damages can be a frustrating, uphill process. Airbnb often issues partial refunds without your consent, and sometimes even full refunds within cancellation windows—regardless of circumstances. While the platform does a great job of getting your listing seen and booked, don’t expect a fair resolution when conflicts arise. As for retaliatory reviews? Unfortunately, contesting them is nearly always a losing battle.

review_title: Customer Service and Poor Website Redesign
review_text: While Airbnb is a massive global platform, the quality of its customer service is surprisingly poor. It’s frustrating to see that a company valued at $84 billion has such a low average rating of 1.4 on Trustpilot—clearly, I’m not the only one who feels this way. The lack of responsive and helpful support is simply unacceptable. Additionally, the recent website redesign is a step backward. The new layout is confusing, cumbersome, and far more complex than the previous version. If something works well, why change it? The new interface makes navigation unnecessarily difficult, which only adds to the frustration when trying to resolve issues. For a company of this scale, I expected far better in both customer support and user experience. I hope Airbnb takes the feedback seriously and makes meaningful improvements.

review_title: No Airbnb reviews after 14 days
review_text: This  is a review of from a customer support perspective. I have been a customer of Airbnb for 12 years. I can say I have had mostly very good to great hosting and accommodation from this company. Recently we had two great  Airbnb experiences in Portugal and when I returned home I wanted to give them 5 star+ reviews. After further travel and catching up with business at home I sat down to write  reviews but was informed that I had passed a 14 day limit for reviews. I reviewed this policy and could find no good rationale or logic for it. I contacted customer support texted them and talked to them on the phone. The customer support center is obviously located as a call center probably in South Asia somewhere and the staff and senior advisors are handcuffed when it comes to this policy. They have no authority or discretion in making decisions. Obviously me writing a five star review would be good for the company, my Airbnb hosts and potential customers. Not going to happen-stonewalled with scripted responses. Wonder what would happen if we ran into some serious problems on the road.

To my mind a property which has blocked drains, a tap which does not work, no bread knife in self catering and cupboard doors which fall off is not 5 star and yet everyone keeps saying they had a five star stay.  So, forget the star rating at the beginning, introduce more categories with comments for verification and clarification.  Start with equipment, standard of furnishings and the like and we will start to see more honest and useful reviews and the overall  score will be more accurate.  And when the payment system with paypal broke down they refused to say it was there problem until lots of pointless emails had been exchanged.  Customer service these days is not good

review_title: Disappointed by Airbnb’s Treatment of…
review_text: Disappointed by Airbnb’s Treatment of Longstanding Hosts I have been a loyal Airbnb host for over six years, proudly maintaining Superhost status and receiving mostly 5-star reviews from wonderful guests. Hosting has never just been a business to me — it’s something I’ve poured my heart, time, and care into. Unfortunately, my recent experience with Airbnb Support has left me feeling completely disheartened. A guest left a poor review on my listing after a rare, temporary water issue in my town — an external problem entirely beyond my control, which affected many homes in the area. I reached out to Airbnb, not to silence the guest, but to ask for understanding, fairness, and at the very least the chance to update my response to the review professionally. Instead, I was met with rigid, robotic responses, no empathy, and even received a warning threatening suspension from the platform if I receive another low-star review — despite the fact that I have a long, proven track record of excellent hosting. Shockingly, they referenced a 3-star review from last September, completely ignoring the countless 5-star reviews I’ve worked hard to earn. This experience has made me feel that Airbnb no longer values its hosts as people — only as numbers on a screen. There was no kindness, no consideration of the circumstances, and no support for someone who has given years of loyal service to their platform. My hope in writing this review is that Airbnb reflects on how they treat their hosts — especially those who genuinely care and take pride in creating beautiful guest experiences. We deserve to feel valued, supported, and treated with fairness — not fear.

review_title: Where do I even start..
review_text: Where do I even start... Been using Airbnb for quite a few trips, and I would say only maybe 2 have been hiccup free. Firstly, they don't seem to vet their hosts very well, and I've had several cancel on me for seemingly no reason! One was 10 minutes before I was due to check-in, and another 2 days before! And both I only found out about because I contacted them!! Granted, Airbnb have sorted out the issues quickly and provided compensation, but they need to have stricter policies with their hosts so save travelers being stranded in foreign cities! The live chat function and helpline are quick to respond and sort our problems, but there are just too many problems to begin with.

review_title: Find another rental service, not protecting the clients
review_text: Pretty bad experience as we had a terrible stay with a host, we left a respectful but truthful review about it and that host retaliated with a vengeful, defamatory comment on my profile. Airbnb chose to leave this comment as it is, i.e.: on my profile forever, affecting all my future stays. Also, that place was of health hazards full of bed bugs and Airbnb did nothing to warn the future guests, in fact, they refused to let us comment about that fact when we tried to. Not recommended and very disappointed of the service and the lack of values of this company.

review_title: Airbnb is a joke
review_text: I have been an Airbnb person for the last three years. I recently Airbnbed out a property of mine in Florida. Let me tell you about the kind of people that came to stay at my place two strippers that got high the entire time and then had the audacity to say they felt like they were being watched and harassed and people don’t like it when the host bothers them. Well, she parked in the main driveway and was asked to relocate her car and that apparently made her feel unsafe and like she had no privacy. Or how about the construction workers that said they had four when my Airbnb specifically said it fits two comfortably or 4 if you’re in a pinch and then they brought eight people who disrupted my tenants tore up my yard and broke all my stuff. But Airbnb didn’t care about that. Although I did get the $20 back for the broken curtain rod, but not the four additional people two additional trucks and all the other damage. or how about the old people that came took all of the lighting fixtures off the walls and said I needed more lighting and rated me a two on cleanliness because they didn’t have a washer and dryer and felt that it needed to be updated. It needed to be updated. You had a stove and oven and everything that you need to live there except a washer and dryer. Let’s not forget the pictures and the square footage are all in the listing. On top of that, guests we’re paying two to $300 more for their taxes and fees and then guests are getting mad at me saying I’m expensive. I unlisted my property after only three months, two drug baggies (different guests) and two people who lied about who was staying. It gives people like me who travel and don’t wanna stay at a hotel, a bad rep. As far as staying at an Airbnb, I have stayed at five different locations. The first one was wonderful, but other guests have ruined it so it’s not listed anymore. One of them was nothing like the pictures and the other one had a host that actually lived upstairs and came to visit several times. (Not ok) i’m not a huge fan. I think I’ll stay with the hotels.

review_title: No what it used to be
review_text: Airbnb used to be my go to place for a holiday. You could stay in some lovely places for a reasonable fee.  However over the years I’ve noticed that the Airbnb service fee plus the cleaning fee has become disproportionate. I’ve just looked to book a week and the Airbnb charges on top of the price of the accommodation adds an additional thousand pounds, it’s just not cost-effective anymore. I think Airbnb have become greedy and they will price themselves out of the market. i’ve previously queried the cleaning fee with some hosts as their accommodations standard of cleanliness didn’t warrant an excessive cleaning fee, only to discover that the host doesn’t even get the cleaning fee.

review_title: Loss of super hosting status due to not selling more than 10 trips a year despite 5*. Madness!
review_text: Well well I knew they were not popular in certain quarters but these ratings says it all. I am writing as a host though I have used them many times as a guest too. Airbnb look after themselves and only themselves! Sound familiar? Sure I’ve heard that in the news about someone else recently 🤣. They have recently removed our super host rating for no good reason. Their thinking is that now we have dropped from 4 to one property with only a summer season to let ( ie 12 weeks or so) we do not meet their silly criteria anymore whereby one must rent more than 10 visits (1 day or 2 weeks makes no odds) per year. Our Villa is sold out all summer mostly by Airbnb but many bookings are 2 or 3 weeks so we don’t meet their target! 5* or not, (we actually had 5* on all our properties until we sold them short while ago) we no longer qualify. How crazy is that? Won’t be with them for much longer me thinks, especially in view of these customer ratings it looks like there is little point anyway. Shame, was once a good company.

review_title: Not the best experiences
review_text: I have stayed in a couple of properties but they were not the best.  I still have some future reservations so who knows?  I have just received a cancellation for a room booked in Naples in May, i now have to find alternative accommodation, so this has finally convinced me to go back to Booking.com.  I know they are not perfect, but i have had good experiences with them and found them fair to deal with.

review_title: Review removed after refund
review_text: While all previous rentals have been good and some very good, I had one recent bad experience for which I got a partial refund.  However, my review was removed (HM9XAHN5T2) creating false ratings for this bad host.

review_title: Safety concerns are deleted from reviews
review_text: I have been using Airbnb for over 9 years and the first time I had a horrible experience with a unit I left a review warning of the place being shared with a daycare and the locks on the door didnt work so kids could easily open them. The owner of the property tried to bribe me yet because I responded saying I would add on my review that they claimed to have fixed all the issues, Airbnb sided with the owners saying I was trying to bribe them.

review_title: What a stupid rule to have only 14 days…
review_text: What a stupid rule to have only 14 days to write the review! We had actually very nice host but I really had no time to look at those emails. That's quite disappointing.

review_title: Platform itself is easy to use but the…
review_text: Platform itself is easy to use but the rules that are set up make it challenging from host to host. We enjoy non hotel trips still. Costs are starting to even it though.

review_title: Customer service helped me get partial…
review_text: Customer service helped me get partial refund after an absolute dreadful stay in Kranjska Gora, Slovenia. Years ago I used to have nothing but good experiences at Airbnb stays but lately it has become obvious that there is just zero regulations. Hosts can get away with a lot and it's not ok. Luckily I managed to get back 30% of my money. Honestly I don't think I'd stay at another Airbnb again I think it's just too risky. The place I last stayed at was absolutely disgusting. But the customer service people went above and beyond to help me and I'm actually extremely impressed with them and their efforts. They called me moments after contacting them out of hours and we spoke on the phone. If only the hosts had more regulations!

review_title: Disappointing stay
review_text: Disappointing stay.  The property wasn't as described in the listing.  Pictures were misleading and the cleanliness was subpar.  Communication with the host was also difficult. Wouldn't recommend.

review_title: Dreadful experience
review_text: Dreadful experience.  The property wasn't as described in the listing, and communication with the host was difficult.  Wouldn't recommend.

review_title: Airbnb a double edge sword for the host
review_text: After spending thousands of dollars on setting up an apartment we have in our home we listed it with Airbnb. After the first several days, we were getting consistent bookings until one day. We got a booking on dates that we had blocked out on the calendar on the Airbnb site, which caused a conflict and no matter how we communicated to the people that were seeking the reservation, we were unable to contact the people, whether it was a problem through Airbnb or the people ignoring the message. The first time it was stated by the customer service on Airbnb that we had a switch turned on that allowed for automatic confirmation of bookings, which I explicitly had gone into the settings and turned off and when I explained it to them, they said that they wanted to go into the settings with me and turn it off while we were on the phone to be certain that it doesn’t occur again And that’s exactly what we did. After receiving numerous notifications of confirmations that we had not made, we contacted the company again and they told us it was an internal error and that they would correct the situation however, it will eventually cause us to have very low ratings and not be able to rent our apartment through Airbnb and they took no interest in that part of my concern. The next thing that I was trying to address was when I ask what country my call to Airbnb is being transferred to they flat out refuse, even though it’s very obvious that it is being routed through India, of which they refuse to admit that the call is going to India and they claim that they’re not allowed to tell us which is against the United States laws that they must tell The person who requests where the call is being routed by US law, but they continue to refuse. I have found in my short time that Airbnb does not care about the people who host on their site. They care about getting their money from their cut of the reservations and they redirect our calls through India even though many times the people on the phone from India are very in polite and do not listen and they talk through you and refuse to answer questions. It is becoming very very evident that I must list my apartment, which is very very nicely furnished, and everyone is overly happy with our hospitality, and I must list it dozens of other places because Airbnb has fallen off. It’s reputation drastically in a short period of time. The owner must be a trillionaire , but he’s fallen asleep at the switch and just living on the royalties I imagine.

review_title: Airbnb lets host down
review_text: we have hosted on airbnb for almost 9 years and have 4.95, superhost rating. Yet a guest recently claimed the accommodation was "unacceptable" supported by photos of hard water stains in the kettle and shower. This enabled them to escape their 1 week booking commitment and get full refund - and at 8.30pm they clearly had alternative (probably with family) accommodation ready. Airbnb's handling was aggressive, citing that there would be "consequences" if we didnt refund despite years of delighted guests.

review_title: Good Stay
review_text: Good Stay, But Airbnb’s Platform Could Improve I booked a weekend stay in a downtown apartment through Airbnb in April 2025. The place was clean and matched the description, and the host was friendly enough, responding to my check-in questions within a few hours. However, the booking process was frustrating—the app glitched when I tried to confirm my dates, and I had to contact Airbnb support to fix it. Their customer service was polite but took two days to resolve the issue, which was stressful so close to my trip. The stay itself was fine, but Airbnb needs to make their platform more reliable and responsive.

review_title: I have been a host off and on since…
review_text: I have been a host off and on since 2020--right when COVID hit. I sold that house with the attached apt and really had no issues with guests or the site. The next time I was a host, I had issues from day one! If it weren't for the necessity of the extra income, I would not deal with this hassle. Most of my guest really are great! Then I get those that want Michelin quality on soup kitchen price. I live in my home and rent a room (rented both spare rooms for over a year with minimal issues). But lately, they are not host supportive. Guest lie about the space and they take the guest word even when they contradict themselves! No one reads the listing, show up and make demands of things I have no control over or complain of things listed in the description. They put on a happy 'I love the place face' and then tear the place down with the review.  It's only to get a discount or free stay--they know the key words to use for this when they talk to the site. As a guest, I have traveled a few places and  only once did I have an issue, took photos of dirt, bugs and even had the agent on the site agree they mislead where the location was. But that time, they took the hosts side! There is no rhyme or reason.

review_title: The experience using on website is…
review_text: The experience using on website is good, nothing to complain. However, the overall experience is not so good as we expect. There is no coupon to apply on rents and get a better price. Regardeless anything: experience, UI, referral program, etc, Airbnb only care to their profits and nothing else.

review_title: I Airbnb ignores my discrimination report against a host
review_text: I submitted an official complaint to Airbnb about a host named Scott who made discriminatory, offensive, and humiliating comments toward me. He refused to rent his property to me solely because I speak Russian. He questioned whether I truly live in the U.S., even though I have been living here for 7 years and my identity is fully verified on Airbnb. Worse, he mocked the way I spelled my own name and added a sarcastic “ha-ha” — clearly ridiculing and disrespecting me in the conversation. I attached screenshots and submitted the complaint through Airbnb’s official channels. Days have passed, and I still haven’t received any response. Complete silence. I expected Airbnb to take discrimination and xenophobia seriously, but it seems like they’re turning a blind eye. For a platform that claims to be built on inclusivity, safety, and trust, this is deeply disappointing. No follow-up. No apology. No accountability. I’m extremely disappointed and feel unsupported as a long-time Airbnb user. I hope someone from Airbnb actually pays attention to this review.

review_title: Mostly good experiences
review_text: Mostly good experiences, but some hosts cancel last minute. The app is easy to use, but customer service isn’t always helpful.

review_title: Airbnb lost its soul
review_text: I’ve used airbnb for many years as a guest in different countries. I was also a host for a few years. Mostly it’s been great, good opportuniites to stay cheaper than hotels and in areas less touristic. Also getting to know people I’d never met otherwhise. A few problems has occured but I can handle that. Recently I’ve had a few issues with bookings and with login and contacted the support team. It’s not been easy and it’s taken a long time to resolve, with messages and phone calls, sometimes confusing what the issue actually is, to some call center in perhaps Bangla Desh or somewhere around there. They’re doing their best I suppose. I just feel airbnb and the idea of what airbnb were standing up for is really unfortunately lost. I do still book rooms through airbnb anyway, because I can usually find cheap places and occationally have valuable encounters with hosts…

review_title: Availability is not always as it seems and vouchers complicate
review_text: I had a problem as airbnb were advertising a property as available but when I booked it did not go through, although I had paid upfront with Blue Light Card vouchers.  Customer service is time consuming, and not the most helpful responses initially.  If you use vouchers they make you pay more deposit and then when things go wrong it is hard to resolve, although eventually it was sorted out.

review_title: Not Too Shabby for First-Timers…
review_text: It was our one and only experience with AirBnb thus far from a few months ago, and while we’ve staved off of utilizing them for years - there really wasn’t much of a choice in one of our trips recently due to the secluded destination we were traveling to as well as the high season for fall foliage. Most hotels were booked to the max and we had extremely limited options and decided to chance it with one of the properties offered on AirBnB. What I thoroughly enjoyed as a tough customer was the reviews provided per property in order to make a sound decision. Sure, I’m not going to take each and every review into consideration if they come off as unreasonable and/or silly but plenty of times low ratings are there for a reason, and especially when folks spend their hard-earned cash to have a good vacation and precious time with their loved ones. After much poring of reviews and accumulated time reviewing various properties, we finally settled on one and luckily it did not disappoint! The property was even better in person and the housecleaning was immaculate. We had no need for further assistance until after the trip, but other than that - for the two nights we’ve spent, we’ve had no complaints. We did leave a camping blanket behind by accident when we left the property and after much back and forth with the owner, we’ve soon realized it was a hassle to even get it shipped. We won’t rule out AirBnb in the future since we are dealing with individual folks but all in all, we can only rate it as neutral for the time being since it was our first experience. We’re not planning on making it into a habit because plenty of mishaps can go awry with vacation rentals like these and who has the time for that? Based on the endless reviews all across the Internet of negative experiences with AirBnb, we are still wary with choosing them whenever we travel. We have and always will stick with mainly hotels as our first option.

review_title: Reviews by guests, lots of lies
review_text: I have loved Airbnb on the whole it is just the review system that has ruined it for me. The review system is ridiculous for hosts. There are nasty people, con artists, or guests just looking to get a refund by lying about the condition, so it stands to reason that at some point, these people will leave bad reviews, and there is nothing you as a host can do about it. Plus, I had 15 5 stars in a row, and my overall score did not change. One bad review, and you are down a point. Most guests were fine but some I considered sueing for defamation. I am Leaving Airbnb soon for the above reasons. Also, one guest gave us a 5 for all areas but a 4 overall when questioned he said 'I never give a 5 to anyone' so we get marked down for that nonsense!!!

review_title: 5 stars, really!
review_text: Last home we stayed in has beautiful, comfortable furniture but unfortunately infested with Asian beetles! Communication with these people? We had to call them 1/2 hour before arrival to get entry info. During this call the lady tells us she was at the home 8 hours earlier vacuuming up the beetles and that there might be a few bugs there when we get there, a few bugs my rear end!! Lady, why didn’t you call us at that point? The stay before that we get a messsge 2 days before we leave on a 1250 mile  trip we might see some pine beetles which in reality were cockroaches, and we might need to change our plans, are you kidding me?! Funny thing was, the people that stayed before us had a wonderful experience, the place was clean and comfortable and just everything you would want to hear! I don’t get it. We’ve been staying in air BnB 12 plus years but we are so done with them! Oh by the way, you gotta love the hosts that have their dog in their family icon picture and then tell you “ no pets allowed “, that makes me feel welcome, NOT! These stays were in Minnesota 10-20/27 and Missouri 10-28-24.

review_title: AIR BNB IN New Orleans 170 St Thomas St
review_text: Not a ding for the actual Airbnb app, but a ding for the treatment by the owner after the stay. We stayed in a beautiful home in NOLA for a week. No issues with the home itself, but after leaving the home, (we stayed at a hotel for 2 days after while still in town), I inadvertantly left behind property  in a bedroom drawer (Samsung Pixel earpods, portable cellphone charger, RayBan prescription eyeglasses, RayBan sunglasses). Owner would not let us return to the home to collect items becuase it was already occupied? They first said they did not find any proeprty, and then claimed they only found the eyeglasses which I had to describe, and said it would  cost $100 to mail them back to me in California. I understand it was my mistake for leaving property behind, but there is no way the home was occupied 2 hours after we left. I have a relative who said she would go pick up the items for me and at first the owner said yes, then a couple of days later (they would not respond to text messages or phone calls) said no because it was a security risk and they could only mail them to me. I know they took the missing items and It will cost me hundreds of dollars to replace everything but lesson learned, keep everything in my suitcase from now on!! So angry!

review_title: Website bugs
review_text: Having constant issues with their website sending my guests the wrong address. Called them to sort it, it’s showing correct on website, but sending wrong address to ppl. I update arrival guide information weeks ago and guests are still being sent the wrong thing. Meaning they can’t find the place. The website itself is causing bad reviews. It’s hard to navigate, the information is all over the place. I did start getting bookings right away which is great. But I need instant updates when I edit stuff to give my guests a better experience.

review_title: Dubious listings
review_text: I have used Airbnb regularly for several years and stayed at excellent places at good prices.  However it seems that increasingly there are dubious listings.  A very common one is for a property which is listed as available to not be be available when you try to reserve it.  The host then tries to offer an alternative ‘off-App’. I haven’t gone down this route but the concerns are obvious.  AirBnB needs to sort this

review_title: Host attempted to cancel 6 hours before check in
review_text: I’ve just had a horrific experience with an Airbnb host. Was basically told she had to cancel my booking just 6 hours before our scheduled check in. By that time of course we were already on our way. In the end, it all got sorted but undue stress was already caused. Airbnb support actually stepped in and helped tremendously. I just don’t think I’ll be using Airbnb again after this though as the experience has really shaken me up especially that I was travelling with small children and to be told we potentially did not have a place to stay for the night was very stressful!

review_title: Do not use gift vouchers unless paying for booking in one payment
review_text: Booked a holiday with £527 due now and £527 due later. Paid £500 with gift vouchers but instead of £27 being the outstanding amount they now wanted £277. Queried it as thought it was an error but no they take the gift vouchers of the total balance and then divide it into two payments and think it is ok to do this as it is in our terms and conditions. I feel robbed by them and know of no other company who treats gift cards differently to card payments. UPDATE Changed from 1 star as Airbnb have now contacted me to resolve but only 3 stars as the warning still applies.

review_title: Disappointing customer service
review_text: I have stayed over the years in multiple AirBnB apartments and in most cases things have worked out well. Last week we came to our booked property which had a misleading info on the listing which didn’t match the reality (1 less bathroom) + bedrooms with windows facing an underground „patio“ with plastic ceiling- dark and with no fresh oxygen entering. We immediately complained and wanted to move out but as other reviews said: i had to explain and write the issue 7+ times to different people. Resolution came after we had left the property and we got compensated only approx. 20% of the value as a compensation for the discomfort. The policy aircover which is supposed to handle such issues was not mentioned and the host‘s false listing info is still there.

review_title: Airbnb Customer Service is terrible
review_text: Airbnb is only getting three stars because of the places I have stayed and their hosts.  Otherwise, their customer support would get a 0.  No matter how many times you call about the SAME issue, they are unable to relay what you have been calling about, so you are forced to reiterate the problem.  Also, they tell you they will call you back and never do!!  So you have to call back and then explain to that person your issue AGAIN.  FIX THIS AIRBNB

review_title: I have to give half way stars on this…
review_text: I have to give half way stars on this company because I had to cancel the remaining of a trip after one day due to plans changing and I did get the problem resolved quickly by AIRBNB and already received a refund quickly with no hassle from the company itself. My complaint is that the hosts of the homes where I have stayed seem to want to vent about their financial situations and are quick to ask you to move in with them for long term or permanent because they are mostly over living their financial means and see you as a bank to support them rather than a guest in their home. I do not want the pressure of someone begging for money and that's what it is. I suggest people doing AIRBNB to make extra income start using their profits for necessary things instead of throwing away what they make and trying to live in a house that's not in the rich area and trying to keep up with the Joneses next door to impress them because if you are a host spending that money on your week family vacation instead of doing repairs to your house.. that's really not my problem.

review_title: A pretty good user experience
review_text: A pretty good user experience, this is my first time using Airbnb, it was fairly simple to navigate the site but is getting to be a frustrating experience. The charges are somewhat ridiculous though, I understand you have to make money but seriously $600 for a platform fee?

review_title: I just got started on it and posted my…
review_text: I just got started on it and posted my listing yesterday. Its still not online though. I verified everything and they say it can take up to 24 hrs for the link to be online and working... kinda complicated to post a listing in my opinion...

review_title: AirBNB hounded us for furniture damage we didn't cause
review_text: My partner and I just spent 9 nights in Mexico City at an AirBNB in a very nice centrally located neighborhood. The design and all the household appliances were very modern and convenient. The water was clean and didn't impart any infectious microbes. At the time the city was having widespread water shortages and water cleanliness problems. It was a very enjoyable stay... except for one thing: there were two wicker folding chairs positioned near a small table in the kitchen. At the beginning of our stay we noticed one of the chairs had a back that was unattached at the bottom such that it was swinging. A couple of days later I realized that the chair was making a cracking sound when I sat on it, but it didn't feel wobbly. However, soon I noticed that there were small pieces of wicker on the floor.  I took a closer look at the chair and it looked like someone had but their knee part way through the seat of the chair. It was clearly damaged. This was now near the end of our stay. I realized that I should have reported this damage at the beginning of our stay. I didn't put my knee through the chair. I didn't notice the extent of the damage earlier because of being distracted by being on an enjoyable vacation. Shortly after we moved out of the AirBNB, AirBNB asked us to  pay about $200. My partner explained that the damage to the chair occurred before we arrived. The consequence was that AirBNB constantly hounded us for $$. And my partner clearly explained how the damage occurred before our stay to no avail. I will not book any further stays in AirBNB.

review_title: Visited a property on the Isle of Arran…
review_text: Visited a property on the Isle of Arran in Scotland.  What we found an absolute rip-off was the cleaning charge made by the host. We were there for two night and charged £125 for cleaning which amounted to 45% of the total bill ! Adding insult to injury the host expected us to strip the beds, wash up all the plates and dishes and put them back in the cupboards and if we had a pet to vac the floors.  Puts one off Airbnb.  If ever I have to use the service again I will look carefully for this blatant way of money grabbing. Post script 04/04/2024 No reply from Airbnb so obviously they condone this rip-off.  Once bitten twice shy from now on !

review_title: i have had a terrible experience on my…
review_text: i have had a terrible experience on my recent trip to miami, as the plane landed, i checked my e mail to see that they had cancelled due to a plumbing problem & the children there, i was offered another accomodation & asked if i agree, without looking at the images i replied yes, as i had to stay somewhere (not on the street) anyway i checked the address where i should  have stayed, believe it or not, it was a fake address, didnt exsist, to be fair  airbnb investigated and agreed and delisted the property,

review_title: Cumbersome proces, but Airbnb revanched
review_text: Update. See below my frustration. But now at the end Airbnb aplogised and assured us that everything would be ok. So after all (and a lot of energy and frustration) things seem to work out all fine. I would love to assist Airbnb to streamline these processes better, avoiding bad customer experience and waste of spilled money. These were my frustrations: My experience was that reschedule a booking means: - No professional email communication; you don't get the requested confirmation. - Communication too late. - You cannot act on behalf, even if you have all information. - The system rules and if it doesn't work it is my fault. - Callcenter help, that only follow the very rigid strict rules. - Very short payment terms, that will make it impossible to fix any bumps in their iron process. In short we were not able to reschedule, and had paid extra for that. Most of the money is gone now, without any wanted booking. So be warned: think careful when booking at Airbnb that you have the right appartment at the designated period.

review_title: Technical service to Host lacks urgency
review_text: A business is judged not when everything is working fine; but how the business responds when there is a problem. When I have had several technical issues, the lack of clear communication and urgency in the matter was especially lacking. The latest issue is where I had a reservation who wanted to add a day to their existing reservation. That day was definitely not blocked but neither the guest or I could add it to the reservation without a error message. When speaking with support, they indicated it was blocked. But it was not blocked. Then they said it would take at least 2 to 3 days for engineering to fix this simple issue. Also they would not connect me with the individual or department that was working the issue. If you are not going to have urgency, you can at least provide transparency.

review_title: Cheeky
review_text: Have travelled several times with AirBnB   Overall good experience. About to travel again but they have increased their service fee in addition to the cleaning fee.  In addition This morning i received an email to tell me that the service fee will now have an extra 2% currency charge. I immediately wrote and said I will pay in the currency preference of the host but this is not possible - I have to pay the fee to them

review_title: Not bad
review_text: Not bad, worse than booking!

review_title: Had a dissapointing experience
review_text: I have been using Airbnb for 6 years and have never written a negative review. Recently while vacationing in Spain, we had a negative experience with a superhost. I reviewed the apartment and host with factual information on our stay. Five days after my review posted, Airbnb removed it. I believe the host filed a complaint and Airbnb took her side. However, I gave only factual details regarding uncleanliness, uncomfortability of beds and nonexistent free street parking. I was told that my review is not relevant in assisting other renters but of course if I had read the review I probably would not have booked this apartment. I now have to wonder how many other negative reviews are removed and why they would allow a host to misrepresent their house/ apartment. I will be hesitant to use Airbnb in the future.

review_title: I have used AirBnB for years with…
review_text: 06/06/23: Recent experiences as a guest have begun to change my view of the company. Its service is deteriorating, despite the fact that I have paid thousands of pounds in service fees and have 50 positive reviews from hosts, every time I look for support from Airbnb they side with the host and completely fail to address my issue. 16/12/23: I have used AirBnB for years with around 60 different hosts all around the world. In all of this I have only had three problem rentals, of which I left one early. Overall, my experience has been great, though as with any company there is always room for improvement.

review_title: Amenities missing, sketchy photos

But they seriously should pay more attention the the photos vs reality issue. There was one bed missing from what they told us and some amenities were broken. We had no AC, in July!!!! Anyway, 2.5/5

review_title: I had some nice stays with Airbnb but…
review_text: I had some nice stays with Airbnb but it’s definitely unreliable. The host can cancel several days before arrival and get away with ZERO penalties. Happened to me many times. By doing so they encourage hosts to cancel for no reason ruining travelers’ plans. They need to make hosts to be responsible by applying penalties for their cancellations! Because now it’s like “I decided to throw a party at my apartment this Friday and there’s your booking on the way. So I’ll just cancel it”. Very unreliable service for sure.

review_title: Using Airbnb less..
review_text: I've had a lot of good Airbnb experiences and a couple that were not so good. Generally, I think their level of customer service is very good. The problem I have is with the App. They keep adding more features that make it more difficult to search. Their search algorithm is flawed. Instead of showing you everything that is available, it shows you only the places it thinks you want to see based on your search history. I'm starting to use another accommodation site simply because the Airbnb app is so much less user friendly than it was.

review_title: Opinion of Super host about Airbnb
review_text: We are Super host with Airbnb for 4 years. However, our hosting experience is much more. We became disillusioned about Airbnb  in our first year . They are pretty much on a side of customers - the one who pays, order the music. However, we are also paying, may be not as much as holidaymakers, but we do. And we are the one who makes the whole business exist. Some customers giving their opinions like they came not to enjoy their holidays, but to make some kind of inspection of your property. Forgetting about how much they would get in the hotel for the same money: entrance, kitchen, sitting and a bed room all in one. Usually the customers who are no good  themselves will complain more then anyone and give you 4* or even 3*. Then you are trying to contact Airbnb and explain your side of story to the so called 'Support Staff'. However, you will get no action from  them. These people don't have any authority, power or wish to do anything. They will pass you to each other like a football and that is it. The most irritating thing about Airbnb is that they are very quick to reduce your rates, then try to raise them up. It will take forever to go one point up. In this way they are trying to bend you to their will. You have to lick customers from top to the bottom, close your eyes on everything they are doing wrong, smile no matter what and jump out of your skin to please them. Really..? I don't think so. Airbnb forgets that they are only agents between hosts and holidaymakers. It is a time to say 'Good buy'.

review_title: Some bad reviews are not posted by…
review_text: Some bad reviews are not posted by owners or host. Do not place hidden cameras in your homes respect everyone’s privacy we have felt someone watching and have found small hidden devices that look like they have a camera. Love some of the hidden jewels on this site. Most host are are friendly.

review_title: Extra fees which were not disclosed at booking, but no help from Airbnb
review_text: Our host turned out to be a large third party provider (BelVilla) who wanted to charge us extra fees in cash (!) at the time of check-in. These fees had not been disclosed at the time of booking and thus were clearly violating the Airbnb rules. Nevertheless, Airbnb did not help us, but rather drowned us with useless, generic responses. We cancelled the reservation and did not receive a refund. Airbnb did not make any effort to challenge the host for charging additional fees nor to compensate us for our loss. 7/11/23: In response to my complaint, Airbnb now refunded my downpayment and they will investigate BelVilla's additional fees. I now feel much better about Airbnb's customer protection and added 2 stars to my evaluation

review_title: Poor experience
review_text: We stay in self catering accommodation a lot. I try and use local property agents to book and have never before had reason to complain nor request a refund. Because Air B and B doesn't do grading or even check listing is true everything is left to the reviews, with a maximum number of characters, to describe the property. We were very disappointed with our recent stay and, put simply, the two major issues would, I'm sure, not happen with a traditional agent as almost no cooking equipment and, in one room, window curtains/blinds weren't provided. It impacted our stay and Air b and b did provide a standard calculated small refund but our stay was a disappointment. When you use valuable holiday days booking somewhere you want to know you can really trust the listing. I don't really want a refund I want the stuff to be there as described so I can enjoy my break. Basically the place we stayed in seemed like a long term renter had done a runner so a few furnishings were bought and it was listed on Air b and b quickly in hope some sucker would trust the listing and stay. Anyway, we've now given our fair review and I guess it will be published at some point. Can't see us ever using air b and b again though.

review_title: Airbnb not posting negative reviews
review_text: In September of 2022, we stayed in a magical treehouse in California.   The treehouse had no insulation and we were extremely cold.  The temperature dropped to the low 50's, inside the treehouse it was maybe in the 40's, and it started to rain.   We were dressed in layers and had blankets, but we were still cold.   The lighting in the treehouse was inefficient and since it was in the trees, it was pretty dark.   Needless to say, we left and stayed in a hotel. I wrote an honest review that had many well-deserved negatives in it and Airbnb removed it.   I contacted Airbnb several times to find out what I had written to warrant the removal.  Needless to say, I never received a response as to the exact reason. This practice of removing honest reviews is deceitful.   Had there been other negative reviews posted, we would have never stayed in this treehouse.

review_title: Airbnb hosts in Ukraine are being punished
review_text: Do you remember how Airbnb helped mediate donations for Ukraine at the beginning of the war? They removed commissions and helped hosts receive donations through their platform. It was a nice gesture, but unfortunately, their actions since then have been a huge disappointment. Instead of supporting hosts with their dwindling income, Airbnb has blocked new listings in Ukraine and delisted apartments in non-occupied parts of the country that are claimed by Russia. It seems like Putin has a say even on territories that are not occupied, such as Zaporizhia. As a host, I have been experiencing the negative impacts of these decisions by Airbnb. Here are some examples: 1. Inability to list new properties: I bought and renovated two apartments in Kyiv downtown and Kharkiv before the war. However, I cannot list either of them as Airbnb always responds with “New listings in Ukraine are blocked.” When I contacted Airbnb support, they cited “sanctions” as the reason. I was confused since Ukraine is not sanctioned, but the support person clarified that it was due to “platform rules”. What rules are these that punish hosts for merely being located in Ukraine? 2. Delisted old properties: My apartment in Zaporizhia, which had good demand during the war from journalists and military personnel, was suddenly delisted by Airbnb after Putin claimed the entire region. Although his army never managed to take the city of Zaporizhia, Airbnb still punished their hosts for having property in the area. How is that helping anyone or keeping Airbnb safe? Aircover doesn’t insure against bombs, only compensating for problems caused by guests or hosts. Therefore, it is irrelevant in this case. These decisions have had a significant impact on hosts like myself. The income that I could have used to support my country's fight against the enemy by donating to volunteers and the military is no longer available. Furthermore, being a “superhost” requires maintaining high ratings, which involves a lot of cleaning, check-ins, and ensuring that guests are satisfied. Although I am grateful to Airbnb for ceasing operations in Russia, I implore them to take action so that Ukrainian hosts can have their income and support their country. Airbnb should re-enable new listings in Ukraine and re-list the delisted properties, just like they did at the beginning of the war when they were helping with donations. PS: If anyone knows anyone who works at Airbnb and can relay this message to the leadership, please spread the word.
