review_title: Beware of the “golden badge on Airbnb
review_text: Beware of the “golden badge on Airbnb: my experience as a host with 4 properties I used to trust Airbnb’s algorithm that assigns the well-known golden badge to listings marked as “guest favorites,” with a percentage showing how they rank compared to others. As a traveler, I often picked listings based on that badge, thinking it was a reliable sign of quality. But now, as a host with years of experience and four different properties listed on the platform, I’ve started to question it—and honestly, I’ve changed my mind. My best-performing listing, a beautiful apartment with a sea view, high-end interiors, an amazing location, glowing 5-star reviews, and a consistently high booking rate… no longer has the golden badge. Meanwhile, my other listings— beautiful as well, same location, same place, in a top position as well, but less popular, no sea view, —still have the badge. This has led me to a simple but disappointing conclusion: the algorithm is not reliable. As someone who manages multiple listings, I’ve been able to compare them directly, and I can confidently say that whether or not a listing has the badge doesn’t always reflect its actual quality or guest satisfaction. MY ADVICE as an experienced host: Don’t rely on the GOLDEN  badge to choose your vacation stay. Always read real REVIEWS, look at the photos, check the details of the home, and pay attention to how the host communicates. The algorithm can be wrong. Real guest experiences aren’t.

We booked this villa in July 2022 for our holiday in May 2023 for 18 days through Airbnb and paid 50% of the cost on booking. I contacted the host to inform them of our arrival time & requested instructions as to how we were going to get into the Villa. The host (Anna) responded to say she would contact us a week before with the details. Two weeks before we were due to fly out, the host cancelled. I can’t explain how upset we were. Not sure if this is a reflection of the owner or the Host, as they appear to be different people. Flights & car hire booked, we now needed accommodation, but at this late stage we were limited to what was still available. We eventually found an alternative but at an extra cost of over £1000! Two days after our booking was cancelled, we see the Villa is available on the exact dates we booked through “booking.com” at Over £900 more than we paid. This rental villa is advertised on several platforms so we are unsure if this is an error, however it wasn’t available for booking previous to our cancellation as I checked because of the several platform availability. review_title: Still the best
review_text: Still the best. I've been traveling for seven years as a nomad and it wouldn't be possible without Airbnb. Despite having some difficulties with the hosts, I still prefer to book using this platform. Some things that could be improved: a limited liability for the tenants with maximum of $100 - such as what they do on VRBO. After several intents I got to speak with an agent named Gabriela who was really attentive and full of intentions to provide the best care possible. After a thorough revision of the case she was able to assist and generate a discount coupon that has covered almost the whole price difference. Need to say that I also made some work to find another option which was not too high price and still available. In this case if you treat well and happen to speak with a good person, the outcome may be positive and quick. My advise: If you you have issues with AirBnb don't give up after the first try and try to call back again. Not all people, unfortunately do their job well and it's a bit of a lottery. review_title: In search of ‘a clean, well-lighted place.’
review_text: I moved to Dayton, for all intents and purposes, in January, 2022. From February 15 through October 10th, I used Airbnbs to have a place to work privately. I was helping my sister recuperate from a serious illness. My stays were great, for the most part. Yet my best stay was with a Host named Matthew. He lived in Long Beach, California, but had a wonderful place in Dayton. At first we couldn’t schedule a reservation, so I went to another Host named Leslie. She had an utterly amazing apartment in Dayton’s ‘Oregon District’. I was so relaxed and satisfied that I didn’t want to leave.  While there, the hot water heating system malfunctioned. No hot water.. I didn’t really care because I was so comfortable and Leslie had EVERYTHING under control, she had even arranged to reserve a second property she owned for hot showers!  This lady is a consummate hospitality professional! I stayed at Leslie’s apartment for a week and felt as if I had gone to Europe on holiday! I had a blast!   Next enters….Matthew Matthew promised to reserve an apartment he managed in September, but Airbnb went behind and booked it out from under me. I was livid. Yet Matthew was cool. We kept in touch and in late September we found dates AND availability. I reserved the entire apartment and waited for something to go wrong. On October 7th, I reserved, paid up front and was about to call a ride share when I saw that the date he reserved was THREE DAYS AWAY!! What was I supposed to do?! I had given notice of Checkout at my current location. There was nothing I could do! But blame….you know..MATTHEW… I wanted to cuss him out. So I called him and when he answered, I barraged him. He remained calm, never raised his voice and all I could feel was embarrassed… He talked me offa the ledge and  encouraged me to look forward to Monday, the day of my reservation. When the conversation was done, I wondered why I didn’t cuss him out like I had planned. It was because Matthew was a professional AND a gentleman. I had to respect such a guy! I moved onto the apartment on October 10th. When I walked into the apartment, I couldn’t believe my eyes! The place looked EXACTLY like the photos on the Airbnb site. Everything was in place. There was even a brand new Keurig! The place was immaculate! I was there for about thirty memorable days and nights. During that time I had NO PROBLEMS. Matthew called once, but I’m SURE he knew that it was all good. He’s just ‘cool like that’!  I’ll never forget that ‘spot’…. Nor will I forget the Host that gave me a reason to BOAST!

After a flight and dragging my suitcase around, it wasn’t the smoothest start to a trip. In the end, I got into the apartment, and the stay itself was okay, but the first impression was already spoiled. The platform works well technically, but since so much depends on the host, the experience can vary a lot. I’ll probably use it again, but I’ll be more careful with who I book from next time.

review_text: As an accommodation provider who recently terminated their contract with Expedia after nearly 10 years I advise against using this company.  Expedia have made contacting guests with crucial pre-arrival information almost impossible.  They now withhold guest contact numbers, in addition to email addresses and postal addresses.  All communication with guests must be via their messaging service which is not fit for purpose.  Firstly, many guests do not read messages sent via the Expedia messaging service.  Previously accommodation providers could phone or text guests to signpost them to the messages.  Many guests also really value this direct contact with their accommodation.  Secondly, many Expedia bookings are made via affiliate, fourth party websites.  All messages then go to the fourth party, who usually do not forward them to the guest.  Expedia claims this issue with affiliate fourth parties no longer happens, but it does.  If you're happy to book via Expedia and risk not receiving crucial pre-arrival information, ultimately putting your booking at risk, by all means go ahead.  Alternatively, book directly with your accommodation provider where you get direct contact and quite often a better deal.

Instead of helping resolve issues, they immediately shift the blame onto the other company involved and leave customers stuck in the middle trying to figure things out on their own. During a very stressful travel situation involving a delayed flight and a prepaid rental car reservation, Expedia was extremely difficult to deal with. It was almost impossible to quickly reach a live representative when I actually needed help. In stressful travel moments, the last thing customers need is to be forced into endless automated systems and chat messaging. What made the situation worse was being pushed to communicate mainly through written chat instead of being able to directly speak to someone over the phone. Sometimes customers need real-time support, clarification on policies, or simply someone willing to help troubleshoot the situation. Instead, the process felt cold, robotic, and unhelpful. Customer service should be about helping people navigate problems, especially when travel disruptions happen. Unfortunately, Expedia made an already stressful situation even more overwhelming. I would strongly encourage travelers to think carefully before booking through a third-party company that does not take ownership when issues arise.

review_text: Wish there was a negative star rating! Based on the photos provided on Expedia, I booked a two-night stay at a property. Upon arrival, the exterior was poorly maintained with overgrown weeds, open windows, and outdated interiors visible from the street. Because safety and cleanliness are my top priorities, I asked to see the rooms before official check-in. Both the first-floor room and the supposedly "updated" second-floor room were entirely unacceptable, neglected, and looked nothing like the advertised photos. I immediately informed the front desk that I would not be staying and requested a cancellation. The staff member explicitly confirmed it was canceled and told me I was "all set." Despite this explicit confirmation, Expedia only refunded me for one night. Their excuse? They claimed the cancellation "missed the deadline"—which is an absolute impossibility, considering the booking itself was made after that arbitrary deadline had already passed. To make matters worse, Expedia's customer service has been a joke. They sent templated emails claiming they attempted to call me but couldn't get through due to "business hours," which is completely false. It’s just a broken back-and-forth designed to wear consumers down so they give up. I refused to stay at the establishment, I am actively disputing the remaining charges with my credit card company, and I will never use Expedia again. They take advantage of consumers with deceptive marketing and predatory policies. Save yourself the headache and book elsewhere.

So I disputed the charges, which was the reasonable & correct reaction. I couldn’t believe how screwed up they are, to try to charge $1205 for flights that I never went on. I filed a claim with Travel Guard insurance and they tell me that they will not honor the claim because it's not a qualifying event. Now if the job involuntary transferred my wife 100 miles away, then they would cover it but we would need to get a NOTARIZED document from the employer. When I called Travel Guard to fight them, we were looking at two different policies. I was being proactive by booking early to get a better price and cancelling early to make sure I get my money back. Now they are sending me the correct policy because the one online is useless but for what, for me to make up a medical issue. I cannot say we got sick because they will respond by saying, "you will get better in four months." After reading the policy, they will not cover cancellations due to pregnancy or pre-existing medical conditions but rest assure, they will cover you if you get HIJACKED! Lunacy is what this is. Why does Expedia partner with companies like Frontier or Travel Guard. With the amount of business Expedia generates Frontier (because that is a crappy airline) they should waive fees for customers booking through Expedia. DO NOT EVER PURCHASE TRAVEL GUARD INSURANCE. So I reached out to Expedia three separate times because I am disconnected and my chat is reset when I'm inactive for less than a minute after waiting 30 of the 3-5 minutes for a response. When I finally did get through I was told that Expedia would not rebook me onto the flight because they had run out of economy seats because of the chat problems. So I tried (once again multiple times because I was reset or agents gave up and left the chat) to move my flight to another day so it was back to 16h (a move that Emirates confirmed is free from them). But poor Expedia could have lost out on the sale of those seats so they have refused to give me any alternative flight which Emirates are proving FOR FREE. I have wasted hours and lots of sleep going in circles trying to sort out my journey home and Expedia have made it as frustrating and difficult as possible while actively blocking me from making a free move offered by the airline because there is a small chance of them making a small amount of money off someone else. Would highly recommend if you enjoy hitting your head against walls for hours on end. Otherwise avoid like the plague and just book whatever you need directly through the provider While the disruption is due to troubles in the Middle East, the handling of my flights can in no way be blamed on that. They are caused by a mixture of an awful chat function, uninformed help agents and a mission to put potential profits before the promises made to existing customers.

review_title: Avoid Expedia for Car Rentals
review_text: Avoid Expedia for Car Rentals I am writing this to warn others about the deceptive practices involving **Expedia** and their partnership with **SurPrice Car Rental** at the Orlando International Airport (MCO). The Bait and Switch Expedia markets SurPrice with a "Good" rating, which is dangerously misleading given their "Poor" standing on TrustPilot and other consumer advocacy sites. I booked a reservation (73364237886296) that was explicitly listed as **"inclusive of all fees, taxes, and charges."** Furthermore, before my trip, I contacted Expedia directly and received confirmation that my personal insurance and credit card coverage would be accepted, with no additional charges due. The Reality at the Counter Upon arrival, the experience was a disaster: * **Insurance Extortion:** SurPrice refused to honor my transferable insurance policies or credit card coverage. They demanded I purchase their internal insurance at limits that are not only exorbitant but, in some cases, exceed legal requirements in Florida. * **Broken Transparency:** The link to SurPrice’s Terms and Conditions on Expedia’s site was—and still is—broken, making it impossible for a consumer to verify these "requirements" beforehand. * **Price Inflation:** My "all-inclusive" $57 rental was leveraged into a demand for nearly eight times that amount. ### Total Lack of Accountability Because of this refusal to honor the booked price, I was forced to abandon the reservation, pay for rideshares, and book a last-minute substitute with Avis. What was supposed to be a **$57** trip ended up costing me nearly **$400**. When I contacted Expedia to resolve this, they offered no satisfactory settlement or reimbursement for the financial hit I took due to their verified (and incorrect) information. It is negligent that Expedia continues to list SurPrice and similar entities like ZezGo despite known issues and broken documentation links. **Bottom Line:** Expedia’s "all-inclusive" guarantees are meaningless if they continue to partner with companies that use predatory tactics. Save yourself the stress and the money—book directly with a reputable carrier.

review_title: Expedia's Poor Booking System Cost Me $400 -
review_text: I'm writing this review to warn other travelers about a serious flaw in Expedia's booking system that resulted in an unexpected $400 charge during my recent trip. When booking my resort stay through Expedia, I carefully entered all required information including details about my daughter. However, Expedia's confirmation email was completely inadequate - it simply showed "1 child" with absolutely no indication of what age I had entered during the booking process. This became a nightmare at check-in. The resort staff informed me that the child's age in their system didn't match my daughter's actual age, and I was hit with a surprise $400 charge on the spot. The most frustrating part? I had no way to verify what information I had actually entered because Expedia's confirmation email provided zero details about the age. Here's what's wrong with this situation: **Expedia's System Failures:** - Confirmation emails lack essential booking details - No way for customers to verify entered information post-booking - Poor communication between Expedia and hotel partners - Zero proactive customer service to catch discrepancies **The Real Problem:** How can customers be held responsible for booking errors when Expedia doesn't even show us what we entered? Their confirmation system is so basic that it creates these exact scenarios where travelers get blindsided with extra charges. **My Recommendation:** Until Expedia fixes their confirmation system, take screenshots of EVERY page during booking, save all details, and call both Expedia and your hotel directly to verify all guest information before traveling. Don't trust their inadequate email confirmations. This experience has completely eroded my trust in Expedia. Other booking platforms provide detailed confirmations that actually help customers verify their reservations. Expedia needs to step up their game - this kind of system failure that costs customers hundreds of dollars is simply unacceptable. Save yourself the headache and book elsewhere

review_title: Expedia seems to be fine for booking…
review_text: Expedia seems to be fine for booking hotels, I've never had an issue with that, so they get 2 stars. However, I tried booking an activity through Expedia, and they screwed me over. I paid, but Expedia never sent me the barcode needed to get into the venue, so my "tickets" were useless. Now Expedia refuses to refund me the $85 I spent, even though it was their fault that I wasn't about to get in. Update:Expedia has refunded me, after several phone calls and chats with unhelpful reps

review_title: What a Mess
review_text: What a Mess!  I gave them 2 stars instead of 1 because they did eventually get everything straightened out but we went through a week of uncertainty and complications because of their unhelpful policies.  We try not to use booking sites but they outsmarted us on this one and we unintentionally used them to book at trip to Utah.  Within a couple of hours we realized the dates were wrong and this was probably our fault.  When we called to correct they won't talk to you about existing reservations and shunted us to an email system.  Something that should have been fixed in a few minutes took 4 emails from us and 3 from them over a period of a week and led to the hotel saying they had multiple reservations that they had to report as no-shows.  We had no idea what additional charges we would pay or not pay.  A giant mess that could have been avoided with prompt customer service.  In the future we will be extra careful to make sure we don't get hooked into using them by their deceptive websites and deceptive Google search results.

review_title: Don't Book 3rd Party Air Through Expedia
review_text: I've used Expedia to book hotels and those experiences have always been positive.  However, this time, I used Expedia to book airfare for a party of four on Aegean airlines.  We paid for extra legroom on our reservation, meaning we would be seated at the front of the plane (where we selected our seats).  When we went to check in to Aegean online, we were told we had to check in at the airport.  Upon doing so, we were given seats in rows with 24 and 25.  There was definitely NO extra legroom and our friends, who had selected aisle seats, were center seated.  Upon returning home, I contacted Expedia.  Was told to contact Aegean.  I have now been tossed back and forth between the two companies, with no resolution, for 6 weeks. My takeaway is that you should not book airfare (which is likely to have an issue) with a third party through Expedia.  They do not provide adequate customer support.  In fact, my last communication with them has gone completely unanswered.

review_title: Beware of false prices
review_text: Update: Expedia did reach out to us and give a partial refund around $81. We appreciate they did more than nothing, but we will still be careful of using their services in the future. Original: We booked a rental through Expedia with a total cost clearly shown as $187.49, including all taxes and fees. Upon arrival at Priceless Car Rental in Tampa, we were told we owed an additional $351.66 in "mandatory insurance" and other surprise charges. Our personal insurance was not accepted despite being valid, and we were forced into overpriced coverage. Expedia has been slow to respond and has not taken responsibility for misleading terms or for vetting a clearly predatory vendor with a history of similar complaints. We spoke to several other customers who had the same experience. Beware of opaque Expedia deals — and avoid Priceless Car Rental at all costs.

review_title: Don't bundle, book seperately
review_text: Frustrating Experience Booking Last-Minute Travel with Expedia My wife and I had to make urgent travel plans for a funeral and used Expedia to bundle hotel and car rental. We’re longtime members of both the hotel and rental car companies, but the Expedia booking didn’t link to our loyalty accounts. This meant we couldn’t manage or modify anything directly—only through Expedia’s call center, which was incredibly slow and unhelpful. During a stressful time and while dealing with flight delays, this lack of flexibility was agonizing. Expedia’s bundling may seem convenient, but if you’re in a hurry or need control over your itinerary, I strongly recommend booking directly with providers.⁸ —Andre

review_title: Negligence and abandonment
review_text: I booked through Expedia at the Park Pointe Hotel in San Francisco. Upon check-in, the hotel demanded a deposit of 100 USD that was never refunded, despite the fact that there was no damage or setback during the stay. The most serious thing is that Expedia totally ignores the matter, despite the fact that the reservation-itinerary: 73119031015417, was made on their platform and they promote that establishment. After complaining, they simply said that the issue of the deposit is between the client and the hotel, which is unacceptable. Why use a platform like Expedia if they are not even responsible for the hotels they promote? This type of practice completely unprotects the traveler and leaves a very negative precedent for those of us who use the platform in good faith. ❗ Beware of unreturned deposits. Expedia doesn't respond. *Return of my 100uSs, NOW!! *

review_title: A hotel booking made with Expedia UK…
review_text: A hotel booking made with Expedia UK with terms payment 50% on booking and 50% just before arrival. No charge arrived at my credit card for the first 50%. Some folk may consider this an unexpected bonus, but sadly I do not. Its a breach of agreed terms. Speaking with an Expedia Agent on their "Chat" service, they could not help as Hotel did not answer them. I raised complaint to ''support at chat.expedia.co.uk'' and 5 days later had received no acknowledgment or reply. Conclusion - dealing with Expedia is fine, unless something goes wrong or you need more information, in which case ... forget it

review_title: Misleading Photos, Poor Service, and Unreliable Bookings – My Disappointing Experience with Expedia
review_text: I am extremely disappointed with my recent experience booking through Expedia. The photos on their website did not accurately reflect what I received. When I booked, I was shown beautiful pictures of a room with an “ocean view,” but when I arrived, it was only a “partial view.” I contacted Expedia, and they told me that at the time of my booking, there was only one option available, even though they had two types of rooms. The photos were outdated and misleading, and they never updated them. To make matters worse, they then told the hotel that I made the wrong choice, even though the error was entirely theirs. Additionally, I had booked a shuttle through Expedia, trusting that they would provide a reliable service. However, I ended up waiting for 45 minutes, which is unacceptable for a company of Expedia’s size. I expected a wait time of no more than 20 minutes. This makes me question the value of booking through them, and I would recommend looking into local options instead.Expedia provided $25 refund that I can use on their website. Lastly, I booked a sunrise tour through Expedia. The communication between Expedia and the tour company was poor, and I ended up waiting alone on a dark street for two hours in the middle of the night because they didn’t send the driver. Although the tour company offered a free tour as compensation, Expedia only provided a refund, which doesn’t make up for the inconvenience, especially during a short vacation. Overall, I no longer trust Expedia. They seem more focused on making quick sales rather than providing quality service, and I would caution others to be careful when booking through them.

review_text: if you are using the 1 key cash program be aware of the fact that it is for hotels only not package deals  after 4 hours of phone calls. and chat finely got my refunds because i wanted to spend my earned rewards from this program     i will not use this site for flights as my Chase travel was 20% cheaper

review_text: I carefully set my local currency, but at some point later the website quietly changed it back to US$, so my tickets cost me more than I thought I was paying.  Maybe a website bug - but I feel I was cheated

review_title: xpedia sold me a flight + car package, then refused refund after provider canceled part of it
review_text: I booked a flight + car package through Expedia that included a 7-passenger vehicle. Later, I was informed that only a 5-seater was available, and eventually, the car rental provider canceled the reservation altogether—not me. Despite this, Expedia refused to refund the flight portion of the bundle, citing airline policy and ignoring the fact that the package was no longer delivered as sold. I spent days in support chats and was told there was “nothing more they could do.” By the time they offered to rebook the car, I had already started reorganizing my plans due to the delays. I'm simply asking for a full refund or penalty-free cancellation due to a supplier-side failure, not a change of mind. This experience left me frustrated and unsupported. I hope Expedia reconsiders how they handle broken packages and treats customers fairly when the issue is outside their control.

review_title: Unsympathetic cheapskates!
review_text: I booked a hotel in Glasgow in January for an awards' ceremony being held there on 28th March. My family arrived to be told our two junior suites had been cancelled and that nothing was available. After an hour's anxious wsit we were given downgraded rooms and managed to attend the event. I explained the trauma this had caused our daughter, who has special needs,and waited on Expedia's response. The first offer was £31. I laughed that off and reiterated the issues the cancellation had caused my daughter. Expedia responded with £71! Again I told Expedia that we expected more than just the difference in the price of our downgraded rooms.         I then spoke to the hotel in question. They told me they had instructed Expedia to compensate us at least half the costs, around £175! How cheap can you get, Expedia?

review_title: I have been waiting forever for them to…
review_text: I have been waiting forever for them to issue a refund back to my credit card. What is with the long delay? It's been like 2 weeks almost

review_title: Frustrating Experience with Expedia: Technical Glitches and Poor Customer Support
review_text: I was an Expedia Gold member for years before COVID, and recently opened their credit card. However, recent experiences with their lack of flexibility, technical glitches, and overall poor user experience are causing me to reconsider my loyalty. A few days ago, I tried using their Price Guarantee feature, but it wasn’t working properly. I kept receiving the message, "Apologies, something went wrong on our end. Please try submitting the form again." Despite trying multiple times throughout the day—especially since the price difference was over $200—I was unable to submit my claim. I took screenshots and copied the link for documentation. Yesterday, I tried again, but the issue persisted, and it was clear that Expedia hadn’t fixed the bug. Frustrated, I contacted customer service, only to be told they wouldn't honor the price match due to the technical issue on their website. As a result of their glitch, I couldn’t submit my request in time, and now I’m stuck paying the higher price. On top of that, I wasn't able to track my membership progress on their site or app at all throughout last year. This lack of functionality made it even more frustrating to be a member, as I had no way of knowing where I stood in terms of benefits or status. It's disappointing that Expedia won’t take responsibility for these ongoing issues, and it’s making me question whether continuing with their services is worth it.

review_title: Booking flights is simple
review_text: Booking flights is simple, but changes or cancellations can be a hassle. Their customer service is hit or miss.

review_title: Bye Bye Expedia
review_text: After 20 years of using Expedia I am going to try another firm. Trip.com and Booking.com get significantly better reviews on Trustpilot and Expedia shows no interest in responding to this. I was already unnerved a couple of years ago when I dealt with a car hire firm via Expedia in Tanzania. The 'airport' car hire business did not even have a desk in the airport and is basically a scam. The operators attempted to extort a huge 'fine' from me with threats of calling the police because they claimed I drove outside the car's permitted range. Fortunately, I had insurance that covered the deposit they refused to give back. However, Expedia showed zero interest that they were advertising a criminal enterprise -- and one that totally misrepresents itself. Nor were they concerned that other customers would be victims of these people. Last month I made a hotel booking through Expedia which turned out on arrival to be booked for the wrong month. I had this problem once before and an agent on the phone said there is a software problem they are trying to resolve. I made a new booking direct with the hotel. Expedia then said it was impossible to get a refund for the incorrect booking. I did manage, by writing to the hotel manager, to get the money repaid. But the total lameness of Expedia made me decide I have had enough. I am also almost certain that Expedia, when you email an 'agent', is using AI to respond to customers. These 'agents' sign with the name of a human but you are actually dealing with a computer. It shows total contempt for customers. I had verbatim the same answers to two different questions, signed by different 'agents'. I will try Trip.com first as it has pretty good reviews. Will a Chinese-owned firm offer better service than America's biggest travel agent?

review_title: Good prices, poor customer service
review_text: Best price on the market, at the time, but the booking process was made difficult due to website issues. If the app didn't redirect to website in this instance and booking could have been completed using only app this may have been easier. Biggest issue of all is Expedia participating in rewards/promotions that they then have issues honouring, despite meeting terms and conditions. Despite resubmitting cashback request (originally submitted with evidence n proof of purchase) Expedia have once again failed to deliver after over 6 months. Customer service at Top cashback have confirmed the issue lies with Expedia too, so no confusion or misinformation here. I think it's disgusting, as cashback may have influenced my decision. Why sign up to participate if you then don't want to honour? Completely unacceptable, and unexpected from such a large company.

review_title: Scam
review_text: They have an option to pay extra so you can change or cancel the booking for a refund. But it's all bogus. If you want to change it, you have to pay the difference in the ticket, which can be thousands and thousands of dollars. And if you cancel it, the 'refund' is not a refund, but instead they only will give you credit that HAS to be used to book a flight to and from the exact same location with the same airline. It's just a big scam. I suggest using literally any other agency.

review_title: Used Expedia for years
review_text: Used Expedia for years. This year their customer service was horrible. Harder than ever to book a vacation. If this continues they won’t be around much longer

review_title: Urge Caution in Purchasing any Extras
review_text: This is more of a warning than a review. My first try with Expedia Canada. Booked a trip with air, hotel and car rental to leave next month and got a $200 (approx) discount. I opted for a cancelable hotel room in case we wanted to upgrade and the way things were worded that meant no penalty for upgrading room. I called Expedia the next day after my wife decided it would be worth another $500 (estimated) to have a better view of the ocean. When I called I spoke a guy who quoted a price of around $700 for the upgrade. I tried to get an explanation of the difference and he tried to deflect but he eventually said the change was due to cancelation of the discount. He tried to claim it wasn't a charge for the cancelation and I told him it seemed like a penalty for cancelation to me and that extra cancelable price was worthless. Anyway Expedia prices seem pretty OK and we will go as originally booked, however I would urge caution in purchasing any extras.

review_title: Expedia policy makes itself useless...
review_text: Booked a two night stay at a hotel on Long Island through Expedia.  Stay was refundable till two days before check-in. I checked in on the date and at check out noted that the hotel receipt was different than the rate Expedia had already charged me; it was $143 less.  I have used Expedia before to book rooms and have never had the hotel receipt differ from the Expedia receipt.  I requested an explanation from Expedia and a refund of the difference and they said no, prices change and thus you pay the rate at booking.  So basically, they are saying I should have kept checking the rate and if I noticed a change, to my benefit, I should cancel and book with the hotel directly.  Why does Expedia exist then?  What is my incentive to use their "service" if I have to do more work? Absurd policy.

review_title: Horrid Customer Service
review_text: After being transferred around 5 different times and clicking the flight option when using chat, I keep having to be transferred and this feels like a way to dupe me out of my flight credits.

review_text: I made a hotel reservation for three days thru Expdeia travel. The first thing they did wrong was to screw up the departure date of my reservation. When I had to cancel my reservation due to illness they charge me a fee for each day of my lodging at $60 a day! If you are using a travel service don't use Expedia!

review_title: Don’t Expect Refund from Expedia.com When Hotel Is at Fault
review_text: As a frequent traveler, I recommend Booking.com versus Expedia.com. I’ve used both extensively and though they do have lots of hotels to choose from and their website is easy to use, Expedia does not support their customers, even when the Hotel is at fault. For the third time, I haven’t gotten my refund. This particular time, after being disconnected several times, I was left on hold for about an hour before I talked with a human. Even though I received confirmation from Expedia.com for a two week reservation in my email, the hotel had no record of my reservation. When I arrived in the evening, no one was in the lobby, which was locked. There was a phone number with no area code taped to the front door, so I had to walk across the street to an eatery to find out what the area code was. After calling, finally, a flunky arrived but for about two hours, no manager could be found. I called Expedia and was assured my reservation was cancelled and I would get a full refund with no penalty. I never received a confirmation email for the refund so after several attempts to get through to a human being, I finally got through and was told that my reservation had NOT been cancelled and was still in force. I was told I would have to pay approximately $175 before I receive a full refund of $717.10. When I expressed my dissatisfaction, I was summarily “disconnected.” I don’t know about you, but this doesn’t sound ethical to me, and I feel like I’ve been scammed.

review_title: Their prices are too high
review_text: It was my popular booking site for a long time. But something changed recently. They became very expensive and provide limited number of vendors. Just an example - Hotel Bellis 28.12-04.01same room Expedia GBP 2745 Hotel web site - GBP 1145 for 3 guest. Expedia, why should I pay you such premium? You need to do something!

review_text: Don’t make me login to you to check in for my flight ( I booked with you ) that quadruples the check in time that I would regularly need because you take me through a bunch of mumbo-jumbo just to do it through your stupid app.

review_title: Dishonest Subscription service fees
review_text: This company operates a dishonest subscription service which they claim I signed up to when I used their Spanish booking site. They have made an unauthorized deduction of €90 from my bank account without contacting me by email or phone or explaining what the deduction was for. This occurred 9 months after I made a booking through their site.. So be warned...They seem to be scam specialists. I have tried to contact their Spanish office about it but it was a frustrating waste of time. Be Warned

review_title: Incorrect hotel information, flights offered 4.5 hours away from hotel -  huge consequences
review_text: I’ve used Expedia for a lot of holiday bookings but this time their site brought up all the weaknesses into one booking rendering the holiday a non-holiday. 1. The package offered (hotel and flights) presented flights to an airport 4.5 hours away from the hotel (the bad) 2. Fortunately I discovered this 5 days before departure and I was able to cancel the hotel and receive a full refund (the good) 3. I find an alternative beach and golf resort nearest to the airport (but still a long 1.5 hour drive) - it ticked the boxes a) good for us b) walking distance to the beach c) has kids club (the ugly falsehood) On arrival we find that there is no kids club (it is seasonal only) So we have a 5 year old grandson to entertain for 7 days and no opportunity to use the facilities for our enjoyment. After an hour on e-chat, I managed to get some credit to my Expedia account for the Expedia error but it really only covered some of the taxi and entrance for activities. We are left out of pocket We were hard placed to find activities to occupy my grandson (had 2 days just on gadgets in our room) We didn’t have an opportunity to use any of the golf facilities, spa or gym facilities because we became full time baby sitters.

review_title: expedia and generali insurance

review_text: I tried to cancel a hotel booking, having pressed the non-cancellable button in error, for March 2025. I then attempted to cancel directly with the hotel and then enlisted Expedia's support and was told they would email the hotel and get back to me. Three weeks later - nothing. I contacted "Traveler Resolutions" (I assume part of Expedia) by email to complain but they appeared not to have the revised email address that I gave when I first telephoned Expedia and so could not find my details until I went back into a document (which I did not have at hand) to provide my Itinerary No. Still no meaningful explanation. Some support - Go booking.com - much better.

review_title: Disappointed
review_text: I booked a stay at Adora Calma Beach Hotel through Expedia.dk, specifically paying extra for a beach view room. However, upon arrival, I was given a tiny, dark, and noisy room with no beach view. When I brought this up to the reception manager, they were unhelpful and dismissive, and despite contacting Expedia for assistance, the only response I received was a token compensation of 130 kr, which did not make up for the poor experience. So disappointed with Expedia.dk The room was far from what was advertised—small, gloomy, and uncomfortable. The hotel’s beach is also practically unusable due to constant heavy waves, and the pool is tiny, making it overcrowded given the number of guests. The location isn’t great either. While the hotel’s website might make it seem like a beautiful, relaxing place, the reality is far from it. The only redeeming factor was the restaurant staff, who were friendly and provided good service. Unfortunately, the overall experience was extremely disappointing, especially considering the higher price I paid for a room I never got.

review_text: To start, we had booked a vacation package to Cancun, expedia collected the full payment to begin with. review_title: I booked a one night stay in the…
review_text: This is a Review of Expedia, not the Hotel: I booked a one night stay in the Druidstone Hotel Haverford West and gave June instead of July. This would have been simple without Expedia in the middle of it all. I then proceeded to get a whole raft of emails that told me nothing and many were just graphics. Some suggested the dates were changed with no charge but no dates were mentioned and no cost. I emailed the hotel and that was rejected as though it did not exist because it was out of hours. I then rang the hotel the next day and the problem was sorted out within minutes. Why didn't I just book direct with the hotel? I thought the website would be easier: think again

review_title: Here's what may happen to you
review_text: Here's what may happen to you if you book a rental car through Expedia. I booked a rental car (provider was Dollar) for two weeks at DFW airport. The car they gave me did not match what I've booked in terms of the size of the vehicle. (standard SUV - fits 5 passenger and 4 luggages) I could not fit my luggages into the car but the Dollar agent told me there's no other option but to pay extra $75/day for a bigger car. I declined the offer and requested to cancel my rental. The Dollar staff voided the rental agreement but a week later, they charged me for renting a car for 13 minutes. $144.74 for 13 minutes when the car hadn't even left the lot. (never drove an inch and it took me 10 minutes in the line at the counter) Expedia will not refund any money (including $940CAD reservation fee) stating that my reservation is non-refundable. Use Expedia at your own risk. Update : Both Dollar and Expedia finally agreed to refund my money back after 20 days. I give one more star for doing the right thing.

review_title: 107 euros in rewards gone!
review_text: I have had good experiences with Expedia regarding bookings... and because of that collected quite some regards, over 100 euro. Apparently they cannot be used for a long time, because I wanted to use them for this weekend, but it seems they are 'expired' about 1 month ago. I called them to ask for some flexibility, but nothing is possible. It feels I lost over 100 euros.

review_title: Amazing staff but poor communication
review_text: I booked a return trip with Expedia from Gothenburg to Auckland with Lufthansa. Unfortunately, one of the flights was cancelled and I had to phone Expedia to get the flight rebooked. Every time I spoke with them they were very friendly and helpful. I called them about four or five times and I only had to wait once for about fifteen minutes before being connected to someone, all the other times I could speak to someone right away. The staff really tried their best to try to get me on another flight, but unfortunately there were no tickets left in my booking class with Lufthansa within a reasonable time frame (+- a week from my original flight date). However, this was not for lack of trying. They phoned Lufthansa several times for me and tried rerouting me through the US or a different country in Asia and I have nothing but praise for the staff on the phones. They were always so kind and went the extra mile for me. I was given a full refund and the money arrived in my account within a few days. However, I will be giving Expedia three stars. The reason for this is that Expedia actually never informed me my flight was cancelled. I found out myself by adding my booking number to the Lufthansa app, where one of the flights came up as cancelled. I don't know how long the flight had been cancelled for before I found out, it could've been days or even a couple of weeks. After finding this out, the Expedia booking on Expedia's own app never changed (it still said confirmed) and there was no email communication from them regarding this. Luckily, I was able to find other flights at a reasonable price. However, had I not checked the booking myself with the airline, I could've found out days before travelling and the prices could've risen so much I would've been unable to travel. Alternatively, shown up at the airport with no flight to catch. The fact that even the Expedia app doesn't show the updated travel itinerary is a huge fault and I should've also been contacted regarding my flight cancellation. My advice is to always add your booking to the airlines app or regurlaly check with the airline that the flights are confirmed! It all worked out for me in the end but not everyone is that lucky. Expedia also needs to ensure their app shows the current flight status.

review_title: A Hotelier's View
review_text: I work at a motel in a very popular beach destination (aka tourist trap).  A great portion of our reservations are made via Expedia Group websites and my experience as an "insider" has me knowing better than to book through any online travel agency (OTA). For one, businesses are not obligated to keep their listings up-to-date.  You'll get the advertised rate, but it's possible (and likely, these days) the room and property amenities have undergone some changes and I've known folks to come by "just for the jacuzzi". Secondly, the advertised rate is NOT the best rate.  Expedia and other OTAs take between 18-25% commission, so most independent hotels will drop the rate by 10% of whatever you find online should you book directly.  Be sure you find the hotel's actual contact information because Expedia Group does have a couple agency services that will lie to you on the phone. Thirdly, customer service can be a bear--especially on a Friday or Saturday evening.  I don't understand the value provided by an agency if not convenience.  Modifying or cancelling a reservation can be done at the hotel's discretion but the hotel also needs Expedia's agreement to waive the commission.  This leads to more phone calls and confusion than necessary.  Discounts for troubled accommodations are rarely afforded to reservations made through Expedia Group, as they will not modify their commission to be commensurate the discounted rate. In short, book directly and save yourself the headache.

review_title: My experience with Expedia recently was…Wonderful and Awful
review_text: My experience with Expedia recently was great...and ugly. Let me explain. My daughter booked a flight from overseas with a hotel stay upon arrival. She needed to change both those reservations at the last minute: nothing to do with Expedia the airlines or hotel. The "ugly" was that there was a very limited time to rebook & she could not get an Expedia rep on the phone from abroad, she experienced super long wait times. Finally I, her father tried, waited three hours the first time with no pickup, and a little over 4 1/2 hours the second time before I got someone live on the phone. The "great" is once I got Subramanya from Bangalore on the phone, he was super helpful, courteous, and answered all my questions. He was able to rearrange the hotel dates. He was not able to help with the flight, because when my daughter could not get a hold of Expedia, she talked to the airline and they re-booked the flight. They were super helpful (Asiana). Just a note...if someone outside Expedia changes a booking, Expedia can no longer see the itinerary and cannot help. So if the airline had not been flexible, my daughter would have been in a real "spot". Expedia's deals come with deadlines to re-book, but it is not responsible on their part not to staff enough people to answer the phone in a timely manner. I have used Expedia in the past, but this very well may be a deal breaker for me to use them or any of the companies they have bought up. I hope they are able to get it together.

I called the Expedia customer service after we got to Pokhara to explain what happened at the airport, the representative didn’t know nor understood my problem, and kept telling me I should have gone to Air Togo terminal after I told her many times that there was no Air Togo terminal at the airport. I hung up the phone after over an hour on the phone, she kept put me on hold 5 to 10 minutes at a time. I wanted to chat instead of talking ti an agent next day, the system acted up and kept disconnected. W finally managed to chat with an agent, and I was assured that I got air tickets from Yeti Airline on our return flight. It was a very painful experience for me, and I hope Expedia should solve this problem in the future. By the way, the price of the flights from Expedia was much more expensive than if I went directly to the airline, and I could have saved the problem, stress, headache and time. review_text: Family trip became very complicated. One member's online reservation was switched from an Airbus to a 2 hr. bus ride. review_title: Two error messages after two payment attempts and now stuck with two non-refundable reservations. Quickly resolved.
review_text: I made a reservation at the Kobe Luminous hotel via the Expedia app. I wanted to pay directly since it was the cheapest option. review_title: Manage your expectations
review_text: Like any travel agent, most of your experience will be seamless until something goes wrong like you need to change a name on your ticket or flight was cancelled. Expedia is an intermediary and so they have to charge fees to pay for the staff making the calls to the airline or hotel. It's always better to book directly. However, it's extremely convenient to book with Expedia and to find some deals. Cancellations or changes were a hassle years ago, but since them, they have automated a lot and are much more responsive. If you are going to book through an aggregator, they're a good choice.

review_title: Extremely easy to use
review_text: Extremely easy to use, however, I did need to go back multiple times to find specific details regarding my hotel and flight information. Other than those minor items, I would highly recommend!

review_title: Really empathetic response to my…
review_text: Really empathetic response to my situation when I was seeking  to rebook a flight cancelled as a result of Covid. The representative tirelessly pursued options for me. I will use Expedia again.

review_title: Lovely Expedia excels in hotel bookings
review_text: Loving Expedia. Used them since 2011 for practically all my private bookings of hotel stays and car rentals, local and international. Up to a few years ago, I used Expedia exclusively for booking flights as well, then I found better alternatives. Now I book flights elsewhere but still bench with Expedia. I'm a gold member (more than 15 nights/yr). I like the bonus promos, discounts and VIP benefits for hotel bookings. On a few occasions, I've made claims and had excellent support. Overcharges made by hotels were refunded to me by Expedia, bookings changed promptly through live-people support. Thank you, and keep up the good work, Expedia. Showing the total price, including taxes and fees for all participants would make your service even more outstanding. Please consider it.

review_title: Very good for booking Trips!
review_text: Very good for booking trips away with everything you need, flights, hotels, experiences and car hire! I’ve used Expedia multiple times for trips away and had faultless service!

review_title: Previous complaint resolved

review_title: I love using Expedia when booking all…
review_text: I love using Expedia when booking all my hotels. They have amazing discounts as well as added extras (like free breakfast included and free internet etc). It makes it really easy and you can save even more when using your Expedia points. Such a great website!

review_title: No complaints, cheap and easy
review_text: Just back from a 5 day trip to Santa Ponsa, Mallorca booked all through Expedia. We booked our flights and hotel as a package, flying with Ryan Air and staying at Zafiro Rey Don Jamie. We had no issues with any of this from the booking, the flights, the transfers or hotels. Once I completed my booking I received my flight confirmation nearly straight away, I waited 48 hours and contacted the hotel who confirmed all was booked and paid for also. We booked a return trip from the airport to the hotel which was great, picked us up right outside the airport and dropped us right outside the hotel. I have had no issues booking through Expedia and for me it was a cheap and pleasant experience. review_title: Expedia Provided Refund After Booking Issue
review_text: I know others have had the negative experience with what I went through, so I wanted to submit this review because Expedia refunded the money I used to book a hotel, after the wrong dates were booked due to a system glitch. I panicked after receiving a confirmation that had the wrong date booked for a hotel- it was actually booked for the present day when I was doing the reservation. Knowing that I was meticulous while making the booking (as it was for a special occasion with a memorable date) and stressing that it was a system glitch, I immediately called Expedia to see if there was ANY possible way to get a refund so that I could rebook for the proper trip dates. I was stressed after reading the company policy and reviews saying that other Expedia customers had the same issue without receiving a refund. So I was extremely happy when the Expedia operator I spoke to was able to promise me a refund, which I received back in my account within 5 hours during the day. Not everyone will have the same experience, and it may have been that the hotel was just as good with allowing a refund, but I was so happy that I wanted to write this and give hope to other customers that may be in a similar situation.

review_title: I'm giving an Expedia of one because…
review_text: I'm giving an Expedia of one because that's the only star I can do. We booked a limo service and Bangkok Thailand with Expedia and the limo service did not show up. After waiting for 2 hours and talking to Expedia who tried to catch them on the phone after I told them we had called them two or three times and couldn't get an answer they have decided that I do not deserve a refund because the company said the driver was at the airport and the lady and I were not. Why would I have spent over an hour on the phone with Expedia if we would have been down there with the driver and ready to come to the Hotel. When Budget wouldn't acknowledge any fault when I called them after my trip, Expedia tried to intercede with them, also without success. review_title: Efficient and responsive call centre
review_text: I booked Air Astana flights with Expedia.fr as they offered me a very good deal for the itinerary I wanted which included different outbound and inbound flights. Unfortunately, this is exactly what happened - Air Astana cancelled my inbound flight and modified my booking by replacing my original inbound flight with another flight, a 30+ hours earlier one than the flight I actually booked. I called Expedia immediately upon the receipt of the modification as the modification didn't work for me at all and they immediately took care of my case. The call was very pleasant and the lady was very kind and understanding and everything ended well for me. So, can't complain so far (as long as Expedia is concerned).

review_text: Booked hotel and flight to Edinburgh, everything went smooth until Expedia called and told us that the booked hotel had closed down. review_title: Good site for price comparison and to buy flights with security
review_text: I have been using expedia.ie (Ireland) for the last 6 years, to book flights in Europe. In general, I have been very happy with them: their costumer support has helped me a lot in some difficult situations, and they have refunded me in one case where there was some misinformation on their part. review_text: I never had any problems with Expedia at all! I booked several times when travelling to different destinations and everything seems to be straightforward. I found the website really easy to navigate, and the content including travelling information very detailed, including hotels taxes and total cost. The only relevant information that I noticed that has been changing,  is the suitcase allowance when booking flights or selecting packages. For example, previously the economy class was including 23Kg suitcase allowance as a standard in most of the Airlines  ( British Airways, Lufthansa, Virgin A etc). I noticed that now,  in Expedia you have to pay the suitcase separately, having only as an allowance a handbag. ( not travelling with Easyjet or Ryanair which I particularly avoid) Taking this into consideration I booked the flight directly with British Airways in the same Economy class but it was including the 23 KG suitcase allowance.  I booked the hotel through Expedia which still they have very competitive prices and easy booking Overall, I am very happy with the service and general customer journey experience. p.s - I love the fact that Nectar's points are added when booking at Expedia.

review_title: Everything was perfect UNTIL...
review_text: The flight booking went perfectly smoothly. We'd booked a flight and hotel bundle, and we got to the hotel with our reservation intact. The problem was, Expedia categorised people above 18 as adults while the hotel considered adults to be above 12 years old, which is why they wanted to charge us extra upon our arrival. After demanding we speak to the manager and have him contact Expedia to deal with the discrepancy, they gave in and realized there was some sort of mistake. My only complaint is that Expedia and some of the hotels it's partnered up with dont have the same idea about adult age and therefore prices are different.

review_title: Last Minute Get Away Fron Toronto, Canada to MGM Grand Las Vegas, Nevada
review_text: We booked our last minute weekend getaway through Expedia to the MGM grand hotel Las Vegas, Nevada. We did have an issue with our return flight missing our connecting flight due to delays, and the AA helped us get on WestJet direct flight to Toronto or we would have to wait for another day which would not have worked in our favour. Expedia gave us $100 credit to use within the year for our inconvenience. (thanks, Expedia, and American Airlines.) From Toronto, Ontario the cost of the trip with the flight and room for three nights was $1000 Canadian! Great deal, but the bed in our room, in the West Wing, was not up to our standard. (poor pillows and sunken mattress). No fridge in the room and the AC vent was right next to our head embedded in the night table. The next day the MGM Grand Hotel service representative April was awesome! She upgraded our room to a larger room for $15 a night. Total $30 US dollars! Not bad for a better room in the newer part of the hotel! The hotel is only a $12-13 taxi ride from the airport. The taxis are available around the clock as the airport is fairly busy, but they have many drivers and taxis available for transport so we moved through the line quickly. We did get buffet free for two people for one of our days stay at the hotel. The buffet would have cost $60US for two people. (not bad price but nicer that it was free with our Expedia package!) Overall, a fantastic hotel close to Vegas Strip, airport, clubs and has a lot of activities. It was a great price for a last minute getaway (thanks, Expedia!).

review_title: Functions well and reliably
review_text: I'm happy with the number of bookings I've done with expedia. Clear process of booking with good ability to check itineraries after. As well as decent email notification and mobile app support. The points program is a plus as well. I have had limited need to phone them, but no problem when I did. The prices and availability of flights and hotels can sometimes be subpar. That would be my main criticism.

review_title: Always a decent experience
review_text: We have had our fair share of issues as the next guy, but overall they are way better than Travelocity. We used them for Vegas, Cabo, Florida and New York and the hotels have always been what they said they were online.

review_title: Refund experience
review_text: Last weekend I booked a flight amounting to just under 500 euros with Expedia. I left out one of the middle names of the passengers and rang them up (5 mins after the booking) to ask if this would be a problem for the airline. The customer service rep told me to be better safe than sorry and that because I had only just booked the flight, he said he'd cancel and refund the flight for me so that I could start fresh with another booking. He told me the refund would be within 72 hours. There was very little stress on the phone - it seemed very straight forward - no issues. Soon after that I did a google search and came across nothing but bad reviews regarding Expedia and refunds. Naturally this got me extremely worried and nervous as to whether I would actually get the refund. However I waited the 72 hours but still nothing refunded - instead it appeared to be two sets of flights charged for instead of one. I got straight onto customer service who said that Expedia hold the money and the airline withdraws also (really confusing). They told me that this was normal and that the refund would definitely be coming through. The next day - about 96 hours later - all funds were back in the account and I was extremely relieved. As there are so many bad reviews of Expedia on this in regards to refunds, I wanted to post this to say that it is possible to get the physical refund back from them within the week you have booked (with a couple of customer service calls) - although maybe I was a rare lucky one?? With regards to cancelling and getting refunds closer to your holiday time - I don't have any experience and it may be a completely different story. I just wanted to share my story.

review_title: Reliable, quick refund. Unable to change reservations, though.
review_text: Booked a room cheaper than the competition with "free cancelation". A few days later, we decided to we would only stay for 2 nights instead of the 3 we booked. Tried to make the change directly with the hotel, with no success. Since I had already paid for it, I was a bit scared by some of the reviews here. Nevertheless, 3 or 4 days later the exact amount I paid was refunded (bear in mind that they inform you that the refund may differ due to exchange rates variation). review_title: Our Money Back Within a Week after Cancellation due to Sickness
review_text: After reading all bad reviews here I wondered how the travel protection plan would work out for us. Our experience was good. We purchased our tickets to Europe for the whole family back in February with the travel protection plan. It said if any of our immediate family members get sick and unable to travel they pay back the money we spent on our non-refundable airline tickets. Sure enough, a week before the journey we got a virus and my wife and son got real sick. I made sure we visited the doctors one day before our planned journey and let them both fill out the claim form. (I could not download it from the site, they sent that via email.) I cancelled the flights via Expedia, filled out the form and they sent the checks in a week. The bad. When I called them they hinted that we could rebook our tickets and they would pay then the rebooking fees AND the price difference between our old tickets and new tickets as long as that difference is less than the price of the original tickets. When I checked the actual explanation of benefits document I could not find it there. I tried to email about this and have this promise in writing. They replied only that I should call them. After the third call they acknowledged that this option does not exist. If I had believed that at the first place, we could've lost everything except the rebooking fees. Read the explanation of benefits carefully. What is not there is not covered by the policy.

review_title: Was able to cancel with refund
review_text: I booked a hotel through Expedia and then had to cancel. There is a no refund for cancellation policy. So I tried to call Expedia. Of course, it's difficult to find a customer service phone number on their website, but if you search for it on the internet you can find one. I got an automated phone system that very quickly was able to look up the booking I was interested in canceling. The automated system informed me, as I knew already, that there was no cancellation for a refund. Would I like to cancel anyway, not cancel, or explore other options? I chose to explore other options and found that Expedia could make a phone call to the hotel to see if they would grant an exception. I chose this option, chose "booking error" as my reason, and got an email reply from Expedia in less than an hour informing me that my cancellation request was approved by the hotel and I would be receiving a full refund. Perhaps I should wait until it shows up on my credit card statement before submitting this review, but so far I found this system to be much more forgiving than I had expected, and fast and convenient, too.

review_title: Had my back
review_text: Mohammed at Expedia helped me get a refund on a horrible experience I had with Ocean Drive Beach and Golf Resort in Myrtle Beach.  I booked an Oceanfront room for 2 nights; $600. on Expedia.   Got to the hotel and wasn't greeted at all, just stared at by 2 front desk staff;  one old man and a young girl. The girl saw I booked through Expedia and gave me an oceanfront room blocked by a row of fully grown palm trees; no oceanfront view.  When I went back to the desk, the old man scolded me for using Expedia.  Said, thats what you get when you book through a 3rd party!! You need to take it up with Expedia.  I called Expedia and the issue was resolved immediately with a refund and an apology!  I will never recommend  booking at Ocean Drive Beach Resort and will always recommend and use Expedia....they had my back!!

review_title: After many years, Its still great!!

I called to notify expedia in hopes they'd update the info. Still no update. Other than this, service is still great!

review_title: Expedia fixed a big mistake I made.
review_text: I was looking for a hotel in Gelena, Ohio on the Expedia website. I found a great hotel and booked it on the spot. The only problem was it was for Gelena, Illinois not Gelena, Ohio! I made a big mistake! I did not realize this until after I booked the hotel. Once I figured out what had happened I contacted the hotel and Expedia via an agent in their online site. The hotel was wonderful and Mark at Expedia was extremely helpful and understanding. He fixed the problem on Expedia's end and he followed up with the hotel and within 12 hours I received back 100% of the monies I had sent to the hotel and I did not have to pay a cancellation fee. I could not be happier and I will use Expedia in the future and I recommend that you give them a try. PS The Steamboat Bed and Breakfast in Gelena, Illinois looks wonderful and I highly recommend them to you if you are in that area and looking for a great bed and breakfast!

review_title: Excellent Customer Service

Will continue using Expedia for my travel needs.

review_title: Received full refund for pass of my father
review_text: I want to make a point of posting my positive experience with Expedia. I booked the flights for myself and my partner to Taiwan. Each flight cost over £1100. Unfortunately, my father passed away before the trip, and I had no choice but to cancel the flight. During these difficult times, I reached out to Expedia customer service and asked for assistance via live chat. The first staff (Tawheed) was very kind and helpful. The second staff (Karina) was also very patient and helpful. They cancelled my flight and requested a refund on my behalf, they kept me updated every three working days, letting me know they were working on my case. It was very helpful through these difficult times as I didn't have to worry about the refund process while going through the funeral. Eventually, surprisingly enough, I got a full refund! It didn't put much hope in it, so this was a big surprise, especially in this unexpected life event that putting me under financial pressure. I surely grow some confidence in Expedia. On the other hand, the other agency showed no support for my circumstance, and as a result, I lost over £500 due to their lack of interest, which I later found out could have been avoided by contacting the flight provider. I very much appreciate Expedia and I will book with Expedia in my future trips.

review_title: Luggage Ground Hog Day.
review_text: In April I traveled on United Airlines to Greece. My bag never arrived. I spent hours daily responding to requests for forwarding the bag. My Apple Tag indicated my bag never left ORD Terminal 5. Ten days after departure after I had replaced necessary items I learned United was finally forwarding my bag. It arrived at our final hotel the night before we returned home. I was charged $211.01  to bring my unused luggage back home. United denies all responsibility stating international law requires the final local Greek airline to assume full responsibility for reimbursement. Those leading our trip did not know this. I did as the Tour Director and EF Tours instructed. I also filed with Blue Ribbon bag location services. They closed the case claiming luggage had been found. But not returned to me!  I always knew where it was!!!  Now I’m applying through insurance. I’ve spent hours daily. All I get are apologies for the inconvenience, no results. I see why people stuff carryon compartments full. Wow.

Staff were friendly and helpful, especially Maria at the front desk who went out of her way to assist with dinner reservations. Breakfast buffet had good variety but food quality was inconsistent. Pool area was clean and well maintained. Overall decent value for the price point, though not exceptional.

review_title: Tripadvisor hotel booking scam
review_text: I made a hotel booking through Tripadvisor with a hotel rate cost totaling $2827.25.  I also agreed at the time to pay an additional $97 for a "cancel for any reason" option -- but instead, when I saw my credit card bill, I saw that they charged me $707 for that service. When I phoned Tripadvisor to object to this ridiculous added fee (that I never even agreed to) they gave me endless run-around, left me waiting on the phone multiple times and just kept denying their error. It was like talking to a brick wall with them. I ended up canceling the entire reservation six weeks ahead of my planned stay because of this bad experience with them and even then, it took multiple times on the phone with them making me wait for extended time on the phone just to get the $2827.25 refunded but with them still denying me a refund for their erroneous added fee of $707.  And who in their right mind would have ever agreed to pay nearly a third of the total cost of their hotel stay to be able to cancel a hotel stay 6 weeks ahead of time??  They are corrupt, and their treatment of me is nothing less than a scam.  I will never do business with them again and advise everyone to not do business with them either!

Tripadvior is also useless in resolution. review_title: TripAdvisor is deceitful and cannot be trusted.
review_text: i left a negative review for a city my wife and I visited.  TripAdvisor sent me an email with a link to their new guidelines that, for all intents and purposes, disallows negative reviews. The incredibly long, lawyer-created, cleverly-worded policy even prohibits any review that is 'biased'.  LOL!!!!  ALL REVIEWS ARE BIASED!!! THAT'S WHAT A REVIEW IS!!! A review is YOUR relating of YOUR opinion biased to YOUR experience of a place or thing. Different people have different experiences and their opinions are biased to their respective experiences.  that one person's experience was negative does not make it less valuable or less authentic than the person who had a good experience. TripAdvisor does not allow the opinions of those who had objectively bad experiences with a place or a service. review_title: Non-existent reservation and lack of information, missed tour and no refund.
review_text: Months in advance, I booked a tour from Buenos Aires to Colonia del Sacramento through TripAdvisor, operated by Colonia Express. We only received a voucher, which clearly stated that it was not the ticket and that the ticket should be collected at the time of boarding. The problem is that, upon arriving at the indicated location and presenting all the information provided by TripAdvisor, there was simply no ticket or reservation linked to our name. Because of this, we were not allowed to board, completely losing the tour. Our entire travel itinerary was organized around this tour, which ended up being wasted. It is unclear whether: • TripAdvisor only sold a "reservation" without generating the tickets, or • there was a communication failure with Colonia Express. The fact is that we received absolutely no guidance on how to collect the tickets, where to do so, or who to contact. I have used TripAdvisor before, and normally the guides contact you the day before explaining the entire procedure—which did not happen this time. The voucher we received was useless, and the reservation, in practice, didn't exist. Furthermore, we were in another country, with communication difficulties, and we were treated hostilely on site. Even in this situation, the refund was denied. Another serious issue was the time provided: The voucher stated that the boarding deadline was 8:30 am, with a recommendation to arrive 1 hour earlier. We arrived at 7:40 am, within the indicated time, and were informed that boarding and the boat had already departed. In other words, the information provided was completely inconsistent. The tour is poorly explained, not intuitive at all, there is no adequate support on site, and in the end, the consumer is left completely helpless. We lost an entire day of travel, in addition to the money paid, for a reservation made months ago that was not honored. Given all these shortcomings, I request: • A full refund of the amount paid, • and a formal explanation of what happened with our reservation. The minimum expected is respect for the consumer and responsibility in the sale of tourism services.

review_title: ⭐⭐ Radisson Barbados
review_text: ⭐⭐ Radisson Barbados – Disappointing 10-Night Stay We stayed at the Radisson Barbados for 10 nights and unfortunately the experience was very disappointing. The breakfast buffet was extremely basic and felt more like a budget hotel than a Radisson. Every day it was largely the same: deep-fried bacon, scrambled eggs, sausages, beans, fish cakes, plantain, a few tiny pastries, melon, grapes, kiwi, and a couple of other fruits. There was a basic omelette station. After a long stay, the lack of variety became very frustrating. One member of staff in the breakfast area, Jeanette, really stood out as friendly and helpful — sadly she was the exception. Housekeeping was very poor. My sons were actually told off by cleaners for their room not being tidy — they are on holiday. Towels were not replaced, water was not restocked, and we were left without toilet roll on more than one occasion. The pool is extremely small, with no towels provided and not enough loungers. The beach area also lacked sufficient loungers. Most of the beach staff were rude and argumentative. One staff member named Shane stood out positively; the rest made interactions uncomfortable rather than welcoming. We also had a frustrating experience with food service at the beach. We ordered three pizzas to our sun loungers. There was confusion over the order, and we were told that “in their culture” a margherita is considered a vegetable pizza, despite our friends clearly ordering margherita, pepperoni, and vegetable. The staff member made a mistake but refused to acknowledge it or resolve the issue, which again came across as argumentative rather than customer-focused. The rooms are very basic, the beds are very small, and overall the rooms feel tired and outdated. To make matters worse, security accused my husband of lying about which room we were staying in, which was completely unacceptable and embarrassing. This hotel could be amazing, as the location is good and we hired cars to get around easily. However, the hotel needs a full refresh, and the staff urgently need proper training in all areas of hospitality. Overall, this was not the standard expected from the Radisson brand, and we would not return unless significant improvements are made

Just because I am looking doesn’t mean I am planning a trip.  What a hassle.  The've really goon down hill. I use Expedia now.  Valuable reviews and no hassle.

review_title: No longer useful
review_text: I know longer have faith that the review system is fair and transparent.

review_title: Reviews are now unreliable.
review_text: The increasing problem with TripAdvisor is that the bot which reads reviews does not work. I reported four reviews/business responses recently. One was patently racist, one was for for a hotel but posted to a landmark (there were a considerable number with the same issue for the same place), and the others were also posted against the wrong place. The bot decided that all of the above met TA's rules. It’s difficult to take it further (you have to be an EU resident to get a button?). I went through FaceBook to get these sorted but realistically this is a waste of my time. I have always noticed reviews in the wrong place etc but it’s now an epidemic and sadly means that the traveller rating is completely unreliable. You have to read a selection of the reviews yourself. Very disappointing as TA is publishing misleading information on an industrial scale. Bot needs to get much better!
