So many single reviews by various people and you would think it would raise an alarm with trip advisor but despite voicing you worries they are always ignored.

review_text: Unity living, Helsinki Well designed studio apartments, but bed not comfortable, central heating in place, cannot be regulated individually in the rooms, no extra fans available. Was advised to open window when I could hear the road  traffic as though they were running right on my head. Breakfast horrible.

review_text: Almost a nightmare with a hotel they refered. Be very very careful with these people

review_title: Poor Service
review_text: Food was good, but service was slow. I think if you pay over £100 for a meal the all experience should be excellent, it wasn’t! The owner doesn’t agree though, seems to think every was fine and won’t accept any criticism. He alleges I was disparaging about the staff, I wasn’t! Apparently we should have gone somewhere we could afford and maybe if I had culinary skills I would understand. Frankly a bit of a rant and over reaction to an reasonable view. So won’t be going there again! There’s many places that are far better!

review_title: TripAdvisor was my go-to site to find…
review_text: TripAdvisor was my go-to site to find reputable tour operators & tours.  I read reviews on those that are highly rated with a high number of reviews then make judgements based on good & bad commonalities of what the customers are saying about the operator.  I am a world traveler and I have not been stirred in the wrong direction by TripAdvisor.  All that has changed in my recent long trip to 3 continents.  I just got back today and decided to review TripAdvisor myself.  For the first time, I had 3 bad experiences with 3 tours listed on TA.  All of them were in the Middle East.  One was a no show. Two sent drivers who supposedly were also guides who did not speak English well and do not know much about the place at all. This made me wonder if TA is screening operators listed on their site.  I also found out that the operator I hired subcontracted it to another operator.  This happened a few times.  So the reviews I read and based my decisions on were not valid anymore.  It happened more than once.  When the operators came to pick us up, I asked for the name of the agency and it was different from what was listed on TripAdvisor/Viator that I contracted.  All 3 bad experiences happened in the Middle East.  Viator is owned by TripAdvisor too and they list the same operators in their respective websites.  These recent experiences put my high regard of TripAdvisor & Viator in question.  I am sad that I feel this way because I relied my judgements on their reputations too. My go-to travel site will not be my one stop shop for tours and tour operators resource any more.

review_title: I wrote a review of a hotel in France…
review_text: I wrote a review of a hotel in France and gave a very truthful review of everything that was wrong with the hotel and restaurant. No curse words, no interracial slurs, just the truth about the smell in the room, an ancient lock that didn't work, a bath tub/shower that was dangerous to get in and out of and the restaurant that both my husband and I got sick from.  This is not the first bad review of a hotel that I wrote, but it was the first not published.  The review sat in a pending status for one week and then poof!  Erased without any explanation.  I have been review places since 2007 for TripAdvisor and never had something like this happen.  This hotel has only great reviews in the past 3 years.  Everyone on the bus tour hated it......  What is the value of writing a review if the bad ones are not published?  Or do some properties pay TA not to publish the bad ones?   And then how can you believe anything on TA? NCcatpeople TripAdvisor did send an email claiming that the sent a verification email to us regarding this review. I never received an email from TripAdvisor regarding my review of the Chateau de Pray.  Very interesting that on November 8, I wrote 5 reviews for places in Spain and France and the only review that you sent this verification email was for the bad review.  Actually, in the 15 years that I have been posting a review, I have never received a verification email. And yes, I have checked my junk email and nothing.

review_title: ANDY’S WATCHES-ICMELER, TURKEY
review_text: I purchased a watch from ANDY’S WATCH CENTRE IN ICMELER, TURKEY and had to return it after 6 weeks as it wasn’t working.  I received it back and after 2 days it broke down again and once again I returned it. To date I have not received it back as he keeps saying he has not got it back. I have sent Royal Mail receipt to him and still nothing.  The quality obviously was poor and I would be very wary of ordering online as you will have nothing but hassle when trying to get back the item you returned. Would I recommend this shop - DEFINITELY NOT. 😢😢😡

review_title: Easter Sunday 4/17/22
review_text: Easter Sunday 4/17/22 Hilton Hotel, Ocala Florida Easter Brunch 1st was seating screw up- we reserved seating with our favorite waitress. Got placed in a different seating area with a different server 2nd - limited food choices- very small salad bar, only carrots on main buffet for the vegetable, no mashed potatoes- just sub par to what we’re used to at this establishment. Would definitely check the menu listing before i ever go back to another holiday buffet here. Very disappointing for the price.

review_title: Onthebeach " beware"
review_text: Onthebeach " beware" I've booked with this company on many occasions and been very satisfied but I've been having nothing but trouble this time trying to sort out my holiday booking with them, their customer service line is closed , they say they are very busy at the moment and told to use the online manage my booking section . It all started with me making an error on my booking , I booked a hotel with the same name not thinking there were three hotels with similar names , anyway after noticing my mistake I got online straight away to change hotels using their system on manage my bookings , I put all the details in and a price came up to change plus I knew there would be an administration fee it all came to just under £1000 I waited to see the change but all I got was a message saying pending , I tried many times to get in touch online and by phone but to no avail so I had to threaten them by going public via social media , I then got a response but the overhaul price of the change had gone up considerably since the date I tried , I complained but was told there's nothing they could do , they wouldn't refund my money  so I could go online myself and rebook at the cheaper price I seen on their website . After speaking to the wife I went online again and tried again to make a change of hotel hoping I would be contacted by a different agent , I waited a while again so I repeated my concern that the change hadn't happened  on the date I requested then hooray they replied and told my there was an increase in the holiday price to £1420  but we were happy with it as we knew the hotel was nice , but unfortunately they have now sent us the new holiday invoice and it's wrongly calculated,  its asking for just under £2000 for the holiday , I tried immediately to find out what's gone wrong but can't get in touch with anyone   it's giving me a nervous breakdown,  I'm due to pay the next installment but the the price is high because of the mistake , I can't cancel  the payment because they will default my holiday and I'd lose the lot .I don't know what to do ??? Stay away from this company.

review_text: Trip advisor allows renters to cancel last minute, receive a total refund due to COVID pandemic HOWEVER they keep their booking fee.  They still make their money and the owner of the property left with no renter late in season and no deposit money, zero compensation for a rental booked over 11 months ago.

review_title: I used “TripAdvisor plus” for the first…
review_text: I used “TripAdvisor plus” for the first time on October 9, 2021 to select a NYC hotel. I chose the Hotel Edison NYC, NY. When I arrived the hotel Edison staff said they automatically add a $35 “facility fee”. I disputed this both on check-in and checkout and was told to take it up with TripAdvisor plus. Adding extra hidden fees renders the TripAdvisor “deal” meaningless. I would’ve selected a different property if I knew the accurate price. I asked the Hotel Edison staff what it was for and they told me for things that I did not use at all such as business Center, breakfast, water, and the gym. Also the room wasn’t even cleaned properly when we arrived (The bellhop told us we had to go downstairs again and get another room). The second room was not thoroughly cleaned either (coffee dispenser not emptied) but we were running late for tickets at MOMA so we had to just live with it. I emailed “TripAdvisor plus” on Sunday, October 10 and still (October 17) have not had a response. Apparently there is no “TripAdvisor plus” customer service once they take your money. Although I think TripAdvisor is great, I would never recommend “TripAdvisor plus” or Hotel Edison.

review_title: TripAdvisor not so honest reviews
review_text: I have, until recently, been an avid TripAdvisor disciple. Every trip I made was preceded by careful scrutiny of TA reviews. However, I now see so many businesses riding high in the ratings based on single (or very close to single) review submissions. It's almost as if businesses know a few fake profiles can propel them up the rankings. TA do not seem to police this. For me, they have lost all credibility

review_title: Ikworth hotel,Horringer Suffolk
review_text: I visited Ikworth hotel on 11Sept. The hotel ,in country grounds looked inviting on the outside. Alas no disabled parking in front of the hotel. The downstairs lounge wasn't country chic ,not even shabby chic, but rather troc au vente. The carpet was covered in bits, and there wasn't  a chair that an elderly guest or disabled person could easily get  out of. The panels of the lounge doors were thick with dust. The dining room carpet was similarly covered in bits and the service was below par. My sparkling water was brought to the table unopened, which I had difficulty in opening( the waiter had disappeared). My fish pie was hardly warm inside and my espresso coffee cold. The afternoon tea looked  excellent and the conservatory looked inviting. Alas the handle on the disabled toilet was broken, and the room itself was messy. Very disappointed.

review_title: I used trip advisor to schedule…
review_text: I used trip advisor to schedule activities while on vacation in TCI.  I scheduled my activities in April 2021 for a trip in August 2021.  Well when I arrived in TCI and called the company to confirm my excursion I was told that they had no record of my activity.  I told them this was impossible because they had just taken the $360 out of my account the day before.  After lots of emailing and texting to the company to prove I had a reservation they agreed that I had the reservation but Trip Advisor/Viator had made an error.  Unfortunately for me I could not do my excursion at the time I scheduled because they had given that time away.  The guy from the Jet Ski company (Sun and Fun ) said he would give me a time when he arrived in the office.  Well I guess it was a long ride to the office because at noon that day he contacted my husband to say we can do it at 3pm.  I was ticked because I waited and held up my day waiting for this excursion time.  Well when the time finally go close it poured down rain.  The guy then says we can wait for the rain to pass and see what happens.  I finally said no and said I want the refund.  He agreed and said when he receives the request from Trip Advisor  he will approve it.  Well I had to call them (2 days later) to apparently begin the process which I thought I had already begun online.  It took me 1.5 hours to get that refund back to my credit card.  I will NEVER book anything through trip advisor.  Buyer beware.  I only gave them 2 stars because I did get the refund, but it was beyond frustrating. Oh and after all that time on the phone explaining and re-explaining they tried to sell me another excursion!   Unbelievable!

review_title: Continued stay at the hogs back hotel and spa
review_text: We arrived at the hogs back hotel and the greeting wasn’t hello welcome like you would expect it was use the self check in I am busy with other customers!!! But whilst using the self check not realising he was taking to us he was shouting out random instructions which was very rude. We was not told about wifi and spa etc so had to go back when when he was less busy even then he was very abrupt. The room is lovely and clean and bed very comfortable. Breakfast was a 45 minute wait whilst watching guests eat that arrived long after us I did go to reception to discuss this but couldn’t find anyone and rang the bell twice, the long awaited breakfast was cold so didn’t eat it anyway. I went to reception AGAIN to find out about the use of the spa and asked if they supplied robes as you would usually find in a spa hotel room but was told they are only for treatments and I could ask if they had a spare if I wanted!!!! I am a keen swimmer and would have used the facilities throughout the day but would prefer to change in my room, I was told they don’t supply them at the Hilton somewhere where the receptionist had previously worked. So I am about to go and have a swim now and see how it is. We have another night yet and came here as our wedding was cancelled due the pandemic as a treat from our children but so far has not impressed us at all!!!

review_title: Edreams booking service linked to Trip Advisor sites- TERRIBLE
review_text: This is a review of Trip Advisor’s linked flight booking service edreams. This is a terrible booking service. Trip Advisor should be ashamed to be linking their customers to this scamming service. Edreams advertises the cheapest price, which then after confirming your booking raises the price without their customers’ knowledge or consent. You are then stuck without an option of refunding through cancellation or paying their inflated price. Their customer service is absolutely terrible, and their money-back guarantee is impossible to satisfy the requirements without purchasing tickets through another company (leaving you with two sets of tickets, and no money refunded.) I cannot believe a company as well-founded as Trip Advisor would use such a terrible flight booking agency. I will never use Trip Advisor again.

I have had clients write "shut this business down", over fake claims and questionable racist language. There is a segment of the popular who uses bullying to  treanten businesses and they feel emboldened by TripAdvisor to do so. It is  Malicious  intent and should not be accepted by Trip Advisor.

review_title: Someone explain why TripAdvisor refuse to publish this review of Kew Gardens
review_text: £18 to get in may well seem a tad over the top given that for decades it was set at 10 pence    (2s or 2/- in old money) by Royal charter (Queen Victoria) Having said that it is so easy to spend an entire day here that actually it is half decent value - even allowing for the various coffee shops outlandish pricing - £9 for coffee and cake (per person) A major downside is the British desire to turn all havens of tranquillity into theme parks - one now has to accept that it is on the school activity day circuit, usually barely supervised with loud screaming infants/boisterous teenagers etc. monopolising the peace around the supersized play zones - no longer the haven of tranquillity it once was! Don’t’ get me going on the mothers with toddlers (the toddlers mainly unnoticed by their mothers) dominating the cafes. Wander off down the Richmond end of the gardens and it is a different world. No play zones, no cafes, just woodland and peace...wonderful. It begs the question, why turn the Kew end into a school outing venue? It's a botanical garden that people from all over the world come to see- world famous for its incredible arboricultural and horticultural work, it’s not supposed to be Disneyland! If you are a member you can access the gardens before the general public and have an hour or so lost in the middle of London with only the birds, trees, plants and the occasional aeroplane coming into Heathrow to bother you… Bliss! Update TripAdvisor are requesting a contact email address from me with no contact address provided by themselves to reply to their request. "No can do" - without your very secretive contact details (see other peoples comments on how to contact them) Update two If anyone can understand this gobbledegook non - response from TripAdvisor they have a better command of language than I have. "Hello, Thank you for contacting TripAdvisor. Your submissions have been pulled aside by the automated filtering system we have created to identify posts that either requires special attention or may violate our guidelines. review_title: TripAdvisor is a business
review_text: TripAdvisor is a business.  It's customers are the hotels, resorts restaurants and attractions that pay to be able to reply to travelers' reviews.  The traveler is not TripAdvisor's customer.  They are the people that enable the company to sell "memberships" to the resorts and hotels.  I have posted a few negative reviews and some have not been published and others were reviewed for over a week and then finally published in chronological order so they were a page or two down so most people would not see it.  If the business is not a member, all reviews are posted and the business cannot respond. Another problem is most reviews are overrated.  Even I will give a 4 to a resort that I think may be a 3-4.  Most reviewers have little experience and may have a great time at a place they visited only once and give it a high rating but, when compared to other resorts in the same area, it may really be only average.  If you look at the ratings, they are highly skewed to 4 and 5

review_title: I get emails about low airline prices …
review_text: I get emails about low airline prices and when I go to check them out they are no longer available. Most time I check them as soon as I get the email. It seems as though there may only be one or two tickets at that price and they are gone before the email goes out. Very misleading. I do like the opportunity to register my reviews of recent activities such as restaurants, hotel stays, cruises etc.

review_text: The Resort is Beautiful the rooms are clean and pretty, the food was very good, this resort has great potential, Pools good no complaints, staff for the most part excellent English is difficult, not many speak it or understand, wait staff very good, front desk staff not all that friendly maybe it's not their fault a lot of complaining about the room cards not working, lack of hot water in the showers and Tv's not working So the hotel needs to correct these problem but over all Loved it for now a 3 star so I hope they get it together they could be 5+

review_title: Hilton Inverness hotel in Denver
review_text: Hilton Inverness hotel in Denver.   Checked in at 2:30pm, room was a little cooler than we wanted.  Turned up the thermostat, but only cool air came out.  Called  the front desk and they sent a maintenance guy. He climbed up the access and "turned off the cold water"  Still no heat. Guy came back and said he could bring a space heater.  Denver forecast was for low 30's. Heater was noisy all night, could not regulate it.   Should have changed rooms.

review_text: The Oaks Highcliffe Dorset - Raymond Blanc Brasserie.  Have had lovely food on many occasions here but the last couple of meals have not been up to the usual standard.  Last week I had to send back my calamari as it was the toughest I have ever eaten.  The duck my husband chose was over cooked and dry - bear in mind he has had this on a few occasions at the Oaks.  Three weeks before the pork belly was very fatty.  This is usually my favourite.  A friend who ate here the week before and also loves pork belly had warned me it was very fatty and not the usual succulent dish we have had in the past. We read, and were informed the bar closed at 11.00pm, unfortunately, nobody informed us the bar was closing before the end of permitted hours. Which was disappointing. As I wanted to 'try' the beer and bar. Its location is OK, but on visiting Burnham, it's nice to be near the river Crouch.The rooms are superb, well equipped,  Lovely towels & toiletries. BUT the owner has omitted to paint the copper pipes in the Bedroom & Bathroom. Making it look like a ships engine room. The carpark is small as 5 chalets have been built in it to accommodate extra guests, making a total of 10 rooms.  But, there is a Free council carpark 150 yards away in Riverside Road. review_title: TripAdvisor takes a major step backwards
review_text: TripAdvisor used to be a terrific way to evaluate places, restaurants and things to do...alas, it is no longer as good as it once was.  While I understand the need for companies to earn revenue, this 'need' for monetization has impaired the usefulness of TripAdvisor.  At one time, when researching 'things to do', the results were presented by traveler rating, providing a fairly unbiased ranking of the options. Today they are listed and ranked firstly by all of the options that can be booked through TripAdvisor and Viator.  You've monetized the ranking process, putting your corporate revenue goals ahead of providing unbiased traveler rankings.  Your Viator options appear ahead of all other options, pushing other options out of the picture.  As a result, I now canvass other sources to help me learn about and experience destinations, and I consciously avoid booking through TA.  I've also dramatically cut back on the number of TA reviews I post, which is a shame since I am a very frequent international traveler. It's also a shame, because what was a wonderful, unbiased resource has morphed into a process where users are funneled into Viator for revenue purposes.

If there were a devoted section stating "your reviews" in it's own category, it would be quicker to find them.  Not going back to what we reviewed, but have it all listed together instead of separately.

review_title: Overall it’s a great place to get…
review_text: Overall it’s a great place to get honest reviews. However as someone who is a consistent reviewer for years, it’s a bit of a mixed bag: while you appreciate providing candid reviews for the traveler community, there is no incentive to do so. Trip advisor needs to be better about providing reviewers some kind of reason to keep on reviewing. Some sort of points system that could lead to benefits while traveling or discounts. Something!

review_title: Not As Good As It Used To Be
review_text: The current version of TripAdvisor is not as user friendly as earlier versions.  My most frequent reason to use TripAdvisor is to search things to do in a particular location.  Now the information is scattered.  There are too many ads and sometimes I feel your whole focus has become selling hotels, tickets, travel, etc.  In the past year I have used TripAdvisor less and other sites more for those reasons.

review_title: TripAdvisor started as a simple review company but where are the rewards for reviewers?
review_text: TripAdvisor started as a simple review company. Most people thought that there was some benefit to continue to contribute. We got all these awards and things but they can't be used to help defray costs, improve status anywhere, etc. You are asking us to simply help others. That's fine but you are making money from our reviews. You are owned by Expedia and Viator is another company that you have. Now, when I make a review, I'm asked to book a hotel or something through you. I'm not sure what your value proposition is anymore for someone like me. Can you tell me what it is? Why should I put all my reviews in your bucket so that you make more money and never give me anything?

review_title: While it is helpful to read what real…
review_text: While it is helpful to read what real people might think of a place, or experience, I think there are some faults with these and other reviews.  Part of the problem rests with the reviewers.  If there are too many positives, are they planted.  If there's one really lousy review, is it someone who simply wants to hear him or herself talk, makes them sound like a big shot, without the decency to take up the perceived problem face to face.  I know there's not much that can be done about either of these, and one hopes people actually take the time to read the reviews, and take them for what they are.  One flaw I think could be addressed is the length of time reviews stay on line.  For instance, a problem with an accommodation, or a product, that occurred 3 years ago, has probably been remedied.  I always take the dates of bad reviews into account, but how many people just don't bother?  My suggestion is take down reviews after two years.  Why should a business suffer from something that happened long ago, and that most likely has been resolved.

review_title: Basically accurate reviews

review_title: Watch their billing!  They quote AUD but bill in a foreign currency
review_text: No issue with the booking as such, however watch their billing!!! Just investigated an unusual entry on my credit card.  Outstanding 'Trip Advisor' balance was $A1188, however I was charged a total of ~$1260, which included $37 in 'foreign exchange fees' by my bank.  The entries on my card imply the charge was in Sterling!   There was no indication on the reminder email or booking confirmation that the charges would be in anything other than AUD. I Live in AUD, booked an AUD holiday via AUD site and was quoted in AUD, so would expect to be billed in AUD! Absolute rubbish!  Will be advising caution to anyone booking via TA in future.

review_title: Hard to select desired restaurant at…
review_text: Hard to select desired restaurant at selected city.  Restaurant and hotel ratings are too generous, more generous than Yelp, so it's hard to choose between so many 4-tar restaurants.

review_title: Not User Friendly
review_text: I love TripAdvisor but don't use it as much as I used to because it is now nearly impossible to find answers to your questions let alone trying to contact TA. And now it's impossible to write and save a draft which is something I did all the time. While I'm traveling I always wrote a draft to the places I've been to which was also my reminder to write the review as it usually was several per day but cannot do this anymore due to changes TA made therefore I don't write nearly as many as I used to. Otherwise I would give it 5 stars just not easy to use anymore.

review_title: Points for Improvement
review_text: There are a few things that would make my experience with Trip Advisor better - 1) Sequence of Photos - the latest photos should be shown first.  Most of the time, I will see a 2019/2018 photo and then the next one will be years old - like 2012.  The sequence jumps all over the place.  The photo sequence is very important when looking at a hotel for example. 2) Likes/Helpful Review - there is an ability to flag a review as Helpful.  There should be a sort order for Most Helpful Reviews.  More often than not, the review is not helpful.  You should also be able to vote on the review as not helpful. 3) New Look - recently, I've noticed a new look and feel for reviews whereby important information shown before is not shown anymore - such as how many reviews this person has done and where the person lives.  When I see a negative review and the reviewer only has done 1 review, I do not give it any merit because this person does not have any credibility.  We should have a way to quickly see how many reviews this person has done without clicking on the user who wrote the review.  Also, where this person comes from is important as well.

review_title: I trusted TA for almost a decade, not anymore
review_text: I trusted TA for almost a decade, only to find out that I have several of my reviews missing! I wasn't checking after posting, my fault. After a dozen attempts, now TA won't even bother to reply to me. So I contacted the resort itself and asked them to contact TA. I contacted content integrity dept at TA, no help there. I posted it in customer feedback section, no help there! For the record, I NEVER EVER ONCE HAVE RECEIVED A CONFIRMATION EMAIL WHERE I HAD TO CLICK TO CONFIRM IT'S MY REVIEW!!  I talked with friends who are level 9 contributors and even they said the same.  TA, ENOUGH EXCUSES, COME OUT CLEAN.  UPDATE: How do I respond to TA without revealing my email address to all who come here? UPDATE 2: My username on TA is rkramadh

review_title: A journey through history
review_text: Over a century ago, when Sri Lanka was Ceylon, elephants trekked a 72-mile journey from Colombo, the capital's port to Nuwara Eliya, the hill country town with the highest elevation where quality tea gardens, a luscious green carpet over hilly terrain, flourish. What they carried - snooker tables manufactured in thje UK - for The Grand Hotel, once the colonial residence of Ceylon's Lieutenant Governor Sir Edward Barnes.  He was one of the Adjutants serving the Duke of Wellington during the Battle of Waterloo. The snooker tables first arrived from London in India and were shipped to Colombo. They are fitted with the patent "Burwat Steel Vacumm cushions by Burroughs and Watts." The cues of that era and snooker balls made of ivory are still there. So are the market boards and building that house the paraphenelia. After 66 years as a colonial residence, it has remained The Grand Hotel which is deeply steeped in history. "We are committee to the twin task of preserving the heritage and the hotel," sayd its Deputy Chairman, Gerard Ondaatjiue. He is hands on visiting this jewel in his hotel chairn. His mission, he says, is to preserve and protect the hotel and its history, to upgrade it and operate with modern conveniences." There are 144 rooms. Some in the middle are small whilst those at the outside are rather spacious. The old fireplace still remain though they do not function. Standing along side are room heaters enough to produce a warm atmosphere. "Our guests are our loyalty," says Refhan Razeen, a veteran in the trade. He says "our personalised service combined with immense opulence make our guests very happy." together withy my wife, we spent three nights. Chef Priyantha is an expert have counted over two decades at this hotel. He was adept at turning out many a delectable cuisine be it from Vietnam, the Middle East or Thailand.

review_title: Our stay in Lowestoft Suffolk.
review_text: My son, and I, drove up to Lowestoft on Tuesday the 21st of July. I had business to do there and I took my Son along for the trip. Because of it being a long day, what with the drive from Dorset and completing my business, I decided that it would be best to stay in an Hotel for the night. We stayed in the Best western Hotel Hatfield. we, actually, stayed at The lodge, which is across the road from the main Hotel. This was because we wanted a Twin room and there are none in the main Hotel. Well, I have stayed there before, in the main Hotel, but never in The Lodge, so i didn't know what to expect.But WHAT a pleasant surprise. The Room, with the two single Bed's in, was very spacious and the Bed's were very comfortable. And the Room was very clean and tidy. The bathroom was also very clean, and tidy, and the Shower was just right. after such a long journey we both had showers and dressed for our evening Meal, which was across at the main Hotel Restaurant. That's when it went a bit wrong, I'm afraid.We both had starters, a Prawn Cocktail each ,which were generous portions and VERY nice. For our main course: my Son ordered Hunters Chicken and I ordered Battered Cod. Mine was delicious, and a generous size, about the best Fish that I have had for a very long time I MUST say. And I thoroughly enjoyed my meal. But my son couldn't eat his he was put off by how it was piled up and he didnt like the taste of it. So, he told the Waitress and She knocked it off the bill and provided Him with a drink courtesy of the Hotel and expressed Her apologies to my Son for the meal not being up to the standard that he expected. That was the ONLY blot on our stay at The Best Western Hotel Hatfield. Because everything else was superb. The Hotel has a nice Bar and ,next morning, when we had Breakfast, we were served in a very friendly manner and the Breakfast was lovely. This was the first time, since Lockdown, that I have travelled anywhere, let alone to stay in an Hotel and dine in their Restaurant, but it was, generally, a very nice experience and I cant wait to go somewhere else soon.

review_text: I looked into getting a puppy from MandMAussiesofNorthCarolina previously named MandMAussiesofMississippi. Dr. Mary Holly Castro owns MandMAussiesofNorthCarolina, now in Florida. After looking for a second Aussie puppy, I saw their GoFundMe page they started for their dog, Nola. They have on instagram they bred Nola for multiple litters without doing any hip testing first--which is the bare minimum for any responsible breeding program. It turns out Nola didn't get checked until she was three and she was then diagnosed with Grade III Hip Dysplasia, the most severe form there is. This was done by a now licensed DVM! The OFA has charts posted on their website that says a female with Grade III Hip Dysplasia paired with a male with Good (Passing) OFA hips still produces 31.5% puppies with hip dysplasia, meaning a litter of 9 will have 3 puppies with hip dysplasia. That's IF they tested the male's hips. At AKC puppy prices, two or more litters that they had from her could have been used to replace Nola's hips multiple times over. So why wait six years and then ask complete strangers to pay for it on GoFundMe? To me, it's a massive red flag regarding the ethics of this program.

I have sent Meta a formal legal notice demanding restoration of my account and page within 14 days, along with a Preservation Notice for all logs. Despite dozens of reports from third parties and clear evidence of criminal activity, Meta has taken zero meaningful action for over two weeks. This is not a simple “policy violation”. It is a serious failure by Meta to protect users and businesses from phishing attacks and account takeovers. Small businesses like mine depend on this platform — and Meta is simply not safeguarding us. I urge Meta to restore my account and page immediately and to improve their security and recovery procedures. Until then, I cannot recommend Facebook or Instagram to any business owner. review_title: When I first got on Facebook
review_text: When I first got on Facebook, it was like a "find the button you really need" quest. The interface is like a buffet: everything seems to be beautifully laid out, but when you want to pick up a fork, they give you a spoon. First week: I made friends of everyone who smiled at me in 2008. Further - worse. The algorithm decided that I was crazy about memes about cats, conspiracy theories, and recipes for perfect pancakes. And now my feed is a strange mix of news from Through the Looking Glass, tips on "how to live a week on tea and bread" and a video about how someone makes furniture out of pallets. Oh, yes, advertising. Do you have a dog? Facebook knows this. Even if there is no dog, you will still be offered collars, beds and, as a final, instructions on How to get a pet in 10 minutes. But the most important thing is the comments. If you didn't participate in the debate under the post about global warming, where the neighbor from the 3rd entrance is arguing with a professor of climatology, have you ever lived? And yet I continue to sit there. Why? Because this is where I found old friends, created a couple of funny memes, and maybe got a little better understanding of how this crazy world works. Facebook is like marriage: sometimes you want to delete it, sometimes you even enjoy it, but more often you just put up with it.

Lastly, I appreciate the privacy settings and control Facebook gives its users. The platform allows for customizing privacy settings for posts, photos, and personal information. This attention to privacy and security makes me feel more confident and at ease when using Facebook. Overall, I highly recommend Facebook to anyone seeking a versatile and user-friendly social media platform. review_title: Volschenk Motors Restored My Faith in Car Dealers
review_text: I recently bought a 2014 Daihatsu Terios from Volschenk Motors, and I can honestly say they’ve restored my faith in car dealerships. After months of being misled and pressured by several other dealers (including some big-name ones like WeBuyCars), I was starting to believe that all car dealers were untrustworthy. Volschenk Motors proved me wrong. I first saw the Terios on Facebook Marketplace and decided to go and view it. The experience was refreshing from the very beginning. The dealer was polite, opened the car for me, explained that it had a full service history and pointed out a few features and then simply let me take my time inspecting it without hovering or trying to “sell” me the car. Unlike the other dealers who insisted their cars were in “amazing” condition (when they clearly weren’t), Volschenk Motors let the car speak for itself. Ironically, this Terios, the oldest car I had looked at out of six, was in far better shape than all the others I had seen. A special thanks goes to Jacolise, who helped me with the paperwork. She was friendly, professional, and never once tried to upsell unnecessary extras like pothole cover, tracking devices, or insurance add-ons. Instead, she took the time to explain everything clearly and even warned me about how some banks and sales reps might try to take advantage. She also explained why my installment rate came out higher (through no fault of Volschenk Motors, but because other dealers had already submitted finance applications without me even looked at the cars yet). That level of honesty and care is something I wish all dealerships had. In the end, I drove away not just with a car I love, but with real peace of mind knowing I was treated with integrity and respect. Volschenk Motors is proof that there are still car dealers who genuinely care about their customers. I highly recommend them to anyone looking for a trustworthy, hassle-free experience.

review_title: I am extremely dissatisfied with the attitude towards vulnerabilities and poor service
review_text: I am extremely dissatisfied with both the Netflix product and their customer service, especially their refund policy. There is no free trial or any proper way to check whether the movies, shows, or series you want are actually available before subscribing. I subscribed specifically to watch Korean dramas, only to immediately discover that many of them do not even offer English voice-over — only subtitles. This is highly inconvenient, especially for people with disabilities, visual difficulties, or other vulnerabilities who cannot comfortably read subtitles while watching. As well, on Google it shows like the movie is available with a link to Netflix , but it's actually not available to watch once subscribed. E.g."This is Us" series. After only two days of being subscribed (tried to watch 1 serie only), I contacted customer support to request cancellation and a refund. Despite explaining my situation and the accessibility issue, they refused to refund. I also requested escalation to a manager. The support agent confirmed that my case would be passed to another team, but after two weeks, nobody contacted me. Netflix simply takes customers’ money and shows very little concern about whether users are actually satisfied with the service. The large number of negative reviews here speaks for itself. This level of customer care is unacceptable for such a well-known streaming platform. Most trusted providers offer either a free trial or money-back guarantee. Based on this experience, I would never subscribe again. It is also disappointing to see how little consideration is given to users with special accessibility needs. Paid 12 euros for nothing.

review_text: GAY FOCUSED :  I have been a subscriber for several years and I am becoming increasingly frustrated with the direction of content on this platform. Almost every new series I start — regardless of genre — features gay relationships as central storylines involving main characters. I recently tried Boots, Heartbreak High, Elite, The Royals and even Outlander, and every single one follows the same pattern. I want to be clear — this is not about hatred toward anyone. This is about content that simply does not appeal to me personally as a viewer. I have to fast forward through significant portions of shows I would otherwise enjoy because the content makes me uncomfortable. That is not an enjoyable viewing experience. What I and many viewers I know actually want is straightforward storytelling about men and women — normal relationships that the majority of the population relates to and lives every day. These stories are becoming increasingly rare on this platform. The content feels agenda driven rather than audience driven. I pay a subscription fee to be entertained, not to have social messaging pushed at me repeatedly across every show I try to watch.

review_title: I am writing to formally express my…
review_text: I am writing to formally express my deep frustration and disappointment with Netflix, particularly regarding Netflix Original movies and series. The problem I am experiencing is not limited to a specific genre. In crime, horror, thriller, and science-fiction productions — genres where such content is often completely irrelevant — there is almost always an explicit sexual scene. Very frequently, these scenes involve homosexual intimacy, regardless of whether it adds any value to the story. I want to ask this clearly and honestly: what is the purpose of these scenes in such genres? Are they truly necessary for the narrative, or are they being inserted deliberately and repeatedly without regard for context, audience, or genre? I want to emphasize something very clearly: I am not a homophobic person. However, the constant and unavoidable exposure to explicit sexual content has begun to seriously disturb me. At this point, this no longer feels like representation or inclusion — it feels like forced exposure. If respect is expected toward homosexual individuals, then respect must also be shown toward heterosexual viewers. It is completely normal for heterosexual people to feel uncomfortable when confronted with explicit homosexual scenes, simply because there is a difference in sexual orientation. Acknowledging this discomfort is not hatred; it is a natural human reaction and a matter of personal boundaries. Beyond sexual orientation, there is a broader issue. Many of these productions include long, explicit sexual scenes that feel excessive, unnecessary, and entirely out of place. In horror or crime series, these scenes often resemble pornographic content rather than storytelling. If I wanted to watch pornography, I would do so intentionally and at a different time. That is not what I expect when I choose a suspenseful, dark, or atmospheric series. Mixing near-pornographic scenes into unrelated genres shows a lack of logic and basic common sense. These scenes do not enrich the story. On the contrary, they destroy the tension, atmosphere, and overall quality of what could otherwise be strong and engaging productions. The beauty of the film or series is completely ruined. As a viewer, I now feel cornered. I cannot safely watch Netflix content with my family, and I feel anxious even watching alone because I am constantly expecting sudden and inappropriate scenes. This has reached a point where I am genuinely asking: If I avoid these scenes, what exactly am I supposed to watch on Netflix anymore? Respect should work both ways. Viewers should not be pressured, disturbed, or made uncomfortable while simply trying to enjoy entertainment. The lack of clear separation, proper categorization, or meaningful filtering options shows a disregard for viewer boundaries and preferences. If this approach continues in future Netflix Original productions and no serious changes are made, I will cancel my subscription out of exhaustion and ongoing discomfort and choose a different streaming platform instead. I respectfully request that Netflix reconsider this content strategy, apply common sense to genre boundaries, and provide viewers with real control over what they are exposed to. Thank you for taking the time to read this feedback.

review_text: I watched Adolescence. As a Social Worker, Psychologist & Psychotherapist of 40 years, I watch such programmes with a critical eye and generally such programmes disappoint as the writers have been lazy in their understanding of psychological issues and police procedures.  This programme's writer had done their homework except for a small error in that an AA, whoever they are, cannot sit in on Solicitor's sessions with their clients, not since the Fred West case as an AA can now be called to give evidence so what is said to the Solicitor in the presence of an AA is no longer confidential.  Also while the psychologist was played well (I am also an expert witness and train therapists, etc) therapists and psychologists are generally trained not to ask questions using the word 'Why' ! Your psychologist used this far too much instead of how, what, etc questions.  'Why' is a blocking question, so would not easily elicit an answer.  Good interviewers on TV rarely use this word.  Unfortunately, the otherwise very good writer had missed these points.  But the programme otherwise did address an important issue that is going under the radar for adults i.e. the problems of cyberbullying amongst young people that are not seen by schools or the parents and other adults around the children and can cause considerable mental health issues among school children.

review_text: I placed an order with Chewy for my dog and turkeys, excited about the 35% off first Autoship discount shown at checkout. But this bait-and-switch was a scam—they delayed shipping for days, made me verify my identity twice, then demanded I cancel and reorder at full price. When I cited their own Autoship Terms (“Chewy will not change the price of your next shipment once you have authorized an order”), they canceled my entire order anyway and refused the discount, hiding behind a "one account per household" rule their Terms do not state. Their Terms only say "you may register for an Account"—nothing bans multiple accounts, and no household restriction appeared where they advertised the discount. Even when I went back to reorder the same products, the 35% discount was still showing in my cart—proving it's their system glitch, not me. Instead of owning it, honoring the discount, and fixing their broken promotions like a reputable company, they put the burden entirely on me. They cherry-picked vague fine print while still enrolling me for future Autoship charges—even though the initial order for my pets never arrived. Their Customer Care Manager promised "I'm here to help guide you through next steps or answer any remaining questions," but after my detailed follow-up email, they went radio silent. Chewy pretends to care about pets and "award-winning customer service," but this proves they only care about money—treating customers like criminals while protecting their profits. Don't be fooled by their empty "So sorry, we care" scripted BS. Across chat support to management, they pretend to feel your pain and "take your feedback," but they honestly don't care and won't actually help you. It doesn't seem like smart business to trade years of loyal customer profits for a $20 discount—a strange hill to die on for a company. review_title: Beware Autoship
review_text: I had previously used Chewy for authorship but recently even though I had skipped several orders they still sent them all anyway.  I had to stop using them because they just send what they want not what you want.  That’s Bad.

review_title: Can''t order anything breakable…
review_text: Ordered (3) 32oz bottles of Wipe Out I cleaner and a reptile light bulb from Chewy.com.  Package arrived utterly destroyed.  No packaging materials used.  Just the bulb and three bottles tossed in a box.  Nothing survived.  We refused the package.  Chewy sent an apology stating that it was "not the Chewy  norm" and that they would reship.  To their credit, they did reship.  Bulb came separately this time in better packaging.  The three bottles of disinfectant were destroyed in transit again and automatically turned around by the carrier.  Chewy again reshipped.  Same thing.  After the third failed attempt, they said they were out of stock of the item and credited my card.  Each of the three time I received an email stating it was not the Chewy norm.  Obviously, it IS their norm.  I have purchased other things from them in the past and have not had a problem.  This experience has been crazy.  I will not order anything liquid or fragile (bulbs, etc.) from them again.  They do not know how to package products for shipment.

review_title: Misleading promos often
review_text: Misleading promos often. Even their page will display a different amount before you checkout. Then the price changes. Whoever said they have good customer service is wrong. They are nice but don’t do anything do actually resolve anything.

review_title: Unprofessional Pharmacy
review_text: Very bad pharmacy experience.  I needed meds for my two dogs immediately as they had Coccidia parasite.  They should have told me they they do not do expedited shipment of less than 3 days, and no shipments on the weekend.  Had I known this, I would have gone elsewhere to get my prescription refilled.  It ended up taking 5 days to get my prescription refill, which meant I ran out of their medicine for over 2 days, and the Coccidia returned in full force and I had to go back to the emergency veterinarian, which is a very expensive process.  My sense was that they really did not care about me or my dogs.  I will not give them my business anymore and would not recommend them.

review_title: Customer Service for pharmacy prescription timely medications not reliable
review_text: Based on my horrible experience with Chewy for prescription, time sensitive medications for my dog, I would NOT recommend them for any immediate need medications.  Please note that I had to check in with their Live Chat at least twice a day to push the order along.  My prescription order was sent to them on Friday.  After contacting them on Saturday, they said they were waiting for approval from my vet.  I then called my vet to have them give approval to Chewy to proceed.  Later in Saturday, I reached out to Chewy again to check on the order and found out that they’ve not do expedited shipments on the weekend.  This makes no sense to me since they are a pharmacy and often times medications are needed ASAP, as was my case.  Today (Monday), I checked back in and they had not even filled the prescription.  I was then told that expedited shipping only happens in a case-by-case basis.  This also does not make sense as my dog needs the meds and I am willing to pay for the expedited shipping.  I summary, I do not feel that Chewy is a reliable source for medications needed ASAP, as they are not set up for it.  Given the amount of hand-holding I had to do, which actually went nowhere, I will take my business elsewhere.

review_title: Expect Shipping Delays--Fedex
review_text: I've been a Chewy customer for years.  I've always found the customer service to be great. They always are generous in resolving issues by shipping extra food and such.  Unfortunately, their delivery times have gone from prompt to whatever. Fedex is the problem. Constant delays.  Looks like reviews for other carriers are equally poor.  In the future I'll be shopping elsewhere.  This is a good reason to return to brick and mortar stores.

review_title: I am so disappointed about the shipping…

I need the hay right now for my Guinea pig. What happened to the speedy service?? They used to be known for. Also the prices have skyrocketed! 😞😞

review_title: I used to order a lot from Chewy but…
review_text: I used to order a lot from Chewy but got tired of the endless web marketing and account sign in games. review_title: Awful courier service usage
review_text: I unfortunately have to leave only a 2 star review. Only reason it's not a 1 star is because they have excellent customer service. review_title: Frustrating experience

review_title: They refuse to honor coupons
review_text: I buy Dr Esley cat litter which contains a dollar coupon in each bag. I sent the coupons back to chewy and they refuse to honor them.

review_title: Product availability and shipping delays..
review_text: Some prices at chewy are quite competitive.  The problem I have is being billed when an item isn't even in stock.  It was never clear how long it would be until an item would be delivered.  Sometimes it was very quick.  Sometimes I would have no idea for quite a few days. For every order chewy immediately billed my account.  In every case, every item was presented as if it was in stock and ready to ship out immediately.  Chewy apparently sometimes takes more than 24 hours to even address an order.  I won't be ordering from chewy again.  I find them unethical.

review_title: Customer service is rough

review_title: Chewy auto subscription is Unreliable
review_text: Back in April, I was waiting on the auto shipment of centraguard for my cat. Card is charged, then the day item is supposed to ship, I get a notification that the item is out of stock. Okay, fine. Things happen. Then in May, and again in June, the same thing happens. They wait all the way until the day of shipment to notify you that the item is out of stock. With a little bit of transparency, they could have avoided all the charges and refunds they had to issue. When your working with medicine, I don't think it's unfair for the customer to expect reliability and transparency. review_title: Auto ships come out on the wrong day …
review_text: I have been receiving Chewy's auto ship for years. I have multiple pets and spend between 1,000 and 1200 every month on my auto ships . I am sooo disappointed in them recently . review_title: The only reason I give chewy this…

review_title: Poor customer service

review_title: Bait and switch
review_text: Bait and switch.  Auto ship will cost you way more than competitors.  $140 for a box of pills can can be had for $100 at many other sellers.  Stay away.

review_title: Are they censoring reviews to sell products?
review_text: Have been ordering from Chewy for years.  Some issues recently--past year or so..  Shipping seems to be a  bit slower.  Not as generous about returns as in the early years.  Customer service reps polite, but not always helpful.  Lower prices at Walmart without having to spend 50.00 for free shipping.  But of course chewy has great selection and home delivery.  Most concerning is that they solicit reviews on every product, but do not publish those that express legitimate concerns and are written according to their submission guidelines.  After thorough research and after speaking with my home vet, I took the time to write a constructive review of a dog food brand which followed all Chewy guidelines for submission, but the review was never posted.  Who are they protecting?  Certainly not our dogs. There are numerous reviews about dented cans and other minor concerns.  Yet they did not publish  my review about a label that  reveals there might be issues with long term feeding due to extremely minimum fat content of the dog food. Chewy vet by chat very nonchalant also.  Did not seem knowledgeable about AAFCO feeding and labeling requirements.   Did not investigate thoroughly or indicate she would would contact manufacturer.  My home vet advised stopping the diet ASAP due to extremely low fat content. Chewy was unconcerned, seemed to be protecting manufacturer and Chewy itself.

review_title: Incompetent Representatives
review_text: Customer service has really gone downhill. I used to brag about how their customer service outdid any other pet food company, but l definitely won't any more. review_title: Bad delivery and service
review_text: Fed Ex sent early morning email saying delivery today.  I had to go to the grocery store early this morning in the pouring rain and was in the pet section and did not get food or litter knowing my order was coming today.  At 10 AM I track my order - Fed Ex shows UPDATE: delivery tomorrow.  The distribution location is 15 minutes from my house so it’s been sitting 15 minutes from me for two days now. I called chewy customer service letting them know I was upset about this and the only thing I was told is that if I wasn’t happy, I could return my order when it arrived - nothing else. I canceled all future shipments. FedEx is not reliable and I’m not impressed with chewy Customer Service at all.   I won’t use them again.  And this is not the first issue I have had with unreliability with chewy.

review_title: Chewy.com is not longer the good company they were.
review_text: 26Jan2024-I had been a $600.-700.00+ monthly auto ship Chewy.com customer since Summer 2018, almost 6 years. I chose Chewy because they did have a good reputation and carried the Orijen dog chow I could not obtain locally. Over past 2 years, this last year being the worst, their dependable, timely service decreased and now no longer exists. I may get one bag within 3-4 days another one or two bags a day or two or a week or longer later. The auto date you choose they move up by 2-4 days which can be an inconvenience. It’s been over 6 months since returning a product, there has been no money refunded to my credit card. They were contacted about the issue, no response, which is not unusual. Their auto ship membership prices had also increased, no longer representing a savings over other retailer’s store prices. After times speaking with the manager of our local PetSense found 4 months ago they began stocking Orijen and insure no less than the 5 large bags I need are on hand the first of every month. In addition I receive a $ off my purchase as reward every month and every 10th bag is free (a $120.00 savings). I’ve gone back to buying the Purina/Friskies and 9 Lives cat chows I need from Walmart. The only thing I order from Chewy now is 3 bags of Journey puppy chow, which may also stop, and if I need replacement parts for elevated pet beds or if they have a cost effective sale on reflective collars or pet clothing. My orders for this month were again spread out, received over 2 weeks with winter weather not being a factor. The convenience of delivery is not worth sacrificing the health and welfare of my rescue pets or the unnecessary addition expense of being forced to buy and feed what is not their established diet.

review_title: Company changing and not to the good.
review_text: Not long ago I would have given them a 5.  But there are 3 big problems with Chewy.  First has become false advertising.  They have constant ads for sale prices and for low prices if you buy with autoship.  These all disappear as soon as you click on the product or try to get the autoship price.  You will never find that discounted price that made you click on the link in the first place.  Recently I gave up and went elsewhere due to this false advertising.  Second: they ship FedEx; as noted in other reviews FedEx delivers by dropping the box in the middle of the street or similar.  The packaging has also become worse with items banging around loose in boxes.  Third: be aware that you cannot trust their onsite reviews because if you leave any negative comments about a product they will contact you directly and pressure you to change your review.  This definitely influences people to just not leave any negative comments.  This used to be my "go-to" source for pet supplies but the company has been changing and not in a positive way.  I am sorry to see it.

review_title: I am honestly over the edge with Chewy
review_text: I am honestly over the edge with Chewy. Every time I try to benefit from their "promotions" I receive an error at checkout. The details and expiration dates are not transparent and the rules seem to change on a whim. At checkout I've experienced my autoship items no longer on sale and the price is hiked way up. Or the promotion doesn't include autoship and an error pops up "not available for autoship." If I transfer everything from autoship into my cart an error pops up "too late- expired." It's just not worth it to me anymore. The whole experience has become a hassle, disappointing, frustrating and is not saving me time or money.

review_title: Customer service is.. interesting
review_text: The customer service is kind of useless. Which was a totally nonsensical suggestion that would likely leave me with two dog carriers sitting on the porch for the three weeks I'll be out of town.

review_title: Chewy does not come through for us on…

They used to be great on this bit no longer.  I'll have to start buying food in store or from a more prompt provider.   Kim McKellar

review_title: Discount Coupon, April Fool!
review_text: Order from them from time to time. Got a coupon in the mail offering $20 off on a purchase of $49 or more. Loaded up $60 worth of items in the cart and tried to apply the coupon. Get a message that the coupon is invalid with possible reasons as expired or entered incorrectly. Neither of which applied here. The coupon does mention excluded items but there were no messages to that effect in the error detail and no link to explicitly state what the exclusions were. Called customer service and it quickly went from information to negotiation. Couldn't tell me why the coupon didn't work. But offered to take $10 off instead of $20 and forward it to some nebulous customer service team who *might* apply an additional discount. Don't think so. It either costs a particular amount or not. What am I going to do if they don't give the additional discount? Pay shipping to send it back? He said I could email customer service. They quickly replied that I should call the customer service phone line. Okay, so how many times am I going to go one place and have them tell me to go back to the original place that sent me. Answer: once, that's it. If you're going to offer discounts then it ought to be upfront on what is included and what is not. And provide the representatives with the ability to either match the discount or tell you immediately that they can't. Not try to negotiate a lesser discount. Oh and when I emailed customer service I told them that I had been on the phone and been directed to them. So in addition to that, they need to actually read the entire message you sent them. Don't say I won't order from Chewy again, but from now on the discounts are going in the trash and I'm only going to order if it's something I can't find locally.

review_title: Chewy will not accept any negative…

review_title: Terrible product quality
review_text: They have some products in stock that other pet stores don't and sometimes they have decent promotions but the quality leaves a lot to be desired. Some of their staff will tell you that you do not need to return, and then another staff tells you that you have to return. I have had to speak to management when one of their staff wrongly informed me to throw away the rotten cans, but then  3 other staff told me I have to ship it back way after it was already out of my house and in a garbage truck. Absolutely god awful customer service. If you can buy from literally  anywhere else, do so. Only buy here if there's some crazy sale and cross your fingers the food doesn't arrive in poor condition.

review_title: Although I have not had a big problem…

I have been waiting a week for an answer.   I did get an email response but it was not even to.the question I asked.   I am still waiting and have sent follow up emails.  In another day or 2 I will go to another company because if the service isn't there when there's an issue to me it's just not worth it.

review_title: FEDEX IS RUINING THIS COMPANY!!
review_text: I love this company and their customer service has always been great.  However, the FedEx service has now made the Chewy experience ridiculous. They have put my deliveries behind my car in the driveway so I can run over them when I don't see them. They have left them on the sidewalk out in the rain and snow. I have a full size porch with plenty of room for dry deliveries and they have left them on the edge of the steps instead of pushing them in another 2 feet to avoid the rain. This has been done when it's been raining all day so it's not because the rain was a surprise event. But this past month took the cake. I did not know I had a delivery coming that day so I was watering my front garden and the sprinkler also reached my front porch. The FedEx delivery driver actually walked through the sprinkler to put the box on the front porch right where I was watering!! The box was drenched. WHY would any delivery driver do that?!! I've received Amazon deliveries when my sprinkler was running and they've left it right off the porch so it didn't get wet. This was a prescription food which was VERY expensive. Yes, Chewy replaced it but that's not the point!! The point is Chewy is allowing FedEx to have no respect for any of the deliveries and is not ensuring that their deliveries arrive intact. I mean, if it's a prescription food, I need to have it when I need to have it because feeding something else would be detrimental.  I have called and complained multiple times and although they are willing to send a new shipment, there is no change in my deliveries! In addition, I've been told that this is a frequent complaint with deliveries now so it's not like my particular delivery driver just does this. I love Chewy and I've used them for years but I've had to stop the autoships on any foods that are prescription and HAVE to be had when I order them and not when they send another order. Shame on them for not handling the problems with their delivery service. I'm so disappointed in them.

review_title: My second order delayed by FedEx ... Again
review_text: My second order delayed by FedEx. No reason given just another company going downhill. UPS turned their company around, wish FedEx would get their act together. No more Chewy orders until they use any another reliable shipping company.

review_title: Worst customer service ever!
review_text: I'm only giving this 2 stars because the last lady that I talked to was very nice. Shanice I think was her name. I went on Chewy with a visa gift card to order over $200 worth of stuff for my dog and cats. I had a birthday coupon that was sent in the mail because my cat's birthdays are 08/25. I scanned the code inside the card and was brought to a page of birthday treats/toys/clothes. I chose the birthday temptations treats and tried to apply the code, but it said invalid. When I reached out to customer service via chat, the first rep told me that I could not use that code on said birthday treats, but could use them on normal temptations treats. Okay. Whatever. I chose something else for them (a birthday cupcake with catnip) and got 80 cents off. Yippee! Then I added 40 lbs of dog food, 22 lbs of cat food, 12 cans of wet dog food, 12 things of wet cat food, the temptations birthday treats that I originally wanted, a dog bone, and dog treats in addition to their birthday cupcakes. I chose autoship for the dog and cat food because we've been buying it from Target so I figured why not. Then I enter the gift card, click submit, think everything is finished. I get an email that says I double used a promotion code and I needed to call Chewy. So I call the number. The lady tells me it's not the promo code that it's the gift card. She verifies the information with me then pushes the charge through. About 10 minutes later, I get another email stating that there's something wrong with my auto shipment. Now, mind you, I have 2 other cards on file with Chewy. Both of them have my name on them and I had to call when I used them both times to verify that it was indeed me trying to place the order. Security is nice and all, but common sense is too. If the card information matches my account information... I probably shouldn't have to call to verify it every time I place an order. Anyway, back to the present. I open the chat again and talk to Ivan P about the situation. He takes literally forever. I was in the chat with him with no resolution for almost an hour. The first order of dry food was cancelled by them days afterwards because they didn't have the product and couldn't ship it to me. No call, just a computer generated email with no real explanation. Several months later I ordered the wet version of the same food. Chewy said that they  tried to contact my vet on a Friday to authorize prescribed food. I checked with my vet on Monday, and they confirmed that they never received a call or request from Chewy. So, then I scrambled to send Chewy a picture of the prescription. 24 hours later, no confirmation email or call. So, I contacted Chewy again, they said that yes they received the document, but it would take 1-3 days to deliver. I requested an expedited delivery option. They said none was available, but I could call Fed Ex and request a hold on delivery. At this point I'm thinking " What exactly does customer service do that an AI wouldn't do better?". I explained that, due to the delay, I was not going to be available to receive the product if it took three days. They then told me I should cancel and reorder when I would be available. I asked how this would effect my discount code that I used. They then said, I should call instead of placing my new order online. It felt like every single problem was mine to solve. At this point, it's just easier to drive the 30 minutes to Petco to get what I need. Two stars instead of just one because they managed to get one, none prescription, order right of some Pro-Pectalin.

review_title: Is there a reliability issue with chewy.com?
review_text: My cats veterinarian put him on Barrier flea control as it protects against many other things and it's a topical that lasts a month. I found Barrier online via chewy com ,a 6 months supply, so my boyfriend ordered it ,then was informed the veterinarians approval was required. Chewy called the vet but since my boyfriend wasn't listed on my cats records it was not approved. Chewy contacted the vet once again and the vet figured out that it was my boyfriend who paid for my cats vet visit and that he is in fact affiliated therefore the vet approved the prescription. Chewy accepted payment from the start,while the approval was given to chewy by the vet we still haven't received notice as to what is going on with this prescription that has been paid for since the 14th of July 2023. My cat has been uncomfortable with irritations such as fleas,mites,etc.and he is due for the next dose but chewy.com has dropped the ball by not contacting us regarding shipping the prescription that was indeed approved also paid for in full. I am beginning to second guess chewys reliability where my cats health and well being is concerned. The order was placed, the vet did approve the prescription, we should have received some response regarding the shipping such as a tracking number , at least confirmation that the order had been processed and is being shipped, but nothing. I assumed that chewy.com was a reliable and trustworthy source, though now such disappointment due to no response especially since they took the payment. We also set up the auto ship implying to chewy that we will be continuing purchasing this item in the future regularly. In my opinion, payment should only be accepted upon approval rather than taking ones payment then leaving them hanging just to wonder what's going on with the order or more importantly their funds. I'm going to contact chewy by phone in just a bit, we will see, I may be revising my review, but at this moment I'm not very happy with the situation and neither is my cat. Going to the vet is very costly and if I have to return to the vet because my cat  contracted something due to his meds not being delivered it will be undoubtedly unacceptable. It's been over a week and that is simply too long to have been waiting . I expected a reply upon approval along with an ETA on the meds .

review_title: Is this company for real???
review_text: UPDATE: So the gift certificate didn't arrive as promised on Christmas day. I called today 12/26/22 to inquire as to it's whereabouts and was greeted by a nice gentleman who told me there seemed to be a payment hold on PayPal's end. So, I checked with PayPal and learned that authorization had indeed been granted on the date I ordered the card and they (PayPal) were waiting for Chewy to process it so payment could be rendered. The gentleman told me to hold and he would get a supervisor on the line to straighten things out. After 5 minutes or so of listening to repeated ads, the line went dead. As Chewy had my phone number, I expected and waited for a return call. Guess what? It never happened! Several hours later I received another email stating that I again needed to call Chewy to verify my order!!! You can't make this stuff up! This company is a total joke!!! Called once again and spoke with a representative who wanted to transfer me to a supervisor. Thankfully this time, I was connected with someone, and after once again verifying my information, I was assured that the gift card would be received sometime today. I have since received an email from Chewy saying that the eCard has been sent but I haven't yet been able to verify this with my daughter. My advice still stands, stay away from this company. There are enough horror stories to warrant seeking an alternative, and there are plenty of them. My Story: Created account to send my daughter an emailed gift card as a Christmas gift, that is to be sent to her on Christmas Day, as a surprise (Hopefully it gets to her!). Payment was made via Paypal and processed immediately according to my bank, yet I received an email from the company stating I needed to call about my order. Called this morning and spoke with a young lady who was very matter of fact, not warm or friendly (in my opinion) yet professional, right up until the point she hung up on me, apparently because she didn't want to hear my rant any longer. I was not rude, I didn't use foul language and even apologized for taking my frustration out on her for needing to take valuable time out of my work schedule to "process" an order that apparently had already been processed (again, according to my bank). Of course, she didn't hear that apology because she had already, unbeknownst to me, hung up! There is absolutely no reason that I should have to create an account, provide personal information (name, email address, etc.) so that I can be added to an email list that they may then sell to other companies, so I can be inundated with spam, all to provide an emailed gift card to my daughter who for some reason has chosen to utilize their services. The amount of the card was not huge and should not have been viewed as a fraud risk since the payment was PayPal verified. I should have been able to accomplish this simply as a guest, as many, many other internet-based companies do. My experience with the company, to say the least, has been unfortunate. And I encourage folks to research other services of this type rather than give Chewy the benefit of your business.

review_title: Happy with Chewy
review_text: I have 18 feline fur babies and for that reason I've been a Chewy customer for a LONG time. Since the pandemic and the supply chain issues my local pet stores simply did not have the stock of food etc. for all of my "kids" but I could always count on Chewy to have the items that we needed. That being said I give them 5 stars for availability. So far my autoship items have arrived on time with no issues, 5 stars for that. The prescription area however is not good at all. There is no way for me to delete outdated prescriptions for the vet food we get..even the ones for fur babies that have passed away many years ago. Yes, I called customer service MANY times regarding this and yes the problem persists. Zero stars for that. I do not order any of their meds from the Chewy pharmacy. They are too important and I cannot take the chance on a screw up. I prefer instead to get the meds from our local compounding pharmacy because I can have human interaction directly, to resolve any issues. As far a shipping goes maybe a few times shipping was delayed but I always order well in advance to counter that problem. And quite frankly, anything I order online with other retailers is delayed by a few days. I have received damaged items due to poor packing. Chewy has always handled that properly and sent me replacements. 5 stars for that. So, the prices for food etc. has gone up dramatically, everywhere. I check the Chewy website frequently for specials as well as other pet stores for the best deals. Yes, sometimes Chewy's prices are the same as other pet stores but again, I have to feed 18 feline fur babies, so quantity becomes the issue, not price. However, no matter what monies are spent, I expect, and have so far received, great service from Chewy. Hopefully that won't change. If it does, I suppose I'll be writing a review to reflect that. Finally, I like the variety of brands they offer, as well as options for amounts such as can sizes and quantity. I even get my wildbird food from Chewy and have been very happy with that.
